abstract: N-type SnSe thermoelectrics have long been constrained by the lack of effective strategies to simultaneously optimize electrical transport, suppress lattice thermal conductivity, and enhance mechanical robustness. Here, we present a dual-scale design framework combining microscopic electroacoustic decoupling with mesoscopic ordered reconstruction to overcome these limitations. Through the incorporation of WCl₆, electroacoustic decoupling is achieved, as confirmed by AC-STEM. Partial substitution of Sn and Se with W and Cl enhances carrier concentration, induces conduction band passivation and convergence, and significantly improves electrical transport. Simultaneously, the formation of low-dimensional defects and mesoscopic ordering reduces lattice thermal conductivity by disrupting phonon transport and aligning grain orientations. These synergistic mechanisms yield a remarkable thermoelectric figure of merit, ZT ≈ 1.9 at 823 K, alongside a substantial improvement in mechanical hardness from 0.87 GPa to 1.5 GPa. This dual-scale approach not only establishes a novel pathway for advancing n-type SnSe thermoelectrics but also provides a generalizable strategy for designing high-performance thermoelectric materials with improved mechanical durability. These findings mark a significant advance in the pursuit of sustainable energy solutions and the development of robust, efficient thermoelectric systems.

title: Strengthening and deformation mechanisms of oxygen-modified nanocrystalline Cu
abstract: Despite the crucial role of oxygen in metallic materials, its effect on strengthening and deformation at the atomic scale remains poorly understood. We investigated the influence of oxygen on the microstructure and strengthening of commercial pure copper processed by high-pressure torsion. Advanced transmission electron microscopy (TEM) studies, combined with atomic-scale quantitative analysis and theoretical calculations using density functional theory (DFT), reveal that the introduction of oxygen intensifies lattice distortion and impacts crystal deformation behavior. Comprehensive research discovered that, contrary to our previous understanding, oxygen can actually suppress grain refinement before the microstructure reaches a steady state (or saturation). At this stage, oxygen exists in multiple forms, including oxides (CuO, Cu₂O), interstitial solutes, and oxygen-rich clusters. Furthermore, the synergy of strengthening mechanisms, including oxide dispersion, solid-solution strengthening, grain boundary pinning, and coherent interface strengthening, results in a significantly improved hardness compared to pure copper Cu nanocrystals. This study provides a new insight into the role of oxygen in nanocrystalline materials. It also demonstrates that oxygen incorporation during severe plastic deformation is an effective and cost-effective strategy for tailoring the microstructure and enhancing mechanical properties.

title: Liquid metal embrittlement in Fe-Zn: What can we learn from atomistic simulations?
abstract: Liquid metal embrittlement (LME) is a bottleneck for applications such as welding of galvanised steels in the automotive industry. The mechanistic origin of this phenomenon is not fully understood. In this work, we address some of the key LME hypotheses by developing and thoroughly validating a machine learning interatomic potential for the Fe-Zn binary system. The interatomic potential is suited for reproducing with good accuracy relevant benchmark properties, dislocation- and crack-related characteristics, as well as intermetallic phases of the Fe-Zn binary system. Based on the validated potential, we conduct a series of numerical fracture toughness tests (K-tests) on ( 110 ) [ 1 ¯ 10 ] single crystals and Σ 3 , as well as Σ 5 grain boundaries in Fe with varying Zn solute concentrations. The K-test results demonstrate the general applicability of the potential for studying complex fracture phenomena at the atomic scale. Furthermore, the conducted simulations suggest that for the prediction of LME, detailed analyses, including realistic Zn distributions, possible formation of intermetallic phases at the crack tip, and combination with microscale modelling, are required. We therefore discuss how machine learning interatomic potentials, like the presented, can be used in follow-up fracture studies to aid a more profound understanding of fracture and embrittlement phenomena in the Fe-Zn system.

title: Non-linear jog-dragging effect on the mobility law of edge dislocations in face-centered cubic nickel
abstract: Dislocation jogs have strong effects on dislocation motion that governs the strain-hardening behavior of crystalline solids, but how to properly account for their effect in mesoscale models remains poorly understood. We develop a mobility model for jogged edge dislocations in FCC nickel, based on systematic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations across a range of jog configurations, stresses, and temperatures. At low stresses, jogged edge dislocations exhibit non-linear, thermally activated dragging and a higher Peierls barrier compared to straight dislocations. Surprisingly, stress-velocity curves for a given jog configuration across varying temperatures intersect at an invariant point ($τ_{\rm c}$, $v_{\rm c}$), where $τ_{\rm c}$ delineates thermally-activated and phonon-drag regimes and is close to the Peierls stress ($τ_{\rm p}$). Motivated by this observation, we propose a simple three-section expression for jogged dislocation mobility, featuring minimal and physically interpretable parameters. This mobility law offers a realistic description of jog effects for dislocation dynamics (DD) simulations, improving their physical fidelity for crystal plasticity predictions.

title: Strain-induced dynamic evolution of the T1 phase and its influence on recrystallization behavior
abstract: This study combines advanced microscopy techniques and theoretical calculations to elucidate the dynamic evolution of the T1 phase, including dislocation slip transmission, thickening, and phase transformation, and their influence on dynamic recrystallization (DRX) in Al–Cu–Li alloys. The results revealed that dislocation shearing preferentially activated the pyramidal II slip system within the T1 phase because of its low energy barrier and high geometric compatibility. This shearing produced high-energy, unstable antiphase boundaries (APBs), which attracted solute segregation and served as preferential thickening sites. Moreover, dislocations accumulated at APBs supplied strain energy and created fast diffusion channels, thereby accelerating solute transport and promoting cooperative multilayer growth, which in turn facilitated rapid thickening of the T1 phase. Furthermore, these dislocation-mediated diffusion channels also facilitated the escape and redistribution of solute atoms, particularly Li, leading to local compositional fluctuations that drove the transformation of T1 into Ω′/Ω phases. The nanoscale evolution of T1 phases exerts a pronounced effect on DRX. The shear-induced thickening of T1 phases accelerated continuous DRX through two complementary effects: (i) promoting the depinning of dislocations, which facilitated substructure formation, and (ii) enhancing the pinning effect of subgrain boundary migration. Moreover, the thickening of the T1 phase broadened the precipitation-free zones, which in turn triggered a distinct necklace-type recrystallization nucleation. These findings establish a clear link between the nanoscale evolution of the T1 phase and the corresponding microscale microstructural transformations, offering theoretical guidance for the thermomechanical processing of Al–Cu–Li alloys.

title: Chemical complexity suppresses interstitial solute segregation to screw dislocation cores in the bcc NbTaTiHfZr high-entropy alloy
abstract: Recent reports suggest that interstitial solute additions to body-centered cubic (bcc) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) may enhance their mechanical properties. However, details of interactions between interstitial atoms and dislocations in these HEAs remain incompletely understood. Using first-principles calculations, we examine the energetics of C, N, and O interstitial solutes in elemental bcc metals and NbTaTiHfZr, focusing on their segregation in screw dislocation cores. We examine two types of core sites and show that the low-energy configuration and associated segregation energy depend on the transition metal group. In NbTaTiHfZr, we find that chemical complexity substantially suppresses interstitial segregation in dislocation cores, as fluctuations in bulk solute energies induce energetically favorable sites that disfavor segregation to core sites. Local chemical order further enhances this effect by promoting solute clustering away from dislocation cores. These findings reveal fundamental differences between the behavior of interstitial atoms in elemental metals and HEAs, with implications for high-temperature plasticity and dynamic strain aging.

title: Analytical model for island growth mode in thin film deposition
abstract: An analytical model for 3D island growth in Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) was derived from geometric and statistical principles. The model accounts for a random island distribution and spontaneous nucleation. A spherical dome shape of islands is assumed, at a specified contact angle with the substrate. The model can be extended to alternative island shapes or processes beyond ALD, including chemical- or physical vapor deposition. Owing to the analytical nature of the model, an influence of process parameters is transparent and evaluation is instantaneous. The model was validated with a Monte Carlo simulation. The latter illustrated the deposit morphology at distinct growth stages: an island nucleation, an onset of coalescence, a peak mass gain per cycle and a convergence to a continuous film. The model can fit any experimentally measured signals in- or ex-situ relating to mass uptake or surface roughness during the nucleation process. The model fit to literature data of deposited mass upon island growth of Pt on Al2O3 and ZnO2 crystals showcased the insights that the model gives, such as estimation of island nucleation density and spontaneous island nucleation rate. If the model diverges from experimental data, it hints at additional phenomena that might govern the process, on top of the island growth. The model serves as a valuable tool to guide process design and optimization, whether the goal is to obtain specific nanoparticle morphologies, as for fields of catalysis or optics, or thin continuous films, for areas of semiconductor and coating technologies.

title: Tailoring dielectric, piezoelectric and ferroelectric properties in aluminum scandium nitride through doping
abstract: We present a comprehensive first-principles investigation of dielectric, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties in wurtzite Al0.75Sc0.25N doped with over 90 elements. Using density functional theory, we screened 368 substitutional and interstitial configurations across nine charge states (3312 total calculations). A two-stage methodology-initial energetic screening followed by ensemble averaging over five independent special quasi-random structures-enabled statistically robust property predictions with quantified configurational uncertainties. DFT+U corrections were applied to transition metals to eliminate d-orbital hybridization artifacts. From this screening, 41 energetically favorable dopants emerged (35 cation-site, 6 anion-site), with 18 isovalent and 23 heterovalent cases requiring charge compensation. Density functional perturbation theory calculations reveal that 76% of dopants preserve the c-axis dielectric anisotropy essential for device integration. Rare-earth elements enhance permittivity by 5–20% while maintaining anisotropy. Piezoelectric optimization identifies Nb, Ti, Cr, and B as top performers, achieving 50–60% improvements in d33 and k332 through enhanced Born effective charges and elastic softening. Ferroelectric analysis shows no single dopant simultaneously increases spontaneous polarization and reduces coercive field; however, Nb, Zr, Cr, and Ti decrease coercive field by 4–7% while retaining ≥95% polarization-attractive for low-voltage switching. Concentration scaling from 3% to 6% reveals dramatic piezoelectric enhancement for transition metals (Zr: +226%, Cr: +174%) but concurrent polarization degradation in 38 of 41 dopants. We identify a tetrahedrality-mediated mechanism (R²=0.66) linking local structural distortion to this piezoelectric-ferroelectric trade-off which is a fundamental consequence of wurtzite coordination chemistry. These results establish quantitative structure-property relationships and practical design principles for rational doping of AlScN in next-generation radio frequency filters, micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS), and ferroelectric memory technologies.

title: Mechanistic insight into cooperative slip system activation under cyclic loading in a near-alpha titanium alloy
abstract: Fatigue crack initiation in polycrystalline metallic alloys is governed by cyclic irreversibility at the scale of individual slip bands, emphasizing the need to understand the mechanisms of slip system activation. In this study, a combination of electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and high-resolution digital image correlation (HR-DIC) enabled advanced slip trace analysis in a TIMETAL® 834 alloy subjected to cyclic four-point bending at stress levels up to 90% of the proof stress. This approach allowed simultaneous resolution of the slip direction, slip plane, and heterogeneous strain distribution for individual slip bands. Within the explored parameter space, basal < a> slip exhibited higher effective shear strain than prismatic < a> slip. Notably, basal slip traces were frequently formed by the concurrent activation of two distinct < a> type Burgers vectors, with their relative contributions varying significantly between different slip traces—and even along a single trace within a grain.Detailed analysis revealed that this variation is driven by a tendency to improve geometric alignment with neighbouring slip bands, particularly across boundaries in clusters of grains with similarly oriented and well-aligned basal planes, irrespective of grain boundary misorientation. For the first time, this phenomenon is demonstrated through precise evaluation of the geometric compatibility parameter (m′) for basal–basal slip interactions, incorporating measured slip directions rather than relying solely on Schmid factor-based assumptions. Additionally, localized strain accumulation during cycling was observed to saturate at the earliest stages of fatigue under low-stress conditions, indicating the potential for early prediction of fatigue crack initiation based on initial plastic slip activity.

title: Hydrogen diffusion in TiCr2Hx Laves phases: A combined ab initio and machine-learning-potential study
abstract: The kinetics of hydrogen diffusion in C15 cubic and C14 hexagonal TiCr 2 H x (0 < x ≤ 4) Laves-phase hydrogen storage alloys is investigated with density functional theory (DFT) and machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). Generalized solid-state nudged elastic band calculations are conducted based on DFT for all symmetrically inequivalent paths between the first-nearest-neighbor face-sharing interstitial sites. The hydrogen migration barriers are substantially higher for the paths that require breaking a Ti–H bond than for those that require breaking a Cr–H bond. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with the MLIPs also demonstrate that hydrogen migration occurs more frequently within the hexagonal rings made of the A 2 B 2 interstitial paths, each requiring the breaking of Cr–H bonds, than along the inter-ring paths. The diffusion coefficients of hydrogen obtained from the MD simulations reveal a non-monotonic dependence on hydrogen concentration, which is more pronounced at lower temperatures. Time-averaged radial distribution functions of hydrogen further show that hydrogen avoids face-sharing positions during diffusion and that the hydrogen occupancy at the second-nearest-neighbor edge-sharing positions increases with increasing hydrogen concentration. The diffusion coefficients of hydrogen within 400–1000 K follow an Arrhenius relationship, with activation barriers consistent with most experimental values. One-order of magnitude overestimation of diffusion coefficients compared with some experiments suggests a substantial impact of hydrogen trapping by defects such as Cr vacancies and Ti anti-sites in non-stoichiometric TiCr 2 in experiments.

title: Bonding relay for room-temperature oxide plasticity like metals
abstract: Oxides have long been regarded as intrinsically brittle due to their strong, directional ionic or covalent bonds, in stark contrast to the ductile behavior of metals, where delocalized electron sharing enables plasticity through facile dislocation glide. Here, we challenge this paradigm by demonstrating that typical oxides, such as SrTiO3 and MgO, can exhibit room-temperature plasticity with pronounced crystallographic anisotropy. Through an integrated approach combining ab initio calculations, large scale molecular dynamics simulations, and experimental nanoindentation, we identify a universal structural criterion enabling room-temperature oxide plasticity: the presence of alternating positively and negatively charged atomic layers along specific slip directions, specifically the (1-10)[110] orientation in perovskite and rocksalt oxides. This charge alternating configuration enables a bonding relay mechanism, in which sequential bond breaking and reformation across the slip plane accompanied by interlayer persistent bonds mimics multi centered interactions in metals, thereby facilitating dislocation motion without catastrophic failure. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized pathway to achieving metal-like plasticity in oxides and establish a structural design principle for engineering flexible and mechanically resilient oxide materials.

title: Editorial Board
Strength-ductility synergy in diamond-nanoparticle-dispersed nanotwinned Cu with defective twin boundaries
abstract: Nanotwinned (NT) metals are known for their high strength and ductility arising from dislocation-twin boundary (TB) interactions. However, when TBs contain defects such as incoherent segments, their mobility can trigger detwinning and softening, thereby reducing work hardening and fracture resistance. Here, we report a diamond-nanoparticle-dispersed columnar NT Cu fabricated by direct-current co-deposition, in which TBs incorporate a high density of incoherent segments and 9R phase defects. Compared with pure columnar NT Cu, the composite exhibits comparable strength and uniform elongation, while surprisingly achieving a markedly higher fracture elongation. Microstructural characterization reveals extensive dislocation accumulation, detwinning accompanied by dissociation of the pre-existing 9R phases, and the formation of twin shear bands during tensile deformation. Molecular dynamics simulations further demonstrate that embedded diamond nanoparticles promote dislocation nucleation and storage, enabling the alloy to achieve high flow stress at relatively larger plastic strains. After necking, severe twin fragmentation, ultrafine grain formation, and strain-induced coarsening via dynamic recrystallization are observed near the fracture surface. In situ fracture experiments reveal crack deflection mediated by twinning and faulting. These results demonstrate that the synergistic activation of multiple deformation mechanisms, promoted by the diamond nanoparticle dispersion and defective twin structures, underpins the enhanced strain hardening and ductility of NT Cu. This work provides a new pathway for tailoring strength-toughness combinations in NT metals.

title: Effect of Fe content on the coupling between lattice distortion and atomic shuffle of the R phase in Ti50Ni50-xFex alloys
abstract: The R phase in NiTi-based shape memory alloys is known to have two crystallographic changes from its B2 parent phase: a lattice distortion and an atomic shuffle. The lattice distortion induces a crystal shape change and is thus more responsive to mechanical influences. In contrast, the atomic shuffle has no mechanical effect and is more likely affected by alloy chemical composition. In an earlier study we investigated the decoupling of the two under mechanical constraints in nanocrystalline matrices. In this study we investigated the effect of alloy composition, more specifically Fe content, on the coupling between the two during B2 ↔ R transformation by means of thermal and electrical analyses, in-situ X-ray diffraction measurements and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. It was found that Fe substitution for Ni in equiatomic NiTi reduces the magnitudes of both lattice distortion and atomic shuffle, with the latter appearing to be more hindered. At 6 at.% Fe substitution, atomic shuffle is completely inhibited whereas the lattice distortion is reduced only by approximately 50%. This is consistent with DFT calculations, which reveal that the magnitude of atomic shuffle follows the order of Ni > Ti >Fe and that increasing Fe content decreases the magnitude of shuffle of all three elements. This is compounded by the additional mechanical constraint of the nanocrystalline grain size which leads to the complete suppression of the B2 ↔ R transformation in the Ni₄₄Ti₅₀Fe₆ alloy.

title: FePO4-guided redox reconstruction unlocks high-efficiency regeneration of spent LiFePO4 cathode materials
abstract: Lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4, LFP) batteries dominate electric vehicles and stationary energy storage owing to their safety, long lifespan, and low cost. However, the rapid retirement of LFP batteries presents growing environmental and resource challenges. In this work, an innovative FePO4-assisted hybrid precursor route is proposed for scalable regeneration of spent LFP materials. The process involves oxidative decomposition of spent LFP into Li3Fe2(PO4)3 and Fe2O3, followed by high-energy ball milling with FePO4 and Li2CO3 then undergoing carbothermal reduction to obtain regenerated LFP (R-LFP). Characterization results demonstrate that FePO4 effectively mitigates Fe3+ defects, reduces Li–Fe antisite disorder, and enhances Li+ diffusion. The regenerated R-LFP exhibits superior structural integrity, uniform carbon coating, and excellent electrochemical properties, achieving 164.6 mAh g⁻1 at 0.1C and 98.7% initial coulombic efficiency, maintaining 97% capacity after 500 cycles. Economic and life-cycle analyses reveal that the proposed route delivers higher profitability (1.159 $ kg⁻1) and lower environmental impact compared to traditional redox-based regeneration and virgin material synthesis. This study provides a cost-effective and industrially viable strategy for high-value recycling of discarded LFP batteries, contributing to the circular economy and carbon-neutral development of the battery industry.

title: Oxygen-ion displacement regulation for designing high-performance P2-type Na-based layered oxide cathode
abstract: The practical application of P2-type sodium cathodes is restricted by intrinsic Na+/vacancy ordering and unstable cathode-electrolyte interphases (CEI). While conventional inactive-element doping improves stability, it typically sacrifices specific capacity. Addressing these challenges, we demonstrate that trace Bi doping simultaneously boosts specific capacity, cycling life, and rate performance, effectively circumventing the classic capacity-stability trade-off. The concurrent improvement primarily originates from Bi-induced structural modulation, which we quantitatively characterize through a newly proposed oxygen-ion displacement rate (δO) descriptor. Through doping control, we successfully synthesized two P2-type materials with significantly distinct δO values (∼38.07 % vs. ∼31.58 %), demonstrating the critical role of δO in governing electrochemical performance. The material with ultra-low δO has suppressed Na+/vacancy ordering due to its weak Na-O correlations. Additionally, its strong TM-O correlations effectively inhibit TM (transition metals) dissolution, construct a stable CEI, and alleviate the lattice strain. Consequently, this material exhibits delivers a 23.1 % enhancement in specific capacity, exceptional cycling stability (72.9 % capacity retention after 1000 cycles), and remarkable rate performance by achieving a 51.1 % capacity within just 34 s. This work introduces a pioneering perspective based on oxygen-ion displacement for designing high-performance oxide cathode materials.

title: Incipient decomposition of nitrogen-expanded Austenite in Si-containing high-Ni alloys during nitriding
abstract: In contrast to the nitride formation in steels nitrided at 480–600°C, low-temperature nitriding (LTN) generates a precipitate-free, interstitially-supersaturated nitrogen-expanded Austenite (γ N ) case in Austenitic stainless steels (SSs). However, the temperature/time-dependent Cr-nitride precipitation in γ N triggers long-range Cr migration, severely deteriorating corrosion resistance. Hence, the upper LTN temperature is often limited to 450°C. Consequently, the diffusion-based γ N -304/316 cases formed are relatively thin, with poor load-bearing capacity (typically < 15 µm, 500 HV 0.3 ), and require extended treatment times (e.g. 20–50 hrs). Here, we demonstrate the concomitant formation of ultra-fine Cr/N-rich (1–6 nm) and Si/N-rich (3–30 nm) nanostructures, with short-range Cr segregation, during the early-stage decomposition of the N-modified Austenite cases from a range of Si-containing and high-Ni SSs nitrided at 430 and 480°C. Depending on temperature and Ni/Si concentration, two early γ N decomposition stages are defined based on the Austenitic matrix, i.e. a N-supersaturated γ N (Stage I) and a ‘less-expanded’ γ (N) (Stage II). The Cr/N-rich nanophase initiates via Cr-N nanoclustering along one of the {200} planes. The Cr-containing, Si/N-rich nanostructure is postulated to evolve from rock-salt FCC-structured (Cr 1-x Si x )N to a nanocomposite consisting of amorphous Si 3 N 4 in-between CrN nanocrystallites. The partially decomposed γ N /γ (N) case obtained at 480°C/10 hrs presents high case thickness (reaching 26 µm), high hardness (at 1550–1750 HV 0.025 ), and enhanced load-bearing capacity (up to 1244 HV 0.3 ), while still providing good corrosion resistance. This points to the development of ‘Nitralloy-like’ Austenitic steels and a time-efficient nitriding approach for partially decomposed nitrogen-expanded Austenite cases.

title: Discontinuous versus continuous yielding in medium-Mn steel: Role of the coherence of ferrite/austenite interface
abstract: Medium-Mn steel typically exhibits continuous yielding after hot-rolling and intercritical annealing (HRA), whereas cold-rolled and annealed (CRA) specimens show discontinuous yielding. This distinct difference is revealed by this study to depend critically on the coherence of ferrite/austenite interfaces. We found that HRA specimens with lath-shaped microstructure are dominated by semi-coherent interfaces, while CRA specimens with equiaxed microstructure are primarily dominated by incoherent interfaces. The formation mechanisms of both types of interfaces were clarified. Austenite memory effect was found in HRA specimens which allows reversed austenite and ferrite to inherit the specific orientation relationships between displacive-formed martensite and retained austenite, thereby forming semi-coherent interfaces. In contrast, cold rolling eliminates the austenite memory effect, leading to the formation of incoherent interfaces. We subsequently revealed the mechanism by which dislocations, through their interactions with both types of interfaces, govern the yielding behavior of medium-Mn steel. In CRA specimens dominated by the incoherent interfaces, the initial number of dislocations within individual grains is insufficient. Mobile dislocations must nucleate at grain boundaries by overcoming an activation energy barrier during deformation, causing an abrupt stress drop and resulting in discontinuous yielding. Interestingly, most dislocations can transmit across the semi-coherent interfaces in HRA specimens. An individual prior austenite grain contains sufficient dislocations to achieve macroscopic plastic deformation, and dislocation interactions within prior austenite grains enable dislocation multiplication and work hardening, leading to continuous yielding. These findings propose a universal strategy to suppress discontinuous yielding in ultrafine-grained materials by introducing coherent or semi-coherent interfaces enabling dislocation transmission.

title: Dynamic electromechanical behavior of Eu-doped PMN-PZ-PT ceramics: Stress dominance and thermal stability for actuator applications
abstract: Piezoelectric actuators are essential components in precision positioning and force generation systems, often operating under complex multiphysics conditions. In this work, soft-type 2.5%Eu-doped 0.52PMN-0.33PT-0.15PZ piezoelectric ceramics with high piezoelectric charge coefficient d33 = 1030 pC/N and piezoelectric strain coefficient d33* = 1120 pm/V were prepared, the electromechanical properties were systematically investigated under varying electric fields, uniaxial mechanical prestresses and temperatures. The results reveal that the strain exhibits a variation of ≈ 50% over the applied mechanical prestress range of 0 - 50 MPa, while showing a variation of < 20% across the tested temperature range 30 - 120°C. This demonstrates that within the tested ranges, mechanical stress is the dominant external factor governing the electromechanical response. With increasing prestress, the strain initially increases—reaching a maximum of 0.150% at 20 MPa—due to stress-assisted non-180° domain switching, and then decreases under higher stress due to domain wall clamping. This behavior reflects a transition from an electric field-controlled regime (< 20 MPa) to a stress-controlled regime (> 20 MPa), where domain wall mobility is suppressed and temperature-dependent phase transition effect is mitigated. Notably, the ceramic achieved a high mechanical work density of 0.040 J/cm3 with electromechanical conversion efficiency of 46.4% at 40 MPa, while maintaining excellent temperature stability across all prestress conditions. These findings highlight the critical role of domain switching dynamics and stress-temperature coupling in determining actuator behavior, providing valuable design insights for the development of high-performance piezoelectric actuators with improved durability, reliability, and energy efficiency under extreme operational conditions.

title: Simultaneously improving strength and thermal stability of Al-Cu-Sc alloys through Cd micro-alloying
abstract: Enhancing the thermal stability of θʹ-Al2Cu precipitates is critical for developing heat-resistant Al-Cu alloys. In this study, we explore the unconventional role of Cd, a fast-diffusing element, and its interaction with Sc in controlling precipitate evolution in Al-Cu alloys at elevated temperatures. We show that Cd-rich particles form prior to θʹ precipitation, significantly refining the precipitate size during aging, and subsequently decorate the platelet rims at the intersections of {100} and {110} facets, where they exert a pinning effect that effectively suppresses the lengthening of θʹ precipitates. However, these Cd particles coarsen rapidly in the Al-Cu-Cd alloy, with a rate much higher than in the Al-Cd binary alloy, which compromises their stabilizing effect and also reduces tensile elongation. By contrast, Sc, added at only 0.055 wt.%, segregates to θʹ interfaces, effectively suppressing precipitate thickening, but is insufficient to prevent lengthening because of its limited content. In the presence of both Sc and Cd, Sc atoms segregating along the semi-coherent θʹ/Al interface suppress Cd interfacial diffusion, thereby effectively delaying detrimental coarsening of Cd particles. As a result, the θʹ precipitates are protected at multiple levels, through Sc interfacial segregation and Sc-stabilized Cd particles, producing the most thermally stable microstructure among the studied alloys and improving tensile elongation at 250 °C. These findings reveal a complementary mechanism, where the drawbacks of the low-melting element Cd can be alleviated by Sc, offering another alloying pathway for further developing heat-resistant aluminum alloys.

title: Vacuum dealloyed brass as Li-metal battery current collector: Effect of zinc and porosity
abstract: “Anode-free” lithium-metal batteries promise significantly higher energy density than conventional graphite-based lithium-ion batteries; however, lithium dendrite growth can lead to internal short circuits with associated safety risks. While porous current collectors can suppress dendrite growth, optimal porosity and composition remain unknown. Here, we show that the temperature during vapor phase dealloying (VPD) of α-brass (Cu₆₃Zn₃₇) controls the surface Zn concentration, decreasing from 8% to below 1% from 500 – 800°C. The surface composition is controlled by the temperature-dependent diffusion. A battery cell maintains > 90% Coulombic efficiency (CE) over 100 cycles when the Zn content is the lowest, whereas the higher-Zn samples degraded to ∼70% CE. The difference in surface composition has hence dramatic effects on battery performance, and our results demonstrate how precise compositional control enables stable Li-metal battery operation, establishing ∼1 at.% surface Zn as optimal for preventing capacity fading and uniform lithium plating, while establishing predictive relationships between processing temperature and surface composition. This work provides design rules for multifunctional current collectors and demonstrates scalable VPD production for next-generation batteries.

title: Designing high-performance aluminum with oxygen-rich nanozones via a multi-scale defect-structure coupling strategy
abstract: Lightweight high-performance aluminum and its alloys is emerging as promising alternatives to titanium alloys and steels in demanding structural applications. However, the inherent instability of the structural and performance of traditional high-strength aluminum alloys, particularly under high-temperature, significantly limits its development and application. Here this research successfully proposes an innovative metal design strategy to develop modified sintered aluminum powder (MSAP) aluminum with oxygen-rich nanozones. Our designed MSAP aluminum exhibit ultra-high strengths of ∼415-553 MPa and exceptional total elongation of ∼7-14% at room temperature. Furthermore, it maintains superior strength across both high-temperature (∼101-163 MPa from 623 K to 723 K) and cryogenic conditions (∼840 MPa at 77 K), significantly outperforming conventional high-strength aluminum alloys. In situ formed multi-scale defect-structure during processing play a crucial role in enhancing both the mechanical properties and thermal stability. This research establishes a novel material design strategy for developing advanced metallic materials capable of withstanding increasingly demanding service environments.

title: Simultaneously enhancing the strength and plasticity of AlxCrFeCoNi high-entropy alloys via heterogeneous structure
abstract: To design high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with high-performance mechanical properties, an in-depth understanding of their complicated composition-microstructure-property relation is of great importance. This study investigated the mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms of homogeneous and heterogeneous polycrystalline AlₓCrFeCoNi HEAs via large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. For the homogeneous AlₓCrFeCoNi alloys, non-deformed models and pre-deformed (PD) homogeneous models were constructed and simulated first and the simulation results show that the PD models accurately capture the Hall–Petch behavior, exhibiting the highest ultimate tensile strength at a critical average grain size of 14.2 nm. Based on the PD models, heterogeneous structures were established with average 14.2 nm fine grains (FGs) of volume fraction fFG and average 20.5 nm coarse grains (CGs) of volume fraction fCG=1−fFG at different values of fFG≈0.53,0.83,0.91. The tensile simulation results indicate that the ultimate tensile strengths of these heterogeneous configurations significantly exceed those of homogeneous counterparts with the same weighted average grain size (16.1, 14.79, 14.49 nm), where the CGs accommodate the majority of plastic deformation, while the FGs reinforce high strength. The synergistic enhancement of strength and plasticity is achieved through strain partitioning and back-stress strengthening at the interface between CGs and FGs. Since compositional inhomogeneity may arise in HEAs, the influence of Al concentration in FGs and CGs on mechanical response was further examined. The results reveal that reduction of Al concentration strengthens the alloys by increasing the stacking faults energy and suppressing Shockley partial dislocation motion. This work provides insights into the design of heterogeneous HEAs with high-performance mechanical properties.

title: Low-dimensional ruddlesden-popper anti-perovskites: a promising platform for flexible and high-performance solid-state batteries
abstract: The development of solid-state batteries demands solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) with high ionic conductivity, broad electrochemical windows, and mechanical flexibility. However, few materials meet all these criteria. In recent years, low-dimensional perovskite materials have demonstrated unique properties in frontier fields such as optoelectronics and catalysis, and typically exhibit better performance than three-dimensional materials. Nevertheless, their research and application in the SSE field remain in infancy. Herein, we used a low dimensional Ruddlesden Popper (RP) Li3n+1OnBrn+1 (n ∈ [1–5, ∞]) anti-perovskite SSE as the model system, combined with machine learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) simulation and first principles calculations to systematically investigate its thermal stability, electrochemical stability, mechanical stability, as well as electronic structure, mechanical properties, ion diffusion behavior, and defect characteristics, and analyzed the variation of these properties with n value. The results demonstrate that this series of materials exhibits outstanding thermal, electrochemistry and mechanical stability, a wide bandgap exceeding 5 eV, low defect formation energy, unique structural flexibility, and low ionic migration energy barriers ranging from 0.02 to 0.26 eV. Interestingly, we found that the n value serves as a key descriptor for regulating the properties of RP materials: as n decreases, material stability progressively increases, the overall bandgap widens, the structural flexibility gradually improves, and the ion diffusion ability gradually improves. Further mechanistic analysis revealed that soft phonon modes at rock-salt layer interfaces within the RP materials facilitate rapid two-dimensional diffusion of lithium ions along the interfaces. This study offers new insights for designing high-performance flexible low-dimensional SSE materials.

title: Comparative study of carbon vacancy structure in sub-stoichiometric titanium carbide and tantalum carbide
abstract: The effect of sub-stoichiometry on the structure of transition metal carbide has long been confirmed by X-ray diffraction. While the cell volume of tantalum carbide (TaC1−x) monotonically decreases with the carbon vacancy concentration x, titanium carbide (TiC1−x) features expanding cell volume at small x. The outward relaxation of Ti atoms enclosing the carbon vacancy was attributed to increase the lattice parameter of TiC1−x (Tan et al., 1997). However, subsequent studies have not established a consensus on the relation between this local relaxation and the global lattice parameter (Hugosson et al., 2001). We investigated the carbon vacancy structure in TiC1−x using DFT calculations with two novel considerations. First, the special quasi-random structure is used to address the disordered carbon vacancy distribution. Secondly, the vacancy structures are compared between TiC1−x and TaC1−x to note the differences associated with the opposite cell volume variation. The lattice parameters are recovered in excellent accordance with the experimental findings for both TiC1−x and TaC1−x. The relaxation in vacancy structure, complying with the opposite cell volume variations of TiC1−x and TaC1−x, is manifested not in the immediate but in the farther neighboring shells from the carbon vacancy. The characteristic dimension of the local vacancy structure is about 2 times smaller in TiC1−x than in TaC1−x. The reduction in bulk modulus due to sub-stoichiometry is calculated. In TaC1−x, a transition in reduction rate is noted around x=0.1. The Rowcliffe–Hollox model of carbide structure provides a unified basis for interpreting all of our findings (Rowcliffe and Hollox, 1971).

title: Machine learning for materials microstructures: A survey of applications and methodologies
abstract: We present here a survey of important machine learning (ML) methodologies and associated applications that have led to recent major advances in the acquisition and interpretation of materials microstructures. These advances have enabled, for example, the automated processing of micrographs to identify defects, such as grain and interphase boundaries, and the subsequent classification of structures and compilation of grain statistics for use in quantitative microstructural characterization. To summarize the role of ML in this domain, we first outline different approaches to image segmentation and feature extraction and then describe various microscopies and associated distinctive issues relating to image partitioning and image object identification. For these microscopies, we review illustrative studies in which ML has played a crucial role in parsing the resulting micrographs. Next, we highlight the contributions of ML in microstructural interrogation and modeling by considering various strategies for image interpretation that exploit, for example, neural networks (NN) in tasks such as classification and clustering. As NNs have also furthered the goals of microstructural optimization and inverse design, we also examine how these tools have been employed to create materials having desirable properties. Finally, we illustrate the use of correlative statistical methods to assess and predict the occurrence of microstructural anomalies (e.g., abnormal grain growth) and report on progress in the creation and curation of microstructural repositories that facilitate data sharing. The aim of this Overview is to make the case that ML tools have become, in a relatively short time, indispensible aids for microstructural image processing and interpretation.

title: Revealing atomic structure and chemical complexity of vanadium carbide nanoprecipitates in microalloyed steels
abstract: • Carbon sublattice atoms are imaged for the first time in M C-type nanoprecipitates. • Co-segregation of iron and manganese is revealed in VC nanoprecipitates. • Interphase VC contains more iron and manganese than random VC. • The complex precipitate composition shows no correlation with precipitate size. • Solute-drag-effect–assisted formation of interphase nanoprecipitates is validated. Microalloyed low-carbon steels strengthened by vanadium carbide (VC) nanoprecipitates are receiving increasing attention, particularly in the automotive industry. A clear understanding of the nanoprecipitate chemistry is essential for optimizing the alloy composition and processing routes, thereby enhancing the mechanical properties of such advanced steels. The chemical evolution of VC precipitates, especially regarding the incorporation of iron into the nanoprecipitates, remains uncertain. Here, a model vanadium-microalloyed low-carbon steel is studied by atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) techniques. The steel contains nanoscale VC precipitates formed either as interphase precipitates (IP) at the austenite/ferrite interface during the austenite-to-ferrite phase transformation, or as randomly distributed precipitates (RP) in the ferrite matrix during bainite tempering. The first-time observation of carbon sublattice atoms in VC is achieved using integrated differential phase-contrast STEM (iDPC-STEM). Non-equilibrium compositions are identified under both precipitation mechanisms, with no correlation between precipitate size and associated elemental contents. Most interphase VC nanoprecipitates contain higher amounts of not only iron but also manganese compared to random VC nanoprecipitates. Complementary ex-situ small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) analysis and solute-drag effect (SDE) modeling support the co-segregation of iron and manganese into the precipitates. Manganese typically appears to form a core–shell-like structure within VC. Experimental evidence is presented for the SDE-assisted formation of manganese-rich–core (fibrous) interphase VC precipitates, and a mechanism is proposed for iron–manganese co-enrichment in random VC precipitates. This study offers new insights into future strategies to tune nanoprecipitate chemistry in microalloyed steels.

title: Sliding ferroelectricity induced and switched altermagnetism in GaSe-VPSe3-GaSe sandwiched heterostructure with strong magnetoelectric effect
abstract: Magnetoelectric coupling is vital for exploring fundamental science and driving the development of high-density memory and energy-efficient spintronic devices. Altermagnets, which merge the benefits of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, pave the way for unprecedented magnetoelectric coupling effects. However, the spin splitting in altermagnets is robustly protected by spin space group symmetry, posing a significant challenge for external manipulation. Here, we propose to utilize the coupling between the layer degree of freedom and the altermagnet to achieve an altermagnetic multiferroic with strong magnetoelectric coupling. In the GaSe-VPSe3-GaSe sandwiched structure, the magnetic order can be switched between altermagnetic and conventional antiferromagnetic by controllably breaking and restoring the combined spatial inversion and time-reversal symmetry using sliding ferroelectricity. Moreover, our systematic investigation of all pathways revealed that the transition from a ferroelectric CB stacking, through an antiferroelectric CC stacking, to a ferroelectric BC stacking is the most favorable, with an energy barrier of only 50.13 meV/f.u.. More importantly, we reveal that the microscopic mechanism of the magnetic phase transition stems from the interlayer covalent bonding of Se-Se or Se-P atomic pairs at the interface. Our findings unveil a new form of magnetoelectric coupling and lay the groundwork for designing miniature information processing and multiferroic memory devices based on altermagnetism.

title: Phase crossover enables large work output and low thermal hysteresis in shape memory actuation
abstract: Achieving both large work output and low thermal hysteresis in TiNi-based shape memory actuators remains challenging due to their inherent trade-off: the B2–B19′ martensitic transformation provides large transformation strain but high thermal hysteresis, while the B2–B19 transformation yields low thermal hysteresis but limited strain. Here, we propose a design strategy to target compositions near the phase crossover between B19′ and B19 martensites, where both phases can coexist. Combined with machine learning-assisted multi-objective optimization of processing conditions, this approach led to the development of a Ti50Ni41.3Cu8Hf0.3Co0.4 alloy exhibiting a low thermal hysteresis about 10 °C and a work output exceeding 30 MJ/m3, outperforming most TiNi-based shape memory alloys. The finely tuned composition improves lattice compatibility to reduce thermal hysteresis, while the B2–B19′ transformation occurred under actuation stress enables large recoverable strain. Additionally, grain refinement and residual dislocations enhance strength, thereby enabling the alloy to realize its full work output potential. This strategy, which integrates phase diagram insights with data-driven materials design, provides an efficient pathway for discovering new phase-change materials with superior functional performance.

title: Corrosion-resistant coatings in molten salts suggested by computational phase-stability diagrams
abstract: Molten salts enable numerous industrial applications, yet trace impurities such as moisture accelerate corrosion despite the salts’ chemical stability. Existing phase stability diagrams, often useful for corrosion analyses, disregard such impurities, underscoring the need for an impurity-aware, holistic framework. Here, we present a computational framework for impurity-inclusive phase stability diagrams in molten salts. Using chloride melts as model systems, we demonstrate three-dimensional stability maps with pO2- and pH as the coordinate plane, revealing how moisture and oxygenated species influence the phase stability of structural materials. Applied to 59 Fe-, Cr- or Ni-containing binary systems, these diagrams quantitatively predict that boriding or siliconizing markedly improves the corrosion resistance of Fe and Cr, and provide explicit purification targets for molten chlorides. The predictions are verified with electrochemical characterizations and static corrosion tests. Our results provide a practical guide to designing molten salt-stable materials or synthesis protocols in molten salts.

title: Bending-induced nanocrystallization enables large deformation in notched micron-sized single-crystal magnesium
abstract: Accommodating large deformation in crystalline metals without facture typically requires sufficient dislocation-mediated plasticity to relax local stress ahead of notches or cracks. Here we demonstrate a complementary mechanism in micron-sized magnesium single-crystals, deformation induced nanocrystallization that carries substantial local strain and suppresses crack initiation. Using in-situ bending tests on notched single-crystal magnesium cantilevers in a transmission electron microscope, a large deflection up to 31° without fracture was achieved. During bending, nanograins formed and grew at the notch root and on the opposite region, converting the original single crystal into polycrystalline. Diffraction analyses indicate these grains generally shared a common <21‾1‾0> axis while exhibiting diverse c-axis orientations. Atomic-scale imaging reveals specific misorientations and interfaces, including pyramidal/basal, pyramidal/pyramidal, prismatic/basal, and pyramidal/prismatic, which are pairs of corresponding planes of twinning modes. Atomistic simulations reveal that interface migration drives grain growth and relieves local stress concentration. Our findings demonstrate a new mechanism of nanocrystallization that accommodates local strains and relaxes local stresses near a notch root.

title: Modulating Li-ion flux by heterointerphase charge reconstruction toward dendritic-free, high-voltage lithium metal batteries
abstract: The practical application of lithium metal anode is hindered by the growth of Li dendrites, which originates from a non-uniform Li-ion flux during Li deposition. Herein, a heterointerphase charge reconstruction strategy that modulates the Li-ion flux environment and improves ion transport kinetics is proposed to regulate the controlled lateral growth of Li, enabling a homogeneous plating/stripping cycle. As a proof of concept, an in-situ N-doped carbon-coated Sn-SnO2 heterojunction (Sn-SnO2@NC/CP) is designed. The work function (φw) difference between Sn and SnO2 induces spontaneous interface charge reconstruction, which significantly improves Li+ flux across the carbon host and promotes rapid Li+ diffusion and alloying kinetics. Moreover, the in situ ultrathin N-doped carbon layer not only regulates the Li adsorption strength and molten Li infusion kinetics, but also confines the contact of Li and Li2O, contributing to homogeneous and dense composite Li anode. Consequently, the Sn-SnO2@NC/CP electrode achieves long-term cycle stability over 600 cycles with ultrahigh Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.9%. The as-obtained anode equipping with LiFePO4 (LFP) cathode demonstrates long lifespan over 1000 cycles with high-capacity retention of 73.6% at 5 C. Even at higher cut-off voltage of 4.5 V, the cell coupled with LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM) cathode delivers a high-capacity retention of 83.0% after 200 cycles.

title: Fracture-resistant ZrN-SS316L graded cermet composite design using finite element simulations and experimental validation
abstract: Ceramic coatings may exhibit immense potential due to their excellent corrosion resistance in high-temperature environments, such as molten salts. However, their application is often constrained by fracture under thermomechanical loads, primarily caused by the thermal expansion mismatch between ceramics and metals. A promising approach to mitigate such fracture is the use of graded designs incorporating ceramic-metal (cermet) composites as transitional interfaces between the pure ceramic and metal layers. Designing an optimal graded structure, however, is complex due to the numerous parameters governing composition, thickness, and property gradients. This work presents an integrated methodology that combines high-throughput finite element (FE) simulations and experimentation to design, optimize, and validate fracture-resistant graded cermet coatings. A ZrN–SS316L functionally graded cermet design was developed and optimized under thermomechanical loading conditions. The optimal designs guided by FE analysis were validated through XRD residual stress measurements and experimental fabrication. The optimized coating remained intact and fracture-free and survived multiple cycles of thermal transient testing up to 1100 °C with rapid heating and cooling rates of 3.3 °C/s and 16 °C/s, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the FEM-guided and experimentally validated framework for functional materials design and optimization.

title: Cooperative structural dynamics in the intermediate relaxation regime between β and α in borosilicate glass
abstract: Borosilicate glass exhibits complex structural relaxation behaviors, involving both network rearrangement and ionic mobility. While β- and α-relaxation processes are well established, the transitional regime between them remains insufficiently understood. Here, an intermediate relaxation regime (IRR, 0.72–0.96 of the glass transition temperature, Tg) was delineated through dynamic mechanical analysis, in situ spectroscopy and refined molecular dynamics simulations. This regime is not a monotonic continuation of relaxation but displays alternating structural adjustment and kinetic hindrance, with a distinct “turning window” (0.79–0.85 Tg) wherein network depolymerization stagnates. Relaxation is ion-selective: Na+ are activated early, promote Qn (n = number of bridging oxygens) species depolymerization, and stabilize non-bridging oxygens (NBOs) via charge compensation. In contrast, K+ remain immobile until the late stage of the turning window, after which their migration coincides with accelerated network depolymerization and topological decoupling, marking the onset of α-relaxation. Experimental evidence includes non-monotonic shifts of Qn distributions, [BOn] units (trigonal [BO3] and tetrahedral [BO4]⁻), a plateau in the non-bridging oxygen to bridging oxygen ratio (NBO/BO), and sequential Na+/K+ activation. Simulations further confirm [BO4]⁻/[BO3] interconversion, Qn redistribution, bond-length fluctuations, and stepwise ionic diffusion. A relaxation pathway map was constructed, outlining the progression from Na+-activated β-processes, through a turning window plateau and K+-assisted cooperative rearrangements, to α-relaxation–driven network collapse. These results elucidate the cooperative dynamics underlying the IRR and provide mechanistic insight for tailoring relaxation pathways in glassy materials.

title: Corrigendum to “Stress-induced amorphization promotes grain boundary sliding in olivine” [Acta Materialia 303 (2026) 121697]
Direct in situ transmission electron microscopy observation of the interaction between gliding 1/2〈111〉 screw dislocations and 〈100〉 prismatic dislocation loops in α-iron
abstract: Accurate knowledge on the interaction between gliding dislocations and radiation-produced defects such as prismatic dislocation loops under deformation is crucial for precisely understanding the mechanical degradation processes of nuclear fission and fusion structural materials upon energetic particle irradiation. However, to our knowledge, no experimental study has directly examined the individual interactions under deformation at high temperatures such as reactor operating temperature. In the present study, using in-situ transmission electron microscopy, we directly observe the interaction between a gliding 1/2<111> screw dislocation and a <100> interstitial-type dislocation loop in iron under tensile deformation at a high temperature (840 K), as well as room temperature (300 K). We classify the interactions into five reactions in terms of the behaviour of the loop. At room temperature, only two reactions happen. In contrast, at the high temperature, all reactions happen. We evaluate the degree of obstacle of a loop against the dislocation glide, such as the dislocation pinning time and obstacle strength factor, for individual reactions. We reveal that both the degrees of obstacle of a loop are higher for the high temperature, which contradicts the traditional notion, where the degree of obstacle of defects is lower for higher temperature.

title: Atomic-Insights into electron-beam irradiation-induced degradation in all-inorganic metal halide perovskites
abstract: The operational stability of all-inorganic perovskites CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br, I) remains a bottleneck in advancing their use in optoelectronics and space-based photovoltaics. A key challenge lies in understanding their degradation under high-energy radiation, which is poorly characterized at the atomic scale, largely because conventional high-resolution characterization techniques often induce structural damage they aim to probe. Herein, we address this challenge by employing an edge-view imaging geometry in-situ scanning-transmission electron microscopy, enabling direct atomic-scale visualization of radiation-induced degradation in orthorhombic CsPbBr3 under controlled electron-beam irradiation. This cross-sectional approach reveals a previously unrecognized degradation pathway: the endotaxial nucleation and growth of metallic Pb nanocrystals within the perovskite matrix, characterized by Pb {111} planes parallel to CsPbBr3 {022}/{202} planes and twinning along Pb {111} planes during growth. Complementary density functional theory calculations show that interfacial Pb atomic layers energetically stabilize this epitaxial alignment, thereby directing the endotaxial growth process. These results reveal the atomic-scale mechanisms governing radiation-induced degradation in CsPbX3 perovskites, which offer broad insights for designing radiation-resistant perovskite-based devices such as space solar cells and for interpreting beam-induced effects in radiation-sensitive semiconductors.

title: Phase selection and structural evolution in the solidified FeSe0.5Te0.5 superconductor via gradient temperature quenching
abstract: Precise microstructural control and performance optimization in FeSeTe superconductors are hindered by the unclear understanding of the phase selection mechanism during solidification. The absence of the ternary phase diagram for the Fe-Se-Te system, specifically around the FeSe0.5Te0.5 composition, presents a major obstacle to clarify its solidification pathway. In this study, the process of structural evolution in FeSe0.5Te0.5 is systematically investigated by the gradient-temperature quenching experiment. The phase composition, microstructure, and superconducting properties of quenched and annealed samples were systematically investigated. The transition from solid-liquid phase coexistence to liquid-liquid phase separation with increasing temperature was clearly demonstrated. The macroscopic phase selection results from the dynamic interaction between the Te-rich tetragonal β phase and Se-rich precipitates. The competition between the Se-rich tetragonal β phase and the non-superconducting δ phase is described in the Se-rich system. The phase field of the metastable δ phase were approximately determined through quantitative analysis. Surprisingly, the most significant annealing effect on critical current intensity (Jc) was achieved for the sample with the highest initial δ phase content. This is attributed to optimized vortex pinning, induced by a solid-phase transition occurring at 440 °C. Our work clarifies the fundamental mechanisms controlling solidification in FeSe0.5Te0.5 superconductors and proposes a phase-engineering strategy that drastically improves Jc.

title: Effect of cementite on grain boundary segregation kinetics in tempered Fe-C-3%Mn martensite
abstract: High-strength steels with tempered martensitic microstructures can exhibit low toughness due to grain boundary fracture. One contributing factor is the segregation of Manganese (Mn) at prior austenite grain boundaries (PAGB), leading to decreased grain boundary fracture toughness. Therefore, controlling the amount of Mn segregation is crucial in material design. The analysis of Mn segregation to PAGB during tempering is complex due to the concurrent partitioning of Mn to the cementite particles that precipitate during tempering. The aim of this study is to explore the effect of Carbon (C) content on the amount of Mn segregation during tempering. Two model alloys with the compositions Fe-0.05mass%C-3mass%Mn and Fe-0.3mass%C-3mass%Mn were tempered at 823 K for durations of up to 3.6 × 10 6 s. Changes in Mn partitioning to cementite and segregation to grain boundaries were assessed using atom probe tomography. The results revealed that the steel with higher C content had a large amount of cementite and reduced Mn segregation at PAGB. Furthermore, it was found that experimental values could be effectively modeled by calculating the Mn concentration of the “boundary phase” which is in “equilibrium” with the interfacial concentration of Mn in cementite.

title: Exceptional impact resistance of a high-entropy alloy governed by abnormally active dislocation behavior
abstract: The exceptional mechanical performance of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) under extreme conditions stems from the synergy of multiple crystalline defects. Targeted microstructural design, however, offers a pathway to selectively regulate specific defect types and further enhance mechanical performance. In this study, a unique microstructure comprising pre-twins and nanoscale L12 precipitates was achieved in a low stacking-fault energy (SFE) Co35Cr20Fe20Ni20Al2Ti3 HEA through cold rolling and subsequent annealing. Dynamic mechanical tests demonstrate that the HEA exhibits the highest dynamic yield strength, 2067 MPa, and strain absorption energy (SAE), 721.4 mJ/m3 reported to date among face-centered cubic (FCC) HEAs, while still maintaining considerable ductility. This exceptional dynamic mechanical performance primarily stems from unusually active dislocation behavior in the low SFE HEA, rather than from its intrinsic stacking-fault or twinning mechanisms. Specifically, nanoscale L12 precipitates suppress twin formation by obstructing stacking-fault emission, while increasing stress promotes massive intragranular dislocation nucleation. These dislocations are strongly pinned by both precipitates and pre-twins, substantially raising strength. Concurrently, the shearable precipitates and progressive twin degradation mitigate stress concentration, enabling strain delocalization and retained ductility. This work pioneers the use of pre-twins and nano-precipitates in a low SFE HEA to enable unusually active dislocation behavior, yielding a practical impact-resistant HEA and providing critical guidance for the design of ultra-strong and ductile materials under extreme conditions.

title: Revisiting Cahn’s expression for grain boundary nucleated transformations using rigorous mathematical methods
abstract: It is well known that grain boundaries are the preferred location for nucleation. Those nucleation sites are not located uniformly randomly in space as assumed by the KJMA theory. As the grains are polyhedra, they comprise faces, edges, and vertices, and nucleation may take place in all these geometrical features. In his pioneering paper, John W. Cahn proposed modeling nucleation and growth on each of these geometrical faces, making some approximations. One of his assumptions was that the grain faces were approximated by "random planes." In this paper, we clarify the meaning of Cahn's random planes by revisiting his derivation using modern methods of stochastic geometry. We illustrate our result with a computer simulation. In summary, this paper provides a mathematical explanation of when and why Cahn's equation, a well-known model, can be used to approximate the volume fraction of phase transformations nucleated on grain faces. We consider both the site-saturated and the constant nucleation rate cases.

title: Aging-meditated element redistribution to strengthen and toughen ceramic/metal interfaces
abstract: With the trend towards material integration, the mechanical properties of phase boundary (i.e., interface) are crucial for robustness in industrial applications. Especially in age-hardenable alloy-based composites, the understanding on interfacial mechanical properties with varying aging conditions remains elusive. Here we utilized an engineering SiC/Al-Zn-Mg-Cu (7A04) alloy composite as a model system, to uncover the impact of aging-mediated precipitate evolution and elemental redistribution on the interfacial properties. Small angle neutron scattering (SANS), complemented by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), was employed to quantify the nature of the precipitates within bulk specimens. In situ micro-compression tests were performed to precisely determine their corresponding interfacial strength and energy density. Per kinetic and thermodynamic analysis, the most compelling synergy of interfacial strength (∼284 MPa) and energy density (∼18 MJ·m-3) in the peak-aged composite arises from the tailored precipitation hardening in the matrix, improved interfacial wettability by Mg segregation, and an optimally balanced interfacial zone that delays failure. These findings not only reveal the quantitative correlation between interfacial microstructures and properties, but also pave the way for tunable interfaces that confer high-performance in structural materials.

title: Local porosity control in magnetron sputtered thin films: Layer design, argon pressure tuning and Kirkendall effect
abstract: Controlled Kirkendall voiding is a promising process to fabricate hollow nano- and micro-structures. This study expands beyond spherically and radially symmetric structures by addressing the voiding behavior of copper-gold thin films manufactured by direct current magnetron sputtering. Double and triple layered samples were fabricated using low and high argon gas pressures during the deposition. Annealing the samples at 300 °Celsius resulted in large voids located at the wafer to film interface and in the center of the film, depending on the layer structure. Additionally, small voids are present in high argon sputtering pressure samples. These are located along grain boundaries, as this is a location of preferential void nucleation. The final position of the voids is a combination of location of preexisting nuclei, the Kirkendall effect and mechanical stresses present in the film. To compare the final porosity of the films after annealing a novel combined approach of Rutherford backscattering spectrometry, atomic force microscopy and focused ion beam tomography was used. It revealed initial porosities of the as-deposited films to be between 0.5 and 5%. The porosity determined by FIB tomographies showed deviations compared to the results from the RBS/AFM measurements. Analyzing the void network by PoreSpy revealed insights into the void network structure. This work extends the use of the Kirkendall voiding as a route to fabricate voids in magnetron sputtered thin films, a process with a high degree of control over the deposited thin films and a pathway to scalable, novel applications of self organized thin film technology.

title: Microstructural features governing the strength of immiscible Fe–Mg joints formed by eutectic melt-induced liquid metal dealloying
abstract: Joining steel to magnesium (Mg) alloy contributes to weight reduction in automobiles, but it is challenging to achieve strong joints because the main elements of these alloys, iron (Fe) and Mg, are immiscible. Here, eutectic melt-induced liquid metal dealloying (EMI-LMD) was used to join pure Fe and Mg and the microstructural features affecting the Fe–Mg joint strength were examined. Nickel (Ni) is essential as a sacrificial element in EMI-LMD, and thus an Fe–Ni layer was prepared in advance by annealing Ni-plated Fe. EMI-LMD between Fe–Ni and Mg formed a composite layer consisting of α-Fe and Mg phases with a continuously changing interlocking structure at the Fe–Mg interface. The compositional profile of the Fe–Ni layer affected the thickness and structure of the composite layer. The microstructure at the dealloying back, i.e., the interface between the composite layer and Mg, was the most important factor affecting joint strength. Formation of a composite layer with an Mg area fraction exceeding ~50% at the dealloying back increased joint strength because stress concentration in Mg parts of the composite was distributed effectively. Ideal joint strength was achieved when the composite layer thickness was ~20 times that of the α-Fe ligaments at the dealloying back.

title: Disconnection formation via segregation-induced grain boundary phase transitions
abstract: Disconnections, long recognized as the key mediators of grain boundary (GB) kinetics in polycrystalline materials, have traditionally been understood to nucleate through thermal or mechanical activation. In this work, using atomistic simulations, we reveal a distinct nucleation mechanism driven exclusively by solute interstitial segregation across multiple substitutional binary alloy systems (e.g., Al-Ni, Al-Fe). This process exhibits zero-nucleation energy barriers, contrasting sharply with the nucleation mechanisms in pure systems. We identify states which are activated through segregation induced GB phase transitions: (i) isolated disconnections or phase junctions that promote GB migration and disappear with continuous segregation, and (ii) composite disconnections that are formed via two oppositely oriented isolated disconnections. The disconnections are mechanically robust, suppressing shear-coupled migration and instead resulting in GB amorphization and pure sliding under applied shear loading. The long-range stress fields associated with these composite disconnections further attract solute atoms and assist the nucleation of precipitates. These disconnections, absent in pure materials, follow unique nucleation pathways as confirmed through dichromatic pattern analysis and persist across different alloy chemistries and crystal structures. Our findings demonstrate that solute interstitial segregation provides a powerful and previously unrecognized pathway for barrier-free disconnection formation, thereby fundamentally extending current understanding of GB kinetics in alloy systems.

title: Study of the influence of hydrogen on strain hardening and strain localization in a Fe-19Ni-24Cr austenitic steel through quantitative dislocation structure analysis
abstract: The evaluation of hydrogen's impact on key variables of dislocation structures—such as scale and boundary thickness/misorientation—in Fe-Ni-Cr austenitic steels offers deeper insight into the influence of hydrogen on deformation behavior. This understanding can aid in designing steels with enhanced resistance to hydrogen embrittlement. In this study, we examined the interplay among hydrogen, dislocation structure, strain hardening, and strain localization in a Fe-19Ni-24Cr (wt. %) austenitic steel through quantitative dislocation structure analysis. The evaluation of strain hardening by a dislocation-structure-based statistical model clarifies the individual roles of dislocation cells, cell blocks, and dense dislocation walls in the hardening process. We find that the impact of elastic shielding on key variables of dislocation structure and the hardening parameter associated with dislocation-forest hardening is limited, leading to only slight variations in hardening mechanisms. The hardening mechanism most dependent on hydrogen is solid-solution strengthening. Additionally, this study uncovers several hydrogen-related effects associated with the activation of secondary dislocation structures and strain localization at cell block boundaries, proposing a dislocation-based model that correlates the observed phenomena. These results provide a comprehensive understanding of the influence of hydrogen on dislocation-based processes controlling the deformation behavior and hardening in Fe-Ni-Cr austenitic steels.

title: Local chemical inhomogeneities in Al-containing multi-principal element alloys explored by utilizing an ab-initio based approach
abstract: Multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) exhibit rich local chemical inhomogeneities (LCIs), such as chemical ordering, elemental segregation, and composition undulation, arising from complex physicochemical interactions. Understanding and controlling LCIs are crucial for tailoring the properties of MPEAs. A novel method based on machine learning algorithm is therefore proposed for quantifying composition undulation. Combined with Warren-Cowley parameters, evolution of LCIs in Ti-Al-Nb-Zr MPEAs was comprehensively investigated through Monte Carlo simulations based on cluster expansion. The results reveal that Al-Zr atomic pairs show the strongest bonding preference and promote the formation of AlZr-rich domains at low temperatures. As exemplified by the recently well-studied Ti58Al13Nb14Zr15 alloy, the AlZr-rich domain is energetically unstable and transforms into a hexagonal structure upon structural relaxation, corresponding to the experimentally observed α2 phase. Under low Zr content, a synergistic interaction is observed among Ti, Al, and Nb. As the temperature decreases, they cooperatively rearrange to form a TiAlNb-ordered phase. Because of the identical compositions of the parent and the ordered phases, the microstructure is characterized by an absence of compositional fluctuations for these alloys. In turn, increasing Al and Nb promotes chemical ordering and raises the order-disorder transition temperature, whereas higher Al and Zr concentrations enhance composition undulation and elevate the phase separation temperature. Comparison to experimental data suggests that the simulations yield reliable predictions on the microstructural evolutions. These findings advance the understanding of LCIs evolution in Ti-Al-Nb-Zr MPEAs, offering valuable insights into composition-microstructure relationships and guiding the design of advanced MPEAs.

title: Mechanochemical fabrication of S, O co-doped Cu for hydrogen evolution reaction
abstract: Metal-based amorphous electrocatalysts have attracted considerable attention due to their disordered atomic structures and excellent electrocatalytic performance. However, their practical applications are often limited by the complexity of traditional synthesis methods. Herein, we developed a green and efficient mechanochemical strategy to fabricate a S, O co-doped Cu noncrystal under ambient conditions. Firstly, S-doped Cu noncrystal was prepared by pressing Cu nanoparticles at room temperature in an aqueous solution of sodium sulfide; subsequently, sulfur atoms were partially replaced by oxygen atoms through electroreduction and then oxidization, leading to a S, O co-doped Cu noncrystal. Mechanistic investigations reveal that S and O co-doping enables a multi-site catalytic mechanism. The synergistic interaction between S and O modulates the electronic structure of Cu atoms and promotes water dissociation. In addition, both S and O act as active sites for H* adsorption, while O atoms further enhance the intrinsic activity of S sites. As a result, the catalyst exhibits a low overpotential of only 56 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2 in alkaline media, along with excellent stability for up to 22 days, significantly outperforming the counterparts doped with a single element. This work provides a new avenue towards designing efficient and low-cost electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution.

title: Dominant role of second nearest-neighbor bonding in strength-ductility tradeoff of bcc refractory high entropy alloys
abstract: Balancing strength and ductility in body-centered cubic (bcc) refractory high entropy alloys remains a fundamental challenge due to the intrinsic trade-off between bond strength and dislocation mobility. Using density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we show that electronic structure and bond strength play a critical role in affecting both strength and ductility. Specifically, there is a noticeable decrease in the density of states at the Fermi level, N( E f ), within a short window of valence electron concentration (VEC) around 5.1 marking a crossover from metallic to covalent-type bonding in refractory bcc alloys. This change is driven by a disproportionate suppression of e g states, responsible for σ-type bonds along second nearest neighbor (2NN) directions, relative to t 2g states. The resulting increase in 2NN stiffness outpaces the increase in the first nearest neighbor (1NN) stiffness and drives steep rise in Young and shear moduli, while simultaneously reducing local lattice distortion and ductility. Enrichment with higher-VEC Group VI elements (e.g., Cr, Mo, W) amplifies these effects, whereas addition of lower-VEC Group IV and V elements (e.g., Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb, Ta) reduces them. These results establish 2NN bonding as the dominant atomic-scale mechanism controlling the strength-ductility balance, providing a pathway for designing next-generation bcc refractory alloys.

title: Unexpected promoter: Thermokinetic role of sigma phase in accelerating stainless steel chromizing
abstract: Chromizing enhances surface protection in harsh environments, yet mechanisms for its material-dependent variability remain unclear. We studied the chromizing of 316 and 310S stainless steels (SS) to explain their divergent layer growth. Unanticipated sigma phase formation occurred exclusively in 316 SS during chromizing, yielding a layer almost three times thicker than 310S SS under identical conditions.
