abstract: The trade-off between a large room-temperature adiabatic temperature drop (ΔTad) and high cyclic stability has long been an obstacle for developing high-performance elastocaloric cooling materials and devices. To overcome this challenge, we tailored the grain size (GS) of a NiTiCuCo shape memory alloy through high-pressure torsion followed by annealing. It is found that the NiTiCuCo with an average GS of 70 nm shows a large room-temperature ΔTad of 21.2 ± 0.3 K which does not degrade over 107 phase-transformation cycles. This unique combination of properties makes this alloy highly competitive among existing elastocaloric cooling materials. The large ΔTad is due to improved phase-transformation reversibility with reduced dislocation-pinned and thermomechanical-coupling-induced residual martensite during unloading. The high cyclic stability stems from inhibited dislocation motion which is due to enhanced lattice compatibility and a significantly lower work stress (σw) compared to the material’s yield stress (σy). Our work provides not only a high-performance elastocaloric material but also an effective strategy to break the performance bottleneck of shape memory alloys by GS engineering.

title: Evaluation of micro-mechanical behavior for low carbon-containing alumina refractory assisted by interpretable machine learning: toward development of digital materials
abstract: Carbon-containing alumina refractories are important materials of several functional metallurgical components, and their service performance is ruled by their micro-scale mechanical behavior. By integrating nano-indentation testing with interpretable machine learning, an experimental-computational workflow comprising probabilistic microstructural clustering and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-guided Tabular Prior-Fitting Network (TabPFN) modeling was established. The study quantitatively identifies the micro-scale functional clusters and corresponding unified microstructural states with the proportion and influence score. A correlation between micro- and macro-mechanical behavior is demonstrated. Additionally, the effects of replacement of 10% flake graphite by 1% expanded graphite as well as the impact of thermal shock on the microstructure and properties evolution are clearly interpreted based on the key feature selection. The processing-microstructure-property integrated material model and methodology established in this study bridge micromechanical mechanisms and macroscopic performance, offering an interpretable basis for the development of heterogeneous digital refractory.

title: Strain-barrier coupled design paradigm: Demonstration of metallic nano-inclusions to advance thermoelectrics
abstract: Decoupling electrical and thermal transport is a core challenge in developing high-performance thermoelectric materials. While nano-inclusions offer a promising pathway toward this objective, their selection has largely relied on empirical approaches rather than universal thermodynamic and transport criteria. Here, we propose a strain-barrier coupled design paradigm based on lattice parameter mismatch and work function difference for the rational selection of metallic nano-inclusions. Using metavalently bonded n-type cubic (AgBiTe2)0.7(PbTe)0.3 as a model system, we construct a 2D screening map that translates this strategy into a practical materials-selection framework. Metallic Mo is identified as an optimal candidate owing to its semi-coherent feature and aligned work function with the matrix. Microstructural and transport analyses demonstrate that Mo incorporation simultaneously regulates phonon and carrier transport while enhancing phase stability, which results in a 407% enhancement in peak zT compared to (AgBiTe2)0.7(PbTe)0.3 matrix, representing a record value among n-type AgBiTe2-based compounds. By contrast, metallic nano-inclusions with poor structural and energy-level compatibility fail to deliver comparable benefit. This work experimentally demonstrates the effectiveness of the strain-barrier coupled design strategy and establishes a generalizable framework for nano-inclusion selection, offering a robust design paradigm for electrical-thermal decoupling and phase stability in thermoelectric and related functional materials.

title: Epitaxial FePd thin films on SrTiO3(001): Kinetics of single-variant L10 ordering and solid-state dewetting
abstract: Thin films of L10 chemically-ordered ferromagnetic alloys are used in spin-electronic devices due to their large magneto-crystalline anisotropy. Controlling orientation of the tetragonal c-axis is required for perpendicular magnetization to the substrate. Here, equiatomic FePd films, ∼26 nm thick, were sputter-deposited on SrTiO3(001) substrates, motivated by the small lattice-mismatch for epitaxial growth. However, differences in surface free-energies of up to ∼0.9 J/m2 induce solid-state dewetting. We tracked kinetics of ordering and dewetting of these films by varying substrate temperature, Ts = 150 to 600 °C, during deposition, followed by ex-situ characterization of structure, morphology, and magnetic properties. Additionally, we calculated the surface free-energy density of {101} planes in L10 FePd to be γ = 1.6 J/m2. With increased substrate temperature, FePd films undergo ordering from a disordered face-centered-cubic phase to a single-variant L10 tetragonal phase with the c-axis perpendicular to the SrTiO3(001) substrate. Epitaxial relationships of these phases are SrTiO3(001)[100]∥FCCFePd(001)[100] and SrTiO3(001)[100]∥L10FePd(001)[110]. Strain in films is relaxed by misfit dislocations at the interface. Onset of solid-state dewetting is from Ts = 300 °C by void formation at the interface, concluding at Ts = 600 °C with island-like morphology of FePd, faceted on L10 tetragonal {011} planes. We observed an intermediate range of Ts = 300–400 °C, in which both ordering and magnetic anisotropy are degraded.

title: Tensile-strained CoS2 with superior lithium polysulfides conversion kinetics for low-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
abstract: Lithium-sulfur batteries (LSBs) have garnered significant attention in view of their ultra-high energy density and low manufacturing cost. Nonetheless, the sluggish reaction kinetics of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) at low temperatures have limited their application in cold environments. Improving the catalytic activity of materials has emerged as an effective route to enhance the conversion kinetics of LiPSs, but the catalytic performance of conventional transition metal sulfides is often inadequate for low-temperature operation. Herein, we enhance the intrinsic catalytic activity of CoS2 by introducing 4.0 % tensile strain, which alters the coordination environment of Co atoms and shifts the d-band center. This modification strengthens LiPSs adsorption and weakens Li-S bonds, thereby improving the redox kinetics of LiPSs at low temperatures. The LSBs with tensile strained CoS2 electrocatalysts demonstrate outstanding cyclic stability at room temperature, with an average capacity fading rate of only 0.052 % per cycle over 500 cycles at 1 C. At −20 °C, the batteries maintain a remarkable capacity of 851 mAh g−1 and retain 91.2 % of their capacity after 100 cycles at 0.2 C. This study presents a new strategy for constructing advanced catalysts for LSBs and paves the way for the development of efficient, low-temperature LSBs for practical applications.

title: Redox-mediated sustainable solid-state synthesis of NiTi: An in situ study of alloying pathways and phase evolution mechanisms
abstract: NiTi shape memory alloys serve in advanced biomedical and electro-mechanical devices. However, conventional liquid metallurgical production of NiTi from primary Ni and Ti is energy and emission intensive. Here, we present a sustainable one-step approach to produce NiTi from NiO and TiH 2 in the solid state. It involves the decomposition of TiH 2 and the reduction of NiO, with concurrent diffusion-based alloy formation. The reaction kinetics were examined by thermogravimetric analysis and in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction. The results show that the decomposition, reduction, and alloying behavior of the system are influenced by the hydrogen partial pressure. Based on these findings, we have developed design guidelines to increase the NiTi-phase yield, resulting in a bulk sample containing up to 33.7 vol.% of NiTi which exhibits the desired thermoelastic martensitic transformation. The findings of this work also provide fundamental insights into sustainable fabrication of application-worthy NiTi alloys fully in the solid-state.

title: Editorial Board
Construction of thermal-stability maps for nanocrystalline metals and alloys with U-shaped dependence of stability on grain size
abstract: Nanocrystalline metals and alloys are attractive for a wide range of applications, but their broader use is often limited by poor thermal stability. Classical curvature-driven grain-growth theory predicts progressively faster coarsening as grain size decreases. However, recent experiments across face-centered cubic (FCC) metals and alloys have revealed a non-monotonic stability trend: the thermal-stability-limit temperature, Tst, defined as the temperature at which grain growth rapidly accelerates for a fixed exposure time—first decreases with grain refinement in the microscale regime but increases again in the nanoscale regime, producing a U-shaped stability response. In this work, we extend the classical grain-growth law by incorporating junction-mediated kinetic resistance, with coherent twin boundary (CTB)-mediated triple-junction drag identified as a key contribution. The dimensionless drag parameter is formulated from mechanistically motivated mobility contrasts, CTB density, and size-dependent junction statistics. A single calibration constant is determined from pure Cu and then held fixed across other materials to test transferability. Time-resolved mean-field simulations—using temperature-dependent parameters and purity-dependent diffusivities—reproduce the U-shaped stability behavior across FCC systems and capture the observed grain-size range of the crossover grain size, dc, while further enabling construction of time-temperature thermal-stability maps. These maps can be used to guide grain-size selection and define practical service windows for property-targeted microstructure design.

title: Spin-state-driven orbital hybridization enables high-performance oxygen evolution in high-entropy sulfides
abstract: Balancing the adsorption strengths of *O, *OH and *OOH intermediates with rapid charge transfer remains the central dilemma in oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Notably, the spin state and orbital occupancy of transition metal centers influence the adsorption energies of intermediates. Introducing a spin-driven d–p hybridization strategy, this study incorporates 3d Mn, 4d Mo, and 5d W into FeCoNiCuMS2 (M = Mn, Mo, W) high-entropy sulfides to tune the spin states of these three metal elements to engineer electronic structures and local coordination for improved OER activity. Experimental and theoretical results show transition metals with distinct orbital characteristics and affect the electron transfer process and induce varied d-p hybridization. It is found that the unpaired electrons in Mn2+ 3d of FeCoNiCuMnS2 endow the material with active electronic structure, which accelerates electron transfer and facilitates participation in reactions. While Mo4+ 4d and W4+ 5d orbitals possess similar electronic configurations, the d-orbital electrons of both elements tend to preferentially fill in pairs into the lower-energyorbitals. The unpaired electron accelerates electron transfer from the catalyst to the reaction intermediate, inducing interaction with S 2p. FeCoNiCuMnS2 achieves a low overpotential of 274 mV at 100 mA·cm−2 with a small Tafel slope of 81 mV·dec-1, and stability of 100 h with 91.7% current density retention. This study not only clarifies the relationship between spin state and d-p orbital coupling but also provides an orbital-resolved design for efficient OER catalysts by spin-activated orbital engineering.

title: Sulfur migration in silver: Insights from first-principles static and dynamic simulations
abstract: Sulfur impurities in silver alloys degrade catalytic performance through tarnishing and poisoning, yet atomic-scale migration mechanisms remain poorly understood. This work combines static density functional theory calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations at 10 K to investigate sulfur migration through Ag(111) surfaces. The cryogenic simulations predict a much lower migration barrier than that obtained with the static protocol. This reduction in the diffusion barrier reflects the thermal accommodation effects and methodological differences in reaction coordinate sampling. Additional simulations at 300 K confirm that the migration barrier remains significantly lower than static predictions, demonstrating that even minimal thermal motion profoundly influences sulfur diffusion energetics. A structural analysis identifies interstitial diffusion as the dominant mechanism. Enhanced lattice accommodation in AIMD – collective atomic relaxation and strain redistribution – produces broader displacement distributions than static relaxations. Electronic structure analysis reveals systematic charge transfer and Ag–S bonding evolution from ionic in the bulk to covalent on the surface through d–p hybridization. These results show that static DFT calculations may significantly overestimate impurity migration barriers by neglecting thermal lattice dynamics. The findings reported in this manuscript provide new insights into sulfur diffusion mechanisms in silver, demonstrating that even minimal thermal motion profoundly influences defect migration in metals, with implications for sulfur-tolerant catalyst design.

title: Nonequilibrium defect-phase nanostructures stabilized by irradiation in undersaturated Ni-Si nanocrystalline alloy
abstract: Nanocrystalline thin films of undersaturated Ni-8.5 at% Si alloy were subjected to 2 MeV Ti irradiation at temperatures ranging from 450˚C to 550˚C. Correlative microscopy combining transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning-TEM and atom probe tomography (APT), surprisingly, revealed that large dose irradiation at 450˚C of samples with initial grain sizes below 100 nm stabilized a novel nanostructure with three co-existing phases, the γ face-centered-cubic (FCC) matrix, γ' L12 ordered precipitates on intragranular dislocation loops and Ni31Si12 precipitates at triple junctions (TJs). In contrast, irradiation at 550˚C and irradiation of larger grain-size samples at 450˚C only produced a γ - γ' two-phase coexistence. Analysis of the three-phase nanostructure and phase field simulations indicates that radiation-induced segregation is most pronounced at TJs, thus triggering the formation of Ni31Si12 precipitates. These incoherent precipitates, in turn, are expected to stabilize the grain size under irradiation. These results are generalized using the concept of driven defect-phases. It is also suggested that the stabilization of driven defect-phases may impart radiation resilience by providing localized relaxation modes to the microstructure evolution during and after temporary perturbations in irradiation conditions.

title: Columnar atomic arrangements in Zr-Pt metallic glasses and their appearance in high-resolution electron microscopy
abstract: The characteristics of medium-range order structures in Zr80Pt20 metallic glasses were investigated through molecular dynamics simulations and transmission electron microscopy. Two dominant Pt-centered atomic clusters, icosahedral and icosahedral-like, were found to exhibit distinct spatial distribution characteristics in the simulated models. The icosahedral atomic clusters are connected through interpenetration, as commonly suggested, forming localized medium-range order. In contrast, the icosahedral-like atomic clusters tend to form more extended structures through edge- and facesharing connections. The latter can be interpreted as interpenetrating when Zr-centered atomic clusters are taken into account. We also show that Zr-centered atomic clusters with relatively higher coordination numbers tend to form interpenetrating structures on a larger scale, compared with Pt-centered atomic clusters. Remarkably bright spots frequently observed in experimental high-resolution electron microscopy images were interpreted as columnar structures formed by atomic clusters aligned along the incident direction of the electron beam.

title: In-situ investigation of stress-induced martensitic transformation in Ti–6Mo–10Al single crystals revealing crystallographic features and deviation from phenomenological predictions
abstract: The phenomenological theory of martensitic crystallography (PTMC) successfully describes the crystallographic features of martensitic transformations in various metallic systems, including Ti–Ni and Au–Cd alloys. In this study, we investigate the stress-induced martensitic transformation (SIMT) in Ti–6Mo–10Al single crystals, with emphasis on the applicability of PTMC. Assuming conventional lattice correspondence and lattice parameters established for thermally induced martensite, we evaluate the PTMC using precise experiments. To ensure high experimental accuracy, we analyze stress-induced transformations in well-oriented single crystals using in-situ optical microscopy, SEM-ECC imaging, and SEM-EBSD under controlled compression conditions. Experimental analyses reveal habit planes and orientation relationships that deviate significantly from PTMC predictions, with discrepancies exceeding 10° and 2°, respectively. Moreover, no evidence of lattice-invariant deformation such as internal twinning is observed when using any of the aforementioned techniques. The transformation proceeds via the growth of a single martensitic variant along habit planes, without satisfying the invariant-plane conditions assumed by the PTMC. Eigenvalue analysis of the experimentally determined total shape deformation confirms the absence of invariant strain directions. These findings show that the PTMC, when parameterized by thermal-martensite inputs, fails to describe the SIMT behavior in Ti–6Mo–10Al alloy, despite its broad success in other systems. This study presents a rare and significant case of PTMC breakdown in an SIMT and suggests the necessity for new theoretical frameworks to explain such crystallographic anomalies.

title: Superior strength-ductility synergy in laser-additive manufactured Ti60 alloy via carbon-driven α₂ phase refinement and pyramidal ⟨c + a⟩ dislocation activity
abstract: Tuning the nanostructure of the α₂ phase is key to overcoming the strength-ductility trade-off in near-α titanium alloys. We introduce an interstitial carbon-driven approach to modulate α₂ precipitates in a laser-directed energy deposited Ti60 alloy. A precise 0.1 wt.% C addition refines α₂ precipitates to ∼3.9 nm via carbon-induced lattice distortion, achieving an excellent strength-ductility balance: 1374 MPa strength and 13.5% elongation at room temperature, and 762 MPa strength and 19.8% elongation at 600 °C. Strengthening is dominated by the Orowan mechanism from dense α₂ nanoprecipitates, which act as strong barriers to promote dislocation tangling and loop formation; thereby, this process delays strain localization and enhances work hardening. Crucially, ductility is improved by the facilitated activation of pyramidal ⟨c + a⟩ slip, which enhances strain accommodation. Finite element modeling confirms that the unique LDED thermal cycling stabilizes this fine-scale microstructure via dynamic dissolution-reprecipitation. In contrast, excessive carbon (0.5 wt.%) forms coarse TiC, severely compromising ductility. This study establishes a new strategy for designing high-performance alloys by precisely orchestrating microstructural evolution and deformation behavior through interstitial engineering within additive manufacturing.

title: Beyond ballistic mixing: New mechanisms for irradiation resilience of immiscible interfaces
abstract: A new mechanism for operando self-healing of irradiation damage, in which amorphization competes with cavity nucleation, is identified in immiscible Cu-10Ta (at.%) heterophase nanocomposite. These phenomena are observed using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) in situ irradiations with systematic variations in irradiating specie (Ne+, Kr2+, or Xe2+ ions), temperature (100-400ºC), and dose (up to 10 displacements per atom, dpa). Irradiation consistently induces amorphization of Cu-Ta interphase boundaries; the dose at which amorphization occurs increases with irradiation temperature and ion mass. At higher temperatures, cavity nucleation occurs prior to amorphization, but the cavity number density subsequently decreases upon the onset of amorphization, representing self-healing. These ion mass and temperature behaviors run counter to the conventional ballistic mixing mechanism of irradiation-induced amorphization. Instead, the amorphization mechanism entails the creation of lattice strains from irradiation-induced vacancies and implanted ions that remaining as point defects in the lattice. This raises the free energies of the immiscible phases, making the amorphous phase thermodynamically favorable. Results are used to identify regimes of irradiation damage energy (ED) and temperature which predict self-healing of cavities through amorphization. This new mechanism challenges longstanding beliefs that irradiation-induced amorphization requires ballistic mixing and low temperatures. Moreover, harnessing this mechanism will enable researchers to design immiscible metallic composites with operando resilience to irradiation.

title: Role of twin boundary and martensitic transformation in strain partitioning and damage initiation in a metastable medium entropy alloy
abstract: Understanding localized deformation and damage initiation in metastable medium-entropy alloys (MEAs) is challenging due to the concurrent operation of dislocation slip, martensitic transformation, and complex crystallographic interfaces. In this study, a multiscale, correlative framework is employed to systematically investigate a metastable Fe45Co35Cr10V10 MEA across multiple deformation stages. The approach integrates nanoscopic strain mapping by high-resolution digital image correlation, macroscopic mechanical responses measured by in-situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction, and local stress partitioning resolved through crystal plasticity simulations. The results reveal that annealing twin boundaries exhibit a dual mechanical role during early deformation. They enable long-range, boundary-parallel slip while impeding its penetration, leading to elevated local stresses. Meanwhile, slip transmission across twin boundaries occurs on alternative slip systems, even under unfavorable geometrical and crystallographic conditions. At later stages, austenite consistently accommodates higher average strain, whereas martensite exhibits pronounced strain heterogeneity that is strongly influenced by the mechanical response of adjacent grains. Favorable crystallographic alignment between twin-related prior austenite grains, as well as between transformed martensite and adjacent untransformed austenite, promotes slip transfer across phase interfaces and enhances strain redistribution. In contrast, local damage preferentially initiates at austenite/martensite interfaces containing narrow austenite channels, where severe strain and stress incompatibilities develop.

title: Spectral decomposition of liquid viscosity into instantaneous normal modes
abstract: Viscosity, the resistance of a liquid to flow, is driven by atomic-scale friction but its microscopic origin remains poorly understood. We use a theoretical framework based on nonaffine linear response to decompose the viscosity of metallic and model liquids into contributions from individual instantaneous normal modes (INMs). Our approach reveals excellent agreement with simulations and exposes the specific excitations that govern viscous dynamics. Above the mode-coupling temperature ($T_{\text{MC}}$), viscosity is controlled by unstable localized INMs (ULINMs), which act as precursors for diffusive momentum transport. Below $T_{\text{MC}}$, we find a dynamical crossover where stable modes govern viscosity, a behavior consistent with a transition in the potential energy landscape from saddle-dominated to minima-dominated dynamics. We also propose a quantitative model connecting viscosity with ULINMs in both Arrhenius and non-Arrhenius regimes. This work provides a spectral decomposition of liquid viscosity, identifying the atomic modes responsible for it and opening a path to predict it from elementary excitations.

title: Metal/nonmetal co-doped Ni electrocatalyst for pH-universal hydrogen evolution reaction: Rapid design and interatomic synergistic mechanism
abstract: Nickel-based materials have garnered extensive attention in electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the rapid and rational design of Ni electrocatalysts modified with metals and non-metals still remains a significant challenge. Meanwhile, some recent studies ascribe the enhanced HER activity to the interatomic synergy effect, whereas the mechanism has not yet been clearly elucidated. Herein, we rapidly design the metal (Fe, Co, Cu, and W) and nonmetal (P and S) co-doped Ni electrocatalysts via density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results indicate that W and P co-doped Ni (NiWP) exhibits the optimal HER activity in both acidic and alkaline medium compared to the other doping candidates. The designing results are verified by experiments, showing that the overpotentials of NiWP in alkaline and acidic medium are 54 mV and 51 mV, respectively. DFT calculations reveal that the doped W serves as the active site, owing to the stronger interaction between W and the adsorbate in the rate-determining step, which is also confirmed by molecular orbital theory and d-band center theory. The introduced P acts as an electron redistributor, which can acquire electrons from the antibonding orbitals formed between W and the key adsorbates, thereby further enhancing the interaction strength and reducing the Gibbs free energy at rate-determining step. This work not only designs W and P co-doped Ni as an excellent electrocatalyst for HER, but also provides a deep explanation for the interatomic synergy effect, which can provide a crucial guide for the future design of electrocatalysts.

title: Flow matching-based computational reconstruction framework for multiphase materials and performance evaluation
abstract: Computational reconstruction of heterogeneous material microstructure is essential for pore-scale modeling and establishing structure–property relationships. Deep learning-based reconstruction methods offer advantages in efficiency, but they struggle with reconstruction accuracy for multiphase microstructure and lack interpretability. Flow matching has emerged as a promising solution, but its application requires a substantial dataset and remains limited to 2D image synthesis. To address these challenges, we propose a novel flow matching-based reconstruction framework for multiphase microstructure. Our method formulates microstructure reconstruction as solving an ordinary differential equation, providing a deterministic and interpretable generative trajectory. Specifically, an optimal transport path is adopted to establish the deterministic trajectory from noisy samples to realistic microstructures. A neural network model is designed to regress target velocity field that governs the trajectory, enabling precise modeling of the deterministic trajectory. The Euler method integration is used to solute the ordinary differential equation, ensuring stable and efficient microstructure reconstruction. The proposed framework is evaluated across three representative multiphase materials (NMC electrodes, Ni-YSZ anodes, and cement paste) through visualization, statistical parameters, and physical property analyses. Experimental results demonstrate that generated microstructures are visually and statistically consistent with target microstructures, accurately capturing their functional characteristics. This work establishes flow matching as an effective approach for generating high-quality statistically equivalent virtual microstructure, providing a reliable digital foundation for property prediction and material design.

title: Nucleation and growth of phase transformation twins via coupled diffusive-displacive mechanism: A case study in Fe-Ga alloy
abstract: Unraveling nucleation and growth of twins is essential for controlling their morphology as well as materials’ property, but remains difficult for the phase transformation twins evolving diffusive and displacive coupled components. Herein, the nucleation and growth of ordered face-centered-cubic (FCC) twins were studied in a Fe72Ga28 alloy, for which the complete transformation from body-centered-cubic (BCC) parent phase requires both drastic lattice distortion and atomic diffusion. Detailed transmission electron microscopy (TEM) investigations revealed that the twinned nano-variants nucleate initially in the form of L60-type face-centered-tetragonal (FCT) intermediate phase, separated either by the untransformed BCC matrix or by coherent twin boundaries (CTBs). The asynchronous transformation of FCT nano-variants, i.e. the lattice distortion towards FCC equilibrium phase preferably occurs inside an individual nano-variant, results in the formation of incoherent twin boundaries (ITBs). Upon further growth into equilibrium FCC twins, the diffusion-controlled lattice distortion leads to stacking faults (SFs) at CTBs, {111}<112>-type stages (dislocations) and rhombohedral structure (9R) at ITBs. ITBs have locally high solute concentrations, indicating that they are atomic diffusion barriers and the twin growth strongly interacts with solute partitioning. These findings add new insights into phase transformation twins. Further tests showed that the preferable growth of transformation twins enables a hardness/modulus gradient from non-equilibrium to equilibrium transformed regions, suggesting that controlling the stage of phase transformation twins can effectively tailor the mechanical properties.

title: An integrated HRDIC framework for slip system identification and CRSS determination in HCP polycrystals
abstract: This study presents an integrated framework for slip identification (SI) and the determination of critical resolved shear stress (CRSS) in hexagonal close-packed (HCP) crystals using high-resolution digital image correlation (HRDIC) data. The methodology introduces two key advancements: an improved local gradient-based SI method and a novel statistical technique for CRSS determination. The SI method modifies the objective function of the established SSLIP approach by incorporating normalized slip resistance and rectifying kinematic ambiguities that previously led to overestimation of pyramidal slip. Concurrently, the statistical CRSS method identifies activation thresholds by relating mean absolute shear to nominal resolved shear stress, effectively averaging out local stress heterogeneities. These procedures form an efficient, iterative framework that simultaneously converges on slip activities and CRSS values. The framework's validity was confirmed via cross-validation against slip trace analysis, Schmid factor analysis, and crystal plasticity finite element (CPFE) simulations. Determined CRSS values for Zircaloy-4 (RT: Basal 120 MPa, Prismatic 97 MPa) and Ti-2Al-2.5Zr (RT: Basal 114.5 MPa, Prismatic 87.6 MPa; 300 °C: Basal & Prismatic 68.2 MPa) align excellently with literature. Furthermore, implementing these values in CPFE models for Zircaloy-4 accurately predicted both local strain fields and macroscopic stress-strain responses. This approach offers a robust tool for characterizing deformation mechanisms and calibrating high-fidelity constitutive models.

title: Comparative analysis of helium bubble formation in 9Cr and 14Cr ODS steels implanted at different temperatures
abstract: Helium (He) accumulation and bubble formation pose significant challenges for the structural integrity of fusion materials. Oxide dispersion-strengthened (ODS) steels mitigate these effects by their finely distributed nano-oxides. This study investigates He bubble formation in 9Cr and 14Cr ODS steels implanted at 25 °C, 400 °C, and 600 °C. High-angle annular dark field (HAADF) imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) were employed to analyze bubble nucleation sites and He retention mechanisms. Distinct He trapping behaviors are observed between two alloys. In 9Cr ODS, He bubbles consistently form at incoherent nano-oxide interfaces across all temperatures, also at grain boundaries (GBs). In contrast, 14Cr ODS shows temperature-dependent behavior: at 25 °C, coherent nano-oxides are inactive, and bubbles form mainly at GBs and within matrix; at 400 °C, coherent oxides become active traps, significantly reducing GB bubble density; at 600 °C, bubbles reappear at GBs alongside continued trapping at nano-oxides. EELS analysis of He atom density inside bubbles, compared with theoretical equilibrium models, reveals that in 14Cr ODS, most He bubbles in matrix at 25 °C and along GBs at 600 °C are supersaturated. In contrast, bubbles in 9Cr ODS remain near equilibrium at all temperatures. These findings highlight the impact of temperature and microstructural differences on He behavior. Incoherent nano-oxides are efficient traps but low in density, while coherent oxides are thermally activated and only effective over a narrow temperature range. These results provide new insights into the mechanisms of He trapping and their implications for the development of radiation-resistant ODS steels.

title: Chemically tailored planar defect phases in the Ta-Fe μ-phase
abstract: Intermetallics often exhibit complex crystal structures, which give rise to intricate defect structures that critically influence their mechanical and functional properties. Despite studies on individual defect types, a comprehensive understanding of the defect landscape in μ -phases, a class of topologically close-packed phases, remains elusive. In this study, we investigated the planar defect structures in the Ta-Fe μ -phase across a compositional range of 46 to 58 at.% Ta using electron microscopy and density functional theory calculations. Electron backscatter diffraction and high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a transition from basal twin boundaries and planar faults containing C14 TaFe 2 Laves phase layers at a low Ta content to pyramidal { 1 1 ̄ 02 } twins at a higher Ta content. Density functional theory calculations of defect formation energies confirm a chemical potential-driven stabilisation of Laves phase lamellae. The prevalence of pyramidal twins in Ta-rich μ -phase samples is attributed to the competitive nature of different planar defects during solidification. A defect landscape for μ -phases is proposed, illustrating the interplay between site occupancy, dislocation types and planar faults across the chemical potential space. These findings provide fundamental insights into defect engineering in structurally complex intermetallics and open pathways for optimising material properties through chemical tuning.

title: Dislocation substructure evolution and cyclic damage origins in additively manufactured CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy via in situ electron channeling contrast imaging
abstract: Additively manufactured (AM) alloys exhibit complex, hierarchical microstructures typically characterized by bimodal grain size distributions and sub-micron dislocation cellular structures. To elucidate the role of these features in fatigue damage accumulation, the cyclic deformation behavior of a laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy using in-situ electron channeling contrast imaging (ECCI) at a strain amplitude of ± 0.7% was investigated. The combined influence of grain size and orientation (through the Taylor factor, M) on dislocation pattern evolution is evaluated. In coarse grains, cyclic deformation localizes via slip band formation that is accelerated by higher M. Conversely, fine grains accommodate strain through dispersed planar slip, where increasing M intensifies dislocation activity, leading to the formation of high-density dislocation regions and walls. This divergent dislocation evolution governs the overall cyclic mechanical response of the alloy. The pre-existing dislocation cells drive the initial rapid cyclic hardening, but their subsequent breakdown induces the observed persistent cyclic softening. In-situ observations confirm that the coarse columnar grains act as the weak areas under cyclic loading, where the rapid formation of persistent slip bands and associated crack initiation lead to accelerated fatigue failure. These findings provide a crucial crystallographic perspective for designing fatigue-resistant additively manufactured alloys.

title: The impact of trace Y addition on the static recrystallization behavior of Mg: A quasi-in-situ EBSD study
abstract: The development of a strong basal texture during cold or thermo-mechanical processing adversely affects the mechanical performance of Mg alloys. Alloying with rare earth (RE) elements has been demonstrated to be an effective approach for weakening basal texture in deformed Mg alloys during recrystallization. Nevertheless, the underlying mechanisms responsible for texture weakening in Mg-RE alloys remain ambiguous. In this study, using a dilute Mg-0.3Y (at.%) binary alloy as a model system, we systematically investigated the static recrystallization behavior of rolled Mg-RE alloy through a quasi-in-situ electron backscatter diffraction technique. Our results reveal that the newly nucleated grains with various orientations predominately emerge within shear bands, however, the nucleation incubation period of Mg-0.3Y alloy is significantly extended compared to that of pure Mg. During the subsequent grain growth stage, the preferential growth of basal grains, commonly observed in pure Mg, is markedly inhibited in the Mg-0.3Y alloy. Due to the inhabitation of growth selection, the volume fraction of non-basal texture eventually exceeds that of the initially dominant basal texture in the deformed matrix, contributing primarily to the texture weakening. Notably, higher segregation energy at high-angle grain boundaries facilitates Y atom accumulation along grain boundaries of recrystallized grains, homogenizing and reducing interfacial energy, which thermodynamically enables the sluggish grain growth. The direct visualization of static recrystallization behaviors offers critical insights into texture evolution mechanisms of deformed Mg-RE alloy and provides fundamental guidance for developing highly formable Mg alloys through grain boundary engineering.

title: Influence of temperature and strain rate on the competition between dynamic precipitation and dynamic dissolution in an aged 7xxx Aluminum alloy
abstract: Warm forming of high strength Aluminum alloys is a promising process for avoiding the low formability intrinsic to these precipitation-strengthened materials. However, during a process combining temperature and strain, precipitates undergo complex a dynamic evolution due to the plastic strain, which is not quantitatively understood in terms of influence of initial temper, strain, strain rate and temperature. Deformation can both induce precipitate dissolution due to shearing or accelerate the precipitation kinetics by producing excess vacancies. In this work, Small Angle X-ray Scattering in situ tensile tests have been performed on aged Al-Zn-Mg-Cu samples over a wide parameter space to understand the influence of deformation on precipitation. A competition between dynamic dissolution and dynamic precipitation has been highlighted, which depends on the temperature and the strain rate. Dynamic dissolution mainly depends on strain. Conversely, dynamic precipitation is a diffusive process, and therefore depends on the deformation temperature and the deformation duration. This competition has been confirmed by selected atom probe tomography observations. Dynamic precipitation in Al-Zn-Mg-Cu T6-aged alloy In-situ SAXS during tensile test enables determining the evolution of precipitate size distribution Competition between dynamic dissolution and dynamic precipitation depends on T, ε ˙

title: Composition dependence of the critical Rayleigh number curve for macrosegregation in multicomponent metal alloys
abstract: Convective instabilities in the semi-solid mushy zone can trigger channel formation that leads to defects known as freckles, channel segregates and A-type segregates. In the present work, Flemings' model is used to determine conditions for the onset of local remelting when buoyancy-driven flow is suddenly triggered in an initially stagnant mushy zone. An expression in the form of a Rayleigh number $Ra$, and its associated critical value $Ra_{\rm crit}$, above which the local remelting condition is satisfied, are derived. Using thermophysical data from CALPHAD, these expressions are evaluated using results from benchmark experimental and numerical studies for the nickel-based superalloy SX-1 and Pb-Sn alloys. The correlation of this local-remelting criterion with previously reported empirical criteria is also tested for various steel compositions. It is found that $Ra_{\rm crit}$ varies with the local average solid fraction and several thermophysical properties. Since these properties can vary substantially within a relatively narrow composition range, it is suggested that $Ra_{\rm crit}$ is a strongly composition-dependent parameter.

title: Nacre-like cermet-metal composite architectures for biomimetic, fracture-resistant electrode design in solid oxide fuel cells
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) have attracted considerable attention due to their high energy conversion efficiency and fuel flexibility. However, limited durability remains a key challenge for industrial applications particularly the unpredictable mechanical damage occurring during high-temperature operation. In this work, a nacre-like cermet-metal composite architecture is proposed, in which a porous Ni layer (PNL) is introduced between adjacent Ni-YSZ layers to enhance the mechanical properties of anode support layer (ASL) without affecting electrochemical performance. Two types of architectures are evaluated and compared with the conventional lamination design through in-situ high-temperature mechanical tests. The three-dimensional microstructure, reconstructed using the Focused Ion Beam-Scanning Electron Microscope (FIB-SEM) technique, is used to quantify microstructural parameters and obtain homogenized mechanical properties, which are further employed in a phase-field model to investigate the mechanical behavior of ASLs and the electrochemical performance of corresponding SOFCs. The results show that the nacre-like architecture significantly enhances the maximum fracture displacement and suppresses crack propagation. The multiphysics-coupled simulation results of single-cell performance agree well with experimental observations, elucidating the mechanical response characteristics and their influence on electrochemical performance. The proposed nacre-like cermet-metal composite architecture and the numerical simulation framework provide a feasible structural design strategy for future long-durability SOFCs.

title: Solute-controlled formation and property evolution of Schwarz crystal structures in Al-Mg alloys
abstract: Solid solution strengthening in metals is intrinsically limited by equilibrium solubility. Although grain refinement can trap solutes beyond these limits to form supersaturated solid solutions, low-melting-point alloys such as Al-Mg suffer from rapid solute diffusion and excessive grain boundary density, resulting in poor thermal stability. The emerging Schwarz crystal (SC) structure offers a pathway to overcome this instability through suppressed atomic diffusion. However, the role of solute concentration in governing its formation and resulting properties remains unexplored systematically. Here, we prepared a series of single-phase supersaturated Al-Mg alloys containing 0–25 wt.% Mg via high-pressure torsion (HPT) to examine the evolution of SC structures. A manifold morphology and coherent twin boundary networks confirm their formation. With increasing Mg concentration, the formation pathway evolves from defect-accumulation-driven grain refinement to a process dominated by deformation-induced dissolution of the β phase. All SC samples maintain nanograined supersaturated solid solutions up to the solidus temperature, demonstrating exceptional thermal stability. Yield strength rises monotonically with Mg concentration, reaching an unprecedented 2.28 GPa in Al-25 Mg, while retaining a high strength of ∼1.7 GPa even after annealing at a homologous temperature of Ta/Ts = 1. This work establishes solute-mediated SC design as a transformative strategy for ultrahigh strength and thermal stability in lightweight Al-Mg systems.

title: Suppressed glass transition behavior through high configurational entropy in high-entropy metallic glasses
abstract: The nature of the glass transition remains a central debate in condensed matter physics. High-entropy metallic glasses (HEMGs), with their inherently high configurational entropy, offer a unique model for investigating how entropy governs this transition. Here, we employ large-scale molecular dynamics simulations using a machine-learning potential to compare the glass transition behavior of a prototypical Zr20Ti20Cu20Ni20Hf20 HEMG with that of a conventional Cu46Ti30Zr8Ni8Hf8 MG. The HEMG exhibits a suppressed heat capacity jump (ΔCp), markedly sluggish dynamics, and a more gradual structural evolution during vitrification. To elucidate the microscopic origin of these features, we propose a decomposition of the total configurational entropy (Sconf) into three physically distinct contributions: chemical entropy (Schem), local Voronoi entropy (Svoronoi), and medium-range connectivity entropy (Sconnect). This framework reveals that the suppressed ΔCp in the HEMG stems from a smoother reduction of Svoronoi and Sconnect near the glass transition temperature (Tg), as quantified by an Ehrenfest-type relation. This gradual entropy reduction is attributed to denser atomic packing and higher activation barriers for atomic hopping, which restrict translational degrees of freedom. Concurrently, the persistently high Sconnect creates an intricate network that impedes cooperative rearrangements, explaining the sluggish dynamics through a modified Adam-Gibbs relation. Our work clarifies how high configurational entropy suppresses the glass transition via coupled thermodynamic and kinetic constraints arising from its decomposed evolution, providing an entropy-focused perspective for understanding and designing stable MGs.

title: Tailoring solid state dewetting patterns via phase transformation in steel thin films
abstract: Solid state dewetting of polycrystalline (PX) thin films typically yields disordered patterns due to the lack of long-range orientation alignment. In contrast, single-crystalline (SX) films exhibit highly ordered, symmetry-driven dewetting morphologies governed by anisotropic surface energies and epitaxial orientation relationships (ORs). Here, we introduce a phase transformation assisted strategy that overcomes this intrinsic limitation in PX Fe–C–Fe tri-layer films (25 nm Fe/1.3 nm C/25 nm Fe) on c-oriented sapphire substrates. Carbon redistribution during annealing at 1050 °C induces partial BCC to FCC phase transformation, establishing two distinct dewetting pathways: carbon-lean domains remain ferritic (α-phase), while carbon-rich domains transiently form austenite (γ-phase). This dual-pathway mechanism gives rise to three remarkable phenomena: (i) formation of straight, long PX nanowires, which can only be observed in heteroepitaxial SX systems; (ii) coexistence of three-fold (star-like) and four-fold (dendrite-like) symmetry patterns within a single film, defying the substrate-imposed symmetry constraints; and (iii) localized high dislocation density segments within nanowires, in contrast to the defect annihilation typically accompanying dewetting. The ferritic domains stabilize three-fold patterns via heteroepitaxial variant selection, while the γ-phase domains yield four-fold symmetry through high temperature anisotropy and subsequent γ to α reversion obeying the Bain OR. These findings demonstrates that phase transformation can be harnessed to modulate dewetting symmetry, opening new opportunities for designing ordered nanostructures from polycrystalline films.

title: A 2D and 3D microstructural descriptor approach to bainitic steels: Insights from phase-field simulations
abstract: Understanding the morphology and spatial orientation of microstructures is essential for predicting and optimizing the macroscopic behavior of advanced steels. In this study, we present a unified framework for microstructural characterization that combines experimental analysis with phase-field simulations. On the experimental side, two-point spatial correlation analysis of EBSD-derived microstructures was employed to quantify variant morphology, thickness and spacing, establishing a robust baseline for validating computational predictions. Complementing this, three-dimensional phase-field simulations were carried out under applied strains representative of press hardening conditions. Two-dimensional image analysis enabled the extraction of conventional morphological descriptors such as area, length, thickness, aspect ratio, compactness and eccentricity from cross-sections, while three-dimensional statistical measures based on 2-point statistics quantified spatial correlations, anisotropic growth and variant alignment across the simulated volume. The combination of conventional descriptors with statistical correlations provides a multiscale and multidimensional perspective on the evolution of bainitic microstructures. This integrated approach advances the understanding of complex morphological anisotropy, strengthens process–structure relationships and establishes a foundation for data-driven design of high-performance steels subjected to thermo-mechanical conditions.

title: Evolution of electrochemical redox activity and capacity in vanadium-enriched solid-solution MXene-derived oxides for Li-ion batteries
abstract: Solid-solution MXenes emerged as promising precursors for the synthesis of bilayered vanadium oxides (BVOs), offering the ability to introduce multiple transition metals and tune electrochemical properties. However, limited understanding of transition metal site incorporation in the resulting oxides has hindered reliable design. Here, we report the transformation of vanadium-enriched (NbyV2-y)CTx (y = 0.00, 0.25, 0.50) MXenes into MXene-derived BVOs via a two-step dissolution–recrystallization process. Increasing Nb content in the precursor leads to more polycrystalline oxides, reflecting cation size mismatch and its effect on long-range particle growth. Electrochemical testing of (NbyV2-y)CTx-derived oxides in non-aqueous Li-ion cells reveals new redox features at lower potentials and higher charge storage capacities, reaching up to 495 mAh g⁻¹ at 20 mA g⁻¹ (1.0–4.0 V) for the Nb0.50V1.50CTx-derived oxide, along with enhanced rate capability. Atomic-level characterization confirms uniform Nb distribution, indicating that Nb forms substitutional defects within the bilayers which, for the first time, leads to intralayer Nb-doped BVO with superior electrochemical activity relative to the parent phase. These findings demonstrate that solid-solution MXenes enable heterogeneous atom doping directly within the layered framework, offering a powerful route to novel doped oxides with enhanced functional properties beyond those achievable by conventional methods.

title: Phase transitions and enhanced piezoelectric response in high-index (310)-oriented BiFeO3 thin films
abstract: In this work, a modified thermodynamic theory for (310)-oriented BiFeO3 films reveals that the unique point group 2/m symmetry transforms the coupling between antiferrodistortive (AFD) and ferroelectric (FE) from competitive to cooperative. This pivotal change not only rewrites the phase transition pathway but also stabilizes previously unreported triclinic phases, M2C(II) and M3C(II) absent in (001)-oriented films. In isotropic misfit strain-temperature (um-T) phase diagram, three triclinic ferroelectric phases (space group P1) emerge at room temperature: a tetragonal-like M3C(II) under compressive strain, an orthorhombic-like M2C(II) under tensile strain, and an intermediate rhombohedral-like Tr(II). In anisotropic misfit strain (u1-u2) phase diagram, anisotropic strain further stabilizes a monoclinic M1C(II) phase (space group Cm) absent under isotropic strain, in addition to the three triclinic phases. Strain-driven tetragonal-to-rhombohedral (T-R) and orthorhombic-to-rhombohedral (O-R) morphotropic phase boundaries (MPBs) are identified under isotropic compressive and tensile strains, respectively. Under anisotropic strain, two distinct strained T-R MPBs can form under tensile and compressive u2, respectively, when u1 (along [001]) is highly compressive, whereas two strained O-R MPBs appear under tensile and compressive u2, respectively, when u1 is highly tensile. A small negative out-of-plane piezoelectric coefficient is also predicted for the M2C(II) phase under tensile strain. This work not only provides a thermodynamic framework for interpreting recent experimental observations [Paull et al., Nat. Mater. 21, 74 (2022)] but also establishes "cooperative AFD-FE coupling" as a new design principle for engineering functional properties in low-symmetry ferroelectric systems.

title: A novel mechanism for hole concentration modulation in Ag-doped Sr2Ca2Cu3Oγ cuprate superconductors
abstract: Controlling the hole concentrations in the superconducting planes of cuprate superconductors is an important aspect of optimizing the superconducting properties of these materials. Conventional carrier-tuning strategies are typically based on charge reservoir layers or nonstoichiometric oxygen contents, while alternative approaches that directly modulate the electronic states of the superconducting planes remain relatively limited. The present work investigated the Sr2Ca2Cu3Oγ(0(Sr)223) system. This system comprises a charge-reservoir-free cuprate that is stable only under high-pressure conditions and offers highly restricted chemical degrees of freedom for carrier modulation. A previously unrecognized means of tuning the hole concentration in this system through aliovalent substitution by monovalent Ag+ was discovered. During the high-pressure synthesis of this material, Ag was incorporated primarily in the form of Ag+ ions and most likely preferentially substituted for Sr sites rather than entering superconducting CuO2 planes. Various structural, chemical and electronic analyses, including by X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, established that this aliovalent substitution induced a remote redistribution of charge toward the CuO2 planes. This effect, in turn, increased the hole concentration without the involvement of conventional charge reservoir layers. As a direct consequence, the original superconducting transition temperature (Tc) for the undoped Sr2Ca2Cu3Oγ of 105 K was increased to 112–113 K after Ag addition. These values represent the highest Tc reported to date for the 0(Sr)223 phase. These results indicate that aliovalent substitution represents a new and effective approach to carrier control in cuprate superconductors.

title: Coupling defect chemistry and configurational entropy to enhance cathode electrocatalysis in protonic ceramic fuel cells
abstract: The strategic manipulation of A-site cationic environments in K₂NiF₄-type oxides presents an effective approach for electrocatalytic optimization. This study introduces a defect-entropy coupling strategy integrating A-site cation deficiency and high-entropy design to advance Ruddlesden-Popper (R-P) cathode performance in protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs). Entropy-engineered La0.4Sm0.4Gd0.4Ca0.4Sr0.4NiO4+δ (LSGCSN) significantly improves the cathodic activity compared with the parent La1.2Sr0.8NiO4+δ, while further introducing A-site cation deficiency to form (La0.4Sm0.4Gd0.4Ca0.4Sr0.4)0.95NiO4+δ (D-LSGCSN) leads to additional performance enhancement. The optimized D-LSGCSN cathode exhibits a transition from semiconductor-like to metal-like conduction, a remarkable reduction in hydration energy from 1.95 to 0.02 eV, increased oxygen-vacancy concentration and electronic conductivity, and enhanced proton/oxygen transport kinetics, thereby accelerating the overall oxygen reduction reaction process. As a result, the D-LSGCSN-based cell delivers an exceptional peak power density of 1892 mW cm−2 and an ultralow polarization resistance of 0.045 Ω cm2 at 700 °C. These values surpass those of most reported Ln₂NiO₄-based cathodes, representative R-P cathodes, and high-entropy cathode materials. The combination of high power output, reduced interfacial polarization, and excellent stability over 300 h highlights D-LSGCSN as a highly promising cathode material for PCFCs. This work demonstrates cation-vacancy-mediated A-site high-entropy engineering in K2NiF4-type oxides and establishes an effective design paradigm for developing advanced cathodes.

title: Suppressed phosphorus segregation strengthens martensitic steel for sustainable alloy design
abstract: To achieve high strength and ductility in steels without relying on high-purity demands or the addition of expensive alloying elements, the present study explored a strategy that combines warm rolling with the formation of nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates. Suppressing phosphorus (P) segregation at prior-austenite grain boundaries (PAGBs) improved strength and ductility, with retained P contributing to strengthening through solid-solution and deformation-induced dislocation interactions. Atom probe tomography results revealed that P and B co-segregated to PAGBs in the hot-rolled steel, whereas an intermediate heat treatment followed by warm rolling substantially reduced P enrichment at PAGBs. This suppression was attributed to the increased dislocation density, modified substructure, and possible interactions associated with Cu-rich clusters. These results indicate that concurrent dislocation multiplication with Cu clustering by warm deformation can alter solute partitioning behavior and suppress P segregation to prior grain boundaries, providing a mechanistic pathway for impurity tolerance in low-purity martensitic steels.

title: Femtosecond laser interaction with ULE® glass
abstract: Ultra-Low Expansion (ULE®) glass, a silica-based glass with TiO 2 content below 10%, possesses the lowest coefficient of thermal expansion among engineered materials and is integral to high-precision optical systems. Despite its technological importance, its interaction with ultrafast laser irradiation remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate structural and chemical modifications induced by sub-ablation femtosecond laser pulses in ULE® glass and assess how Ti incorporation alters energy absorption and relaxation pathways compared with pure silica. Using Raman spectroscopy, optical microscopy, and birefringence analysis, we show that TiO 2 modifies the nonlinear absorption threshold and promotes defect-assisted energy localization, leading to distinct regimes of photodarkening, localized densification, and nanocrystallization. The presence of Ti further drives photo-induced phase segregation and Ti-rich nanocluster formation, suppressing the well-defined nanograting periodicity typically observed in fused silica. These results reveal how Ti-induced network heterogeneity and Ti-O bonding chemistry govern ultrafast energy deposition and structural evolution, offering new guidelines for controlled laser processing of ultra-stable low-expansion glass systems.

title: A hetero-grained L12-strengthened high-entropy alloy with remarkable resistance against intermediate-temperature intergranular embrittlement and thermal instability
abstract: Alloys with coherent L12-type nanoparticles usually possess high strength and ductility, making them promising for wide usage in various technologies and energy-saving strategies. Despite years of effort, most L12-strengthened high-entropy alloys (HEAs) still exhibit serious intergranular embrittlement in the intermediate temperature regime (typically around 600–800 °C), limiting their applications in elevated-temperature environments. In this study, we successfully overcome this critical issue by engineering the microstructure with a heterogeneous architecture consisting of columnar grains (CGs) and fine grains (FGs) in the NiCoFeCrAlTiNb-type L12-strengthened HEA. Different from the brittle intergranular fracture in the equiaxed counterpart, a ductile fracture at 700 and 800 °C associated with a good ductility of 22.0 and 9.8% is achieved via the heterogeneous-grained architectures, while maintaining a high strength level of 1190 and 820 MPa, respectively. At 700 °C, superlattice intrinsic stacking faults (SISFs) dominate the plastic deformation in the equiaxed grain region, whereas nanotwins are also activated in the heterogeneous grain region. By contrast, dislocation loops, as well as stacking faults, carry the plasticity when tensioned at 800 °C. More significantly, benefitting from the strong pinning of the coherent L12-type nanoparticles with low coarsening rates, the heterogeneous structure and associated mechanical properties could be well maintained even after the long-term annealing at 800 °C for 336 h. These findings pave an effective way for the development of high-performance alloys for elevated-temperature applications.

title: Anharmonic theory of the martensitic phase transitions in shape memory alloys
abstract: Strong anharmonicity in the austenite phase of a shape memory alloy (SMA) makes the martensitic phase transition possible. However, the crucial role of anharmonicity has not been well understood from fundamental physics even though numerous accurate numerical calculations have been carried out. Here we rationalize a model describing the relationship between anharmonicity and the martensitic transition temperature (MTT) in SMAs. The strength of anharmonicity is quantified by the energy difference (denoted by ΔE2=EB2−EB2′) between the austenite B2 phase and the B2′ structure defined as the lowest local minimum of the cubic structure subject to atomic displacements according to imaginary phonon modes. We argue that both the anharmonic energy of the austenite phase and the change of entropy during the phase transition are linearly dependent on ΔE2. Thus MTT can be approximated by a simple function of ΔE2 and ΔE1 (=EB2−EM), with the latter the energy difference between the austenite and the martensite phases. The four fitting parameters in this model are obtained from fitting the calculated energetics and MTTs of five binary alloys, namely NiTi, NiZr, NiHf, PdTi and PtTi. Then this model is applied to the off-stoichiometric binary and ternary SMAs, and the MTTs predicted by this simple model agree reasonably well with experimental data. Thus theoretically these results confirm the quantitative role played by anharmonicity to reduce the MTT, and practically this model can be employed to fast screen alloy compositions for device applications towards the target operating temperature.

title: A quantitative model for strength–fracture toughness trade-off in metallic materials
abstract: Strength and fracture toughness are two critical mechanical properties of metallic materials that determine the structural reliability of components, yet they are often mutually constrained, exhibiting a trade-off relationship. However, few physically based models are available to quantitatively describe or predict such trade-off relationship. In this work, we develop a strength–toughness trade-off model based on the quantitative contributions of piling-up of dislocations to both ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and fracture toughness. The trade-off model reveals that UTS and fracture toughness follow an inverse functional relationship, which is validated by the extensive experimental data from steels and titanium alloys available. For a given alloy composition, variations in microstructure size naturally lead to a strength–fracture toughness trade-off relationship, explaining the intrinsic constraint between the two properties. With only limited experimental data, the model enables rapid construction of strength–toughness curves, significantly reducing the cost of mechanical property evaluation for metallic materials. Furthermore, a strength–toughness synergy factor is proposed based on the trade-off model, which allows for ranking of strength–fracture toughness level, providing a valuable tool for alloy compositional screening. Taken together, the proposed trade-off model offers both mechanistic insight and practical guidance for predicting and optimizing the mechanical properties of metallic materials in future.

title: A multi-length-scale study on the light etching region due to rolling contact fatigue in AISI 52100 bearing steel
abstract: Light etching region (LER) is one of typical microstructural degradations observed during rolling contact fatigue (RCF). Conventionally, LER formation has been associated with bearing steels, commonly reported in aerospace applications requiring high temperature, such as M50 and M50NiL. However, this study demonstrates that LER can also form in AISI 52100 bearing steel under laboratory ball-on-rod accelerated testing at room temperature, indicating its formation is not limited to specific steel grades. To investigate the formation mechanism of LER, a combination of characterization techniques is employed, including SEM, ECCI, EBSD and TEM. The results show that LER appears as white patches in subsurface after etching and exhibits a hardness increase relative to the parent martensitic matrix. This is attributed to the altered microstructural colonies within the LER. These colonies exhibit a high density of low-angle grain boundaries and develop a texture with the <111> axis aligned parallel to the normal direction. Within the colonies, the intrinsic microstructures consist of irregular, kinked vermicular dislocation walls, with thicknesses on the order of tens of nanometers. Such dislocation walls are formed due to the unique stress condition induced by RCF, subsequently evolving into isolated dislocation cells. Concurrently, pre-existing cementite particles generally decompose from their boundaries, presenting a zigzag morphology. The supersaturated carbon atoms released during the cementite decomposition lead to the reprecipitation of nanoscale carbides. These findings establish a multi-scale mechanism for LER formation in AISI 52100 steel and provide a more detailed understanding of microstructural degradation during RCF.

title: Self-pinning mechanism for grain boundary stabilization
abstract: Previous research focused on two different mechanisms of microstructure stabilization in alloys: thermodynamic stabilization by reducing the grain boundary (GB) free energy and kinetic stabilization by suppressing the GB mobility by solute drag or embedded pinning particles. Here, we propose a new GB stabilization mechanism, called self-pinning, in which the segregation atmosphere of a moving GB spontaneously breaks into solute-rich clusters, which produce a strong pinning effect in addition to the free energy reduction resulting from the segregation. The cluster formation is caused by strong solute-solute attraction at GBs, leading to a first-order transformation between solute-lean and solute-rich GB phases. The effect is demonstrated by kinetic Monte Carlo simulations capturing segregation thermodynamics, GB dynamics, and solute diffusion. The self-pinning provides an intrinsic stabilization mechanism for suppressing grain growth that couples thermodynamics and kinetics. The mechanism obviates the need for pre-existing second phase inclusions, refocusing the alloy design on GB phase behavior.

title: Equilibrium statistical mechanics of grain boundaries
abstract: • A bicrystallography-based framework is developed to span the microstate configuration space of grain boundaries. • Grain boundary microstates are linked to physically meaningful defect content in the form of intrinsic disconnections. • A statistical mechanical formulation is used to compute grain boundary free energy, internal energy, and entropy. • The framework identifies known grain boundary ground states and yields competing metastable microstates. • Grain boundary phase diagrams are obtained from free energies.

title: Analyzing the polytwin microstructure in L10+L12 Fe–Pd alloys: Theory and experiment
abstract: Bulk Fe–Pd within the L10+L12 eutectoid region forms a two-phase microstructure consisting of L10 polytwin plates embedded in an L12 matrix. Analyzing this microstructure via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is challenging due to its complex three-dimensional (3D) nature, which involves multiple L10 orientation variants, local lattice rotations, and numerous twin boundaries and habit planes oriented along diverse crystallographic directions. To address these challenges, this study utilizes Invariant Plane Strain (IPS) theory to guide TEM experiments and provide a robust framework for data interpretation. By integrating this theoretical framework with dark-field TEM imaging, specific zone axes and superlattice reflections are strategically selected to quantitatively reveal the 3D geometrical features of the polytwin microstructure. This methodology enables precise identification of L10 orientation variants, measurement of twin variant volume fractions, and determination of the orientations of both twin boundaries and habit planes. Furthermore, the influence of sample thickness variations on the observed microstructure is analyzed, explaining the emergence of wedge-shaped boundary shadows and the progressive narrowing of visible internal twin areas within the plates in electropolished TEM specimens. The excellent agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental observations unveils the intricate microstructural details of the L10+L12 Fe–Pd system with unprecedented clarity. Ultimately, the established theoretical framework is generally applicable to other alloy systems forming polytwin microstructures.

title: Synergistic defect and domain engineering for high piezoelectric response in Na0.5Bi4.5Ti4O15-based ceramics
abstract: Bismuth layer-structured Na0.5Bi4.5Ti4O15 ceramics are prime candidates for high-temperature piezoelectric sensors due to their high Curie temperature (Tc > 650 °C). To fully harness their potential in demanding industrial environments, enhancing the piezoelectric coefficient d33 through strategic defect and domain engineering remains a pivotal research endeavor. Herein, we propose a strategy to improve the d33 value by substituting Ti4+ ions at the B-site of the crystal lattice with (Mn1/3Ta2/3)(4+δ)+ complex ions. This substitution induces lattice distortion and promotes the formation of high-density multi-domain states. As a result, a large piezoelectric coefficient (d33 = 31.2 pC/N) was achieved while maintaining a high Curie temperature (Tc = 663 °C). The enhanced piezoelectric performance can be attributed to the defect dipole compensation effect and the reduced dynamic potential energy associated with ferroelectric domain switching of perovskites layer. This work represents a notable breakthrough in optimizing the performance of high-temperature piezoelectric materials, paving the way for their broader applications in high-temperature piezoelectric ceramics.

title: Observing dwell fatigue stress redistribution in Ti-6Al-4V grain neighborhoods using high energy X-rays
abstract: Dwell fatigue failure nucleation in the hexagonal close packed (α) phase of Ti alloys has been linked to increases of stress and accelerated microscale creep in grains with particularly deleterious microstructural configurations. To observe these processes in situ within the material bulk for the first time, rapid far-field high energy X-ray diffraction microscopy (HEDM) measurements were performed on Ti-6Al-4V during tension-only cyclic fatigue loading with 2 minute dwell periods at peak load. Series of far-field HEDM measurements taken within individual dwell periods reveal continuous stress redistribution. Extreme increases of basal plane normal stress, as identified by quantitative extreme value analysis, are found in grains with orientations previously linked to crack initiation. Specifically, subsets of grains in which plastic deformation is difficult to activate and grains oriented for easy slip both show basal plane normal stress increases that are a hypothesized driver of failure nucleation, explaining conflicting reports regarding proposed failure origins. In addition, analysis of diffraction peak profiles shows transient defect population evolution indicating strain accumulation occurring during dwell in agreement with theorized failure mechanisms.

title: Ferroelectric polarization mapping through pseudosymmetry-sensitive EBSD reindexing
abstract: Ferroelectric materials are used in a broad range of functional applications because of their switchable, spontaneous polarization. The bulk ferroelectric response is linked to the underlying domain microstructure, motivating methods that can quantitatively resolve local polarization directions. However, in application-relevant polycrystalline materials exhibiting a distribution of grain orientations, a direct mapping of the polarization direction in three dimensions has remained inaccessible using conventional experimental approaches. Here, taking barium titanate single crystals and lead zirconium titanate polycrystals as our bulk model systems, we map the local polarization directions using a new electron backscatter diffraction indexing technique based on simulated pattern-matching. Through improved pre-processing techniques (including optimized pattern processing, a new pseudosymmetry-sensitive neighbor pattern averaging method, and DIC-based global sample-detector geometry calibration) and a new pseudosymmetry confidence index (which considers not only pattern similarity but pattern dissimilarity trends with other domain variant patterns), we successfully distinguish between the six polarization directions, despite the challengingly small unit cell aspect ratio of the selected materials. The methods developed in this work are not only applicable to ferroelectrics but any material which exhibits close crystallographic pseudosymmetries—extending the current capabilities of EBSD.

title: Characterization of elastodynamic wave emission from dislocation nucleation events during shock compression
abstract: Nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations are employed to characterize elastodynamic wave emission from dislocation nucleation events in shock compressed Al along the 〈110〉 and 〈111〉 orientations. Oscillations in pressure (or shear stress) in the elastically compressed region during shock wave propagation are identified and traced backwards in time to the elastic-plastic interface, showing their alignment with discrete jumps in plastic wave velocity. It is found that the details associated with dislocation nucleation events change considerably as shock pressure increases. At low shock pressures, but above the Hugoniot elastic limit, dislocations are nucleated heterogeneously and continuously at the elastic-plastic interface with periodic homogenous nucleation events a short distance in front of the elastic-plastic interface. At higher shock pressures, in addition to heterogeneous events, discrete bursts of dislocations can nucleate several nanometers in front of the elastic-plastic interface. These details and the transition between regimes are captured in this work only because of the length of the simulation models used, which are well beyond what is typically employed in molecular dynamics simulations. Understanding the mechanisms associated with dislocation nucleation during shock, and their length and time scales, is critical to inform higher length scale simulations and models for shock induced plasticity.

title: Temperature-dependent dielectric properties in polar vortices lattice within the terahertz range
abstract: Polar vortices in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice, formed by balancing electrostatic, elastic, Landau and gradient energies, show great potential for optoelectronic devices operating in the terahertz band. However, their performance in this range is not well understood. This study systematically investigates the dielectric properties of polar vortices in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice within the terahertz range as a function of temperature. Using in situ terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS), a monotonically continuous increase relationship between the real part of the permittivity of the superlattice and temperature is revealed and the imaginary part of the permittivity reflects absorption of the characteristic response frequency of polar vortices and a1/a2 stripe domains. Combined with in situ reciprocal-space mappings and phase-field simulations, it is suggested that the polar vortex phase transition merely induces a gradual rise in the real part of the permittivity, rather than an abrupt change over the entire measurable frequency window. The distinct soften mode of the toroidic mode of polar vortex dynamics may account for the subdued macroscopic dielectric response despite the significant structural reconfiguration. These findings deepen our understanding of electromagnetic response of polar vortices in the THz range within the operating temperature range of electronic devices, which can provide important theoretical support and experimental evidence for the design and optimization of THz optoelectronic devices.

title: Non-van der Waals Heterostructures
abstract: Beyond the study of individual materials, their interfaces and arising functionality are crucial enablers of fundamental science and technological progress. Recently, the arena of two-dimensional (2D) materials was extended to so-called non-van der Waals (non-vdW) compounds derived from strongly bonded non-layered bulk crystals. These nanosystems have advantageous active surfaces and thus now complement – through their chemically bonded heterostructure (HS) interfaces – the established space of weakly interacting vdW HSs. Here, we study a wide range of 55 candidate non-vdW HSs with extensive density functional calculations and find that the resulting interfacial chemical hybridization and bonding is the key factor determining their electronic and magnetic properties. It gives rise to the formation of unique hybrid interface bands, strong magnetic coupling, and substantial electronic as well as magnetic moiré surface property modulations upon twisting.
