Our work thus provides a valuable platform for charting the new interface class of non-vdW HSs.

title: Ultrahigh electromechanical response at low electric field in Pb-free piezoelectric ceramic via defect engineering
abstract: Lead-free piezoelectric ceramics have emerged as an environmentally friendly alternative to toxic lead-based ceramics for next-generation actuators, while achieving ultrahigh electromechanical response at low electric field remains challenging. Herein, we report a defect engineering strategy that remarkably enhances the electromechanical response at low electric field via establishing an internal bias field and inducing the electrobending effect in poled and aged piezoceramics. At 30 kV/cm, an electrostrain of 0.29% (with a d33* of 970 pm/V) is achieved, and an electrobending-induced strain of 3.15% is observed in 0.79Bi0.5Na0.5Ti0.99Al0.01O2.995-0.2Bi0.5K0.5TiO3-0.01K0.5Na0.5NbO3 ceramic. The underlying mechanism of the ultrahigh electrostrain in the poled-aged ceramic is disclosed by modifying the testing method. The inhomogeneous distribution of oxygen vacancies and defect dipoles on the upper and lower surfaces of BNKA ceramic due to poling and aging is evidenced as the origin of the electrobending effect. The study demonstrates that rational defect engineering can simultaneously optimize low electric-field actuation and achieve a thickness-tunable electrobending response, thus paving the way for the development of lead-free piezoelectric ceramics with large electro-induced displacements.

title: On the mechanism of phase transformations in t' yttria stabilised zirconia relevant to thermal barrier coatings
abstract: Prolonged thermal exposure during service leads to the gradual transition of t' yttria stabilised zirconia (YSZ) thermal barrier coatings affecting their durability. The mechanisms of the high temperature phase changes in initially t' are not fully understood in terms of the role of the material shape and processing steps. Moreover, contrasting mechanisms of spinodal decomposition and conventional nucleation and growth have been propounded. In the present study, a detailed comparison of the mechanism and the kinetics of phase transformations has been carried out in high purity powders and pellets, as well as air plasma sprayed YSZ coatings. On thermal exposure at 1200–1350°C up to 512 h, the initial t' YSZ experienced the precipitation of yttria-rich c phase along with single or multiple tetragonal phases. In air plasma sprayed (APS) free-standing topcoats with commercial as well as high purity, new t and c phases appeared while some amount of the initial t' was retained, which disappeared after prolonged thermal exposure. In contrast, the phase assembly observed in 8YSZ powders and pellets were t, c, and m. Electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction analysis of APS coatings show that a cellular precipitation mechanism explains the observations better than spinodal decomposition in scenarios where t' is present along with t and c. Conventional precipitation mechanism explains the absence of t' during aging of powders and pellets. The phase transformation kinetics were correlated with changes in Raman spectra and benchmarked against XRD results.

title: Internal architecture and multiple structural transformations of large-height stacking faults in 4H-SiC trapezoidal defects
abstract: 4H-SiC is a critical compound semiconductor for high-power electronic devices. However, the performance of 4H-SiC substrates and epitaxial wafers is often compromised by structural defects, predominantly stacking faults (SFs). Trapezoidal defects (TZDs)—bar-shaped SFs exceeding 1000 µm in length—are prevalent in these materials. Although achieving defect-free 4H-SiC is crucial, the fundamental crystallographic nature of TZDs remains largely elusive. In this study, we demonstrate that TZDs are not single SFs but comprise multiple Shockley-type large-height SFs (LHSFs) of up to 32 layers. These form through successive structural transformations between SFs via the gliding of basal plane Shockley partial dislocations (BPSPDs). These mechanisms were comprehensively confirmed using photoluminescence (PL) mapping, KOH etching, X-ray topography, and high-angle annular dark-field high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF HR-STEM). Our findings reveal that the stacking fault energies of almost all LHSFs are exceptionally low (< 1 mJ/m²), elucidating the thermodynamic driving force for their facile and multiple transformations. Furthermore, we successfully identified the previously indeterminate PL emission wavelengths for various LHSFs, narrowing their signatures to a precise 425–431 nm range based on their specific fractional configurations. Crucially, we highlight the severe risk of defect misidentification; relying solely on these optical signatures can lead to erroneous conclusions, as starkly demonstrated by a Shockley-type LHSF emitting at 457 nm—perfectly mimicking a Frank-type defect. Ultimately, this study provides a fundamental understanding of atypical yet pervasive Shockley-type LHSFs, which is essential for advancing the physical understanding of defect evolution and crystallographic stability in wide-bandgap semiconductors.

title: Coupled influence of structural relaxation and compositional complexity on deformation behavior and intermittent plasticity in Cu-Zr-based metallic glasses
abstract: Understanding the coupled influence of sub-glass-transition ( T g ) annealing and alloying on plastic flow in metallic glasses (MGs) remains a challenge because structural relaxation and compositional complexity simultaneously change the local atomic environments which govern shear activation. Here, we combine high-energy X-ray total scattering, differential scanning calorimetry, nanoindentation, and molecular dynamics to establish a structural-state description that links local structure to deformation behavior in Cu-Zr-(Al/Ag/Ti) MGs. Sub- T g annealing and increased compositional complexity sharpen the primary peak of the pair distribution function, produce a small dilation of the nearest-neighbor distance, increase the peak-position ratio, and the fraction of quasi-icosahedral local environments, while reducing the magnitude and spatial connectivity of excess free volume. These coupled changes are summarized by a structural coordinate R , constructed from descriptors of short-range structural ordering, relaxation enthalpy, and local atomic packing, and validated on the alloying-order-swapped alloys using the same calibration. The indentation response varies systematically with this structural-state description: strain-rate sensitivity increases with R , whereas the shear activation volume decreases. Intermittent plasticity also weakens with relaxation, and serration energies and large displacement burst events diminish as the connected plastic-zone footprint contracts. The results show that chemistry primarily determines the initial atomic structure and the capacity for sub- T g relaxation, while annealing progressively drives the MG toward a more relaxed structural state, providing a comparative basis for relating strain-rate sensitivity and the spatial correlation of plasticity to structural state in Cu-Zr-based MGs.

title: Advanced single-atom Fe catalysts via sulfur-mediated spin engineering for high-performance Zn-air batteries
abstract: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are central to renewable energy technologies, yet their sluggish kinetics and reliance on scarce noble-metal catalysts hinder large-scale implementation. Here, we demonstrate that sulfur (S) -mediated spin-state engineering of single-atom Fe catalysts establishes a direct structure-spin-activity relationship for bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis. Optimal S coordination shifts the Fe centers to a high-spin configuration within a porous hollow carbon architecture. This spin-state modulation optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygen intermediates, lowering kinetic barriers for both ORR and OER. FeS2NC-h exhibits outstanding OER and ORR activity in alkaline media, achieving a low potential gap (ΔE) of 0.63 V, markedly outperforming the commercial Pt/C+IrO2 (0.79 V). In rechargeable Zn-air batteries (RZABs), FeS2NC-h enables an open-circuit voltage of 1.50 V, peak power density of 202 mW cm−2, specific capacity of 812 mAh gZn−1, and exceptional cycling durability exceeding 1200 h with round-trip efficiency >58%. This work establishes heteroatom-enabled spin-state engineering as a powerful strategy to transcend traditional coordination optimization, offering a general pathway to noble-metal-free integrated oxygen electrocatalysts for sustainable energy conversion and storage.

title: F-mediated dynamic electronic regulation via CoF2 reservoir enables high-valence Ni for enhanced oxygen evolution
abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is kinetically sluggish, where high-valence metal sites can accelerate reaction kinetics but suffer from thermodynamic formation barrier. Here, we design a hierarchical F-modulated NiFe layered double hydroxide (LDH)/CoF2 heterostructure to enable F-mediated dynamic electronic regulation of Ni sites, where NiFe LDH serves as the primary active phase and CoF2 acts as a dynamic fluoride reservoir, thereby promoting the formation of Ni3+δ/Ni4+. During synthesis, F released from CoF2 can be incorporated into the forming NiFe LDH. Under OER conditions, CoF2 reconstructs into CoOOH, accompanied by partial F re-coordination within the reconstructed (oxy)hydroxide framework. This dynamic F participation redistributes local charge density, renders Ni sites more electron-deficient, and facilitates deep Ni oxidation toward Ni3+δ/Ni4+, as evidenced by spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses. Density functional theory calculations reveal that high-valence Ni sites optimize intermediate binding and reduce the deprotonation energy (*OH → *O). Consequently, the catalyst only requires 290 mV at 1000 mA cm−2 with a 1200-h stability. The anion exchange membrane electrolyzer achieves a low voltage of 1.988 V at 1000 mA cm−2, highlighting its potential for industrial applications.

title: Editorial Board
Intrinsic ductility enhancement in Mg alloys elucidated via large-scale ab-initio calculations
abstract: Magnesium is the lightest structural alloy, yet its practical use is limited by its low ductility. Recent studies suggest ductility enhancement in dilute Mg alloys may stem from favorable solute modification of pyramidal I/II screw dislocation core energy difference, activating slip via a double cross-slip mechanism. This work conducts large-scale DFT calculations, reaching ~6,000 atoms, of dislocation energetics in Mg and Mg-Y/Zn alloys. We find that relative solute strengthening effects on pyramidal I and II screw dislocation glide are crucial for cross-slip enhancement in Mg-Y, in contrast to prior investigations, that find solute-mediated dislocation-core energy modification as the main driver. Our predictions align with single- and poly-crystal experimental results and also capture the transition from pyramidal II to I preferred slip in Mg-Y.

title: A new cracking criterion for additive manufacturing and repair of Ni-based superalloys via laser directed energy deposition
abstract: While the cracking mechanisms of Ni-based superalloys in laser directed energy deposition (L-DED) are relatively well-documented, current multi-element cracking criteria continue to suffer from numerical divergence at the solidification terminus and are further constrained by the limited availability of thermodynamic data. This study investigates the cracking behavior during L-DED of two superalloys, In738 and In939, which possess similar constituent elements but exhibit different cracking susceptibilities. The results demonstrate that cracking is primarily attributed to the evolution of solid and liquid phase properties induced by solute partitioning, which is governed by the initial alloy composition and partition coefficients. Furthermore, a rigorous mathematical proof utilizing matrix space transformations is presented to establish the affine relationship between solidification path and dendritic growth geometry. Building upon this relationship and a two-dimensional bicrystal model, a new solidification cracking criterion Se=2λG[Ta(1−a)−∫a1Tsdfs1/2]was established through continuous analytical derivation, where 2λ is the primary dendrite arm spacing, G is the temperature gradient, and Ts is the solidus temperature at a given solid fraction fs. This criterion exhibits rapid convergence as fs→1 at the solidification terminus, thereby overcoming the inherent numerical divergence of traditional indices, and indirectly indicates of liquation cracking susceptibility. By further incorporating transformation stress and strengthening disparity factors associated with solid-state cracking, a continuous L-DED cracking susceptibility map was constructed. The computation of the new criterion is independent of commercial thermodynamic software. Consequently, this criterion can be applied to guide material selection and high-throughput compositional design for the high-quality additive manufacturing and repair of Ni-based superalloys.

title: Spatial distributions of grain boundary segregation – A combined atom probe and atomistic simulation study
abstract: Understanding grain boundary segregation requires consideration of a wide range of length scales, spanning from grain boundary networks to site-wise atomistics. To understand the impact different length scales have, we use side-by-side segregation measurements from atom-probe tomography and atomistic simulations on a nickel binary system. We first develop a shared framework to analyze both datasets, cross-validating the identification of grain boundary planes and the measurement of interfacial excess in atom probe, as such quantities are directly known in atomistic simulations. By analyzing multiple polycrystalline boundaries, we highlight significant inhomogeneity within a given boundary, compared to the relative similarity between different boundaries. These local variations in concentration are discussed in light of site-wise segregation spectra. The resulting investigation, with knowledge of how segregation varies over different interfacial areas, provides guidelines for extracting the average composition of a given boundary, as well as the measurement of polycrystalline-average grain boundary concentrations.

title: Phase-dependent first-principles prediction of pressure-composition isotherms in yttrium- and zirconium-based metal hydrides
abstract: Metal hydrides are promising neutron moderator materials for advanced nuclear micro-reactors owing to their high hydrogen density and favorable thermodynamic stability. Pressure–composition isotherms (PCI) are fundamental descriptors of hydride formation, phase stability, and functional performance; however, systematic experimental determination over wide composition ranges remains costly and technically demanding. Here, we develop a phase-dependent first-principles thermodynamic framework by incorporating crystal-structure corrections into the model proposed by Mitsuhara, enabling quantitative prediction of PCI behavior using parameters derived exclusively from density functional theory calculations. The framework is validated against experimental pressure–composition–temperature (PCT) data for yttrium- and zirconium-based metal hydrides, showing excellent agreement across wide hydrogen concentration ranges. The results demonstrate that Cr alloying suppresses hydrogen dissolution in yttrium, shifting equilibrium pressures upward and narrowing the two-phase plateau region. In contrast, although atomic-scale calculations predict a plateau-broadening effect for Zr addition, this behavior is not observed experimentally. This discrepancy is resolved by introducing the virtual crystal approximation, which mitigates the over-amplification of localized alloying effects in macroscopic thermodynamic predictions. Overall, the proposed phase-dependent, non-empirical framework establishes a direct link between atomic-scale hydrogen–metal interactions and macroscopic PCT behavior, providing a predictive and mechanistic tool for the design of multi-component metal hydride neutron moderators.

title: Inclination-dependent shear-coupling and energy anisotropy in FCC tilt grain boundaries
abstract: Inclination-dependent grain boundary (GB) energy and shear-coupled motion are studied for [ 001 ] and [ 111 ] tilt GBs in face-centered cubic materials using three-dimensional (3D) phase field crystal (PFC) simulations. A large dataset spanning misorientation and inclination space is systematically generated to evaluate trends in GB energy and shear-coupling. GB energy variations broadly follow ideal faceting and predictions by existing models. The shear-coupling response shows strong dependence on crystallography and GB inclination. Comparisons based on different domain sizes indicate that significant structural differences, including facets of different sizes, do not necessarily produce large variations in shear-coupling behavior. The results also demonstrate the applicability of 3D PFC modeling for systematic studies of inclination-dependent GB properties, extending previous two-dimensional PFC studies.

title: Oxygen interstitial-assisted cation interstitial diffusion in fluorite oxides
abstract: Understanding how defects evolve under irradiation - where atomic displacements generate defects of vacancy and interstitial types - is vital for unlocking the full potential of fluorite oxides in nuclear energy applications. In fluorite oxides like UO2 and ThO2, interstitials often aggregate into dislocation loops, degrading thermal conductivity and promoting cavity swelling, which undermines fuel performance and safety. However, the mechanisms behind loop formation remain elusive due to challenges in scale, even for the state-of-the-art techniques: the relevant atomic processes are too small for direct observation and too complex for modeling. Notably, the low mobility of cation interstitials predicted by density functional theory (DFT) cannot account for the widespread experimental observations of loop formation. Using ThO2 as a model system, we employed computationally efficient molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to capture the real-time evolution of initially isolated thorium and oxygen interstitials and identify stable and mobile interstitial clusters. The thermal stability and mobility of kinetically favorable interstitial clusters were further validated through high-fidelity DFT calculations. Interestingly, the results show that the Th interstitial decorated with O interstitials becomes increasingly stable and mobile until up to four O interstitials, with a decreasing barrier over the cluster size. Bader charge analysis suggests this enhanced mobility arises from O-mediated screening of the Coulomb repulsion between Th ions in the local environment. These insights were extended to UO2 and CeO2 via MD calculations, advancing the current understanding of ionic transport and resolving a critical knowledge gap in understanding interstitial loop formation in fluorite oxides.

title: Segregation-controlled diffusion-induced grain boundary migration in alloy 690
abstract: Grain boundary (GB) migration accompanied by Cr depletion is widely observed in Alloy 690 and is closely linked to intergranular degradation and stress corrosion cracking. However, the fundamental driving force for GB migration and its link with Cr depletion remains unclear. In this work, hybrid molecular dynamics and semi-grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations were employed to investigate GB migration in Alloy 690 under coupled solute diffusion and segregation effects across a range of GB characters. The results show that Cr segregation at GBs, while generally considered favorable for GB stability, can facilitate diffusion-induced GB migration and Cr depletion. Cr diffusion along GBs produces localized Cr depletion zones that are energetically incompatible with positively segregating GBs, generating a chemical driving force that drives GB migration toward the Cr-rich matrix, which ultimately results in persistent GB migration accompanied by a Cr depletion. By quantifying solute–GB interaction energetics, we demonstrate that GB migration is quantitively controlled by the coupled effects of solute diffusivity and segregation strength. These mechanistic insights provide a unified framework that rationalizes experimentally observed correlations between GB character, Cr depletion, and GB migration in Cr-containing alloys.

title: Electric-field-modulated luminescence in highly stable and transparent Er-doped PMN-PT crystals
abstract: Relaxor ferroelectric single crystals, epitomized by PMN-PT, exhibit giant piezoelectricity but are intrinsically bottlenecked by their vulnerability to electric-field-induced depolarization and severe optical opacity caused by complex domain wall scattering. Herein, we propose a synergistic strategy integrating B-site defect engineering and alternating current (AC) domain engineering to construct a highly stable, transparent, and multifunctional Er3+-doped PMN-PT single crystal. Ion radius difference drives Er3+ to preferentially occupy the perovskite B-site, spontaneously generating Er-oxygen vacancy defect dipoles. These dipoles serve as robust pinning centers, constructing an internal bias field that significantly enhances the coercive field and electromechanical stability, while simultaneously achieving a giant piezoelectric coefficient (d33 ∼ 2300 pC/N) at the morphotropic phase boundary. Furthermore, AC-poling selectively annihilates the light-scattering 71° domain walls, reshaping the crystal into a highly ordered “2R” macroscopic domain state and boosting optical transmittance to nearly 70%. Capitalizing on this highly transparent optical window, the intrinsic luminescence of Er3+ is fully liberated. Notably, we discover a unique three-stage, non-monotonic electric-field modulation of photoluminescence intensity, which fundamentally maps the intricate dynamics from the intrinsic electro-optic effect to polar nanoregions (PNRs) competition and eventual macroscopic domain reconfiguration. This work not only resolves the long-standing trade-off between piezoelectric stability and optical transparency but also establishes a compelling materials paradigm for next-generation piezoelectric-optoelectronic coupled devices and smart sensors.

title: Self-healing by amorphous shear-band recovery in crystalline Al-Sm materials
abstract: Durability and longevity are among the key factors for applications of structural metallic materials. Since it is unrealistic to prevent stress-induced damage, self-healing could provide an alternative pathway to extend the material lifetime. Self-healing has been explored before in metals reinforced with shape-memory alloy (SMA). However, the poor interfacial bonding between embedded SMA and metallic matrices resulted in limited strength recovery. Here, we discovered that solid-solid phase transformation within the stress-induced amorphous shear bands in Al-Sm systems provides a promising strategy for strength recovery through self-healing. Based on a combination of experimental characterization and atomistic simulations, we demonstrated that amorphous shear bands in the Al-Sm system could transform back to crystalline structure during annealing at temperatures as low as 150 °C. This self-healing mechanism, driven by the amorphous-to-crystalline phase transformation allows the recovered materials to restore mechanical properties to a similar level as those of the undeformed samples. Our findings provide a potential strategy for the design of easy-self-healing materials with recyclable mechanical properties.

title: Shear-coupled migration governed by misorientation angles and atomistic structures in [1 1 0] symmetric tilt grain boundaries of face-centered-cubic Pt
abstract: Shear-coupled grain boundary (GB) migration plays a crucial role in the deformation of polycrystalline materials. Although this phenomenon has been extensively investigated in [001] symmetric tilt GBs, other important GB systems remain relatively unexplored, hindering a comprehensive understanding of the underlying mechanisms. In this work, we systematically investigated shear-coupled migration in [110] symmetric tilt GBs of face-centered cubic Pt metal using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations by a high-efficient machine learning potential. For low-angle GBs, shear-coupled migration is found to proceed via collective intersecting dislocation glide, which generates steps on the second invariant plane. For GB approaching the Σ3(111) twin boundary, a twin-boundary-mediated migration mechanism is identified. Furthermore, the dependence of coupling mode on both the misorientation angle and the local GB configuration has been elucidated.

title: Bayesian conditional generation of porous media using dynamic surrogate and generative models
abstract: Porous-media performance in energy and materials systems is strongly influenced by microstructure, yet designing architectures that reproduce desired time-dependent flow behaviors remains challenging. Existing approaches, from trial-and-error experimentation and topology optimization to data-driven generative models, often focus on static metrics, neglect uncertainty and non-uniqueness, or rely on costly flow simulations, which limit their use for matching dynamic properties. In this work, we present a dynamic-constrained framework for inverse microstructure design that integrates a latent diffusion generative model with Bayesian inference using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). The transient saturation behavior of each generated structure is predicted efficiently using a residual U-Net-based recurrent surrogate model that learns the mapping between microstructural images and their time-dependent saturation fields. The goal is to generate microstructures whose saturation-curve dynamics match user-specified targets. Two design settings are examined: ( i ) matching a target range of acceptable responses and ( ii ) matching a single prescribed response, each evaluated for cases in which the targets lie within or outside the variability of the prior generative ensemble. When the targets fall within prior range, MCMC sampling reduces uncertainty by concentrating posterior realizations around the target band. When the targets fall outside that range, the sampler moves beyond the prior and adjusts latent variables to synthesize new and physically consistent morphologies whose dynamic responses align with the desired behavior. The improvements are illustrated through property histograms and clustering around the target in principal-component space.

title: Hierarchical polysulfide management via a core-shell host: simultaneous trapping, catalyzing, and buffering for high-energy lithium sulfur batteries
abstract: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries exhibit high specific energy and favorable energy storage properties, challenges such as lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) shuttle and electrode volume expansion remain. Although traditional catalysts can initially mitigate the slow sulfur redox kinetics, the volume expansion caused by sulfur conversion may still lead to structural damage of the electrode, ultimately resulting in rapid capacity decay of the battery. Here, a reasonably designed multifunctional core-shell structure is synthesized as a sulfur host for lithium-sulfur batteries to mitigate the volume effect during sulfur conversion. Meanwhile, the poly(dopamine) coating acts as a dense physical barrier, significantly suppressing polysulfide shuttling. Additionally, Ni nanoparticles within the carbon spheres serve as highly active catalytic sites, substantially promoting polysulfide conversion. Benefiting from this tri-functional synergy combining confinement, catalysis, and mechanical stabilization, the PDA@NHCS-Ni cathode delivers a high initial discharge capacity of 986.2 mA h g-1 at 1.0 C and demonstrates outstanding cycling performance, with an average capacity decay rate of 0.059% per cycle over 1000 cycles. This work offers a feasible strategy for developing high-performance Li-S batteries.

title: Atomistic modeling of polymorphism in iron using an explicitly magnetic machine-learned interatomic potential
abstract: While several efforts have been made to incorporate spin dynamics explicitly into interatomic potentials for magnetic materials, they have typically been unable to account for polymorphism and the change in magnetic interaction with structure. Those that do have had difficulties in reproducing the experimentally or theoretically known properties of multiple phases in dynamic simulation. Using the Rapid Artificial Neural Network (RANN) machine-learned interatomic potential as a template, we introduce magnetically coupled structural fingerprints in addition to the typical non-magnetic descriptors. These are used with a first principles database for pure iron to train an explicitly magnetic RANN potential which reproduces a number of experimentally observed and theoretically calculated properties of both the ferritic and austenitic phases of iron. Critically, these include the magnon spectrum of BCC iron, the demagnetization and Curie Temperature of ferrite, and phase transitions with increasing temperature, including the presence of the high temperature BCC phase. This provides not only a machine-learned interatomic potential which can be used in LAMMPS to study inherently magnetic, mechanical, and thermodynamic properties of iron, but also a template for the creation of magnetic MLIPs for other materials and alloys.

title: Current density dependence of cation diffusion in Er2O3/Y2O3 diffusion couple under AC-flash events
abstract: The dependence of cationic diffusivity on current density was investigated using Er2O3/Y2O3 diffusion couples subjected to alternating current (AC) flash events with current density amplitudes of 30–60 mA∙mm−2 and furnace temperatures of 1050–1300oC at a constant frequency of 1000 Hz. An increase in current density athermally enhanced both the grain boundary and lattice diffusivities, reducing activation energies, whereas the effect of Joule heating on specimen temperature was relatively limited. Porosity also considerably increased with current density, especially at grain boundaries, suggesting that grain boundaries could serve as the source of oxygen gas bubbles (pores) and vacancies under AC flash events. The strong correlation between diffusivity enhancement and porosity evolution indicates that oxygen vacancies generated along grain boundaries play a main role in promoting cationic diffusion during AC flash events.

title: Compatibilities and supercompatibility conditions in shape memory alloys determined from correspondence, metrics and symmetries
abstract: The phenomenological theory of martensite crystallography (PTMC) explains the habit planes of bi-variant laminate martensite product and the transformation twins between the variants. It also permits to determine whether or not the austenite and martensite lattice parameters satisfy supercompatibility by three mathematical equations called “cofactor conditions”. The PTMC calculations are in great part based on mathematical tools of continuum mechanics (polar decompositions and stretch tensors). Here, we propose to use an alternative approach called correspondence theory (CT). Supercompatibility is obtained when three types of compatibility are satisfied: a) austenite/martensite (A/M) compatibility by invariant plane strain (IPS) lattice distortion, b) martensite/martensite (M/M) compatibility by transformation twins, and c) their intercompatibility by a parallelism between the shear direction of the IPS and the shear direction of the twin. The satisfaction of this “shear/shear” condition implies that of the cofactor conditions. These conditions can be written with pure crystallographic parameters (metrics, group of symmetries and correspondence). The twin equations are obtained from double-coset decomposition of the group of austenite symmetries. The A/M compatibility condition appears as a degeneracy condition of a quadratic form of a symmetric matrix called “compatibility by metric correspondence” (CMC). The IPS shear vector in the shear/shear equation is obtained from another matrix called “shear by metric correspondence” (SMC). As example, it is shown that B19’ martensite is supercompatible if its lattice parameters follow specific analytical functions of the monoclinic angle. The CT offers a promising framework to develop new shape memory alloys with supercompatible martensite and high fatigue resistance.

title: Unveiling the role of Co single atoms on the local coordination states and photo-induced electronic shifts in Nb2O5
abstract: Atomically dispersed transition metal sites offer a unique platform to manipulate electronic structure; however, their role in governing photo-induced charge dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we report the incorporation of Co single atoms into Nb2O5 and systematically elucidate their impact on morphology, local coordination, and light-driven electronic behavior. Advanced microscopy and spectroscopy confirm the formation of isolated Co-O coordination environments without cluster formation. X-ray absorption analysis reveals a partially oxidized Co state with a coordination number of ∼5, closely resembling the Nb local environment. Under illumination, Co incorporation induces a red-shift in optical absorption and significantly suppresses carrier recombination, as evidenced by photoluminescence and transient absorption spectroscopy. Electron paramagnetic resonance and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that Co atoms act as electron acceptor centers, introducing impurity states near the Fermi level that facilitate charge separation and electron localization. These photo-induced electronic shifts generate an electron-rich surface. This work establishes a direct structure–property relationship for single-atom and highlights how atomic-scale dopants can be leveraged to engineer light-driven electronic processes.

title: Uncertainty-aware machine learning framework for predicting dislocation plasticity and stress–strain response in metallic alloys, Part II: BCC systems
abstract: There is increasing interest in using artificial intelligence (AI) to accelerate alloy design. However, most AI models for alloy design remain deterministic and often struggle to reconcile the scatter, sparsity, and incompleteness typical of experimental mechanical-property datasets. Here, we present an uncertainty-aware, physics-informed probabilistic framework to predict dislocation plasticity and full stress–strain response distributions in body-centered cubic (BCC) metals and alloys using limited tensile data available in the literature. We first calibrate the generalized size-dependent Taylor strengthening (GS-DTS) model for BCC systems using Bayesian regression, producing probabilistic estimates of the BCC strengthening coefficients. We then train a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model to learn the dislocation density evolution as a function of strain and key microstructural descriptors, providing both mean predictions and calibrated uncertainty estimates. Embedding this probabilistic dislocation-density model within a representative polycrystalline framework enables the prediction of the stress–strain response as probability bands rather than single deterministic curves. The framework is validated against experimental stress–strain data for Nb, V, Mo, and α-Fe, and is further applied to the refractory high-entropy alloys HfNbTaTiZr and NbTiZr. These results demonstrate transferability beyond the initial training set when dislocation-mediated plasticity dominates. Finally, we separate model uncertainty from input uncertainty and show that solute interaction energies and solute concentrations are dominant contributors to prediction uncertainty. Overall, this approach converts uncertainty into actionable information for experiment planning, model reliability assessment, and mechanism-aware exploration of BCC alloy design space.

title: Data-driven quantification of grain boundary structures and their correlation with migration kinetics
abstract: Understanding the complex relationship between the grain boundary (GB) structure and its migration mechanisms is a critical challenge in materials science owing to the difficulty of determining them from experiments and the immense task required in simulations. To accelerate this determination, we introduce a data-driven Process-Structure-Mechanisms-Properties (PSMP) framework to quantitatively analyze the GB structure during motion and link it to process conditions and kinetic properties. The core of this framework is the GB Structure Transition Function (GBSTF), a low-dimensional structural time-series derived from advanced topological data analysis. We quantify the GB structure using persistent homology (PH) and pair correlation functions (PCF), and then apply principal Component Analysis (PCA) to generate the GBSTF. We applied this framework to approximately 2800 molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of various Aluminum GBs, investigating migration driven by either mechanical stresses (τ) or a jump in chemical potential (φ). Our results demonstrate a strong dependence of GB kinetics on the driving force type. It was found that the GB structure as quantified by GBSTFs correlates with the observed kinetic differences, indicating that the driving force type activates distinct migration mechanisms. This finding was validated by calculating the activation energy (Q) for the Σ25a (017) boundary, which showed significantly different values for φ-driven (Q~0.126 eV) versus τ-driven (Q~0.216 eV) migration. The PSMP framework provides a unified, quantitative method to discriminate between complex GB mechanisms, offering a powerful tool for predicting and controlling microstructure evolution.

title: Si-mediated cluster evolution and asynchronous precipitation behavior in Al-Cu-Mg alloy with moderate Cu/Mg ratio
abstract: Silicon microalloying governs asynchronous precipitation dynamics and age-hardening characteristics in Al-Cu-Mg alloys with a moderate Cu/Mg ratio. Microstructural characterizations reveal that 0.3 wt.% Si fundamentally modifies the precipitation sequence of the Al-4.9Cu-1.6Mg-0.3Si (wt.%) alloy aged at 180 °C, which is delineated as follows: supersaturated solid solution (SSSS) → Mg-rich Cu-Mg-Si co-clusters → Si-modified Guinier-Preston-Bagaryatsky (GPB) zones → S phase + Cu-rich Cu-Mg-Si co-clusters → S phase + σ phase. The asynchronous clustering of Mg and Cu atoms mediated by Si creates favorable conditions for the formation of Mg-rich Cu-Mg-Si and Cu-rich Cu-Mg-Si co-clusters. The initially formed Mg-rich clusters act as effective nucleation sites for Si-modified GPB zones, and subsequently induce the precipitation of S phase. The subsequent Cu-rich clusters serve as precursors for the nucleation of the thermodynamically stable σ phase. This asynchronous precipitation accounts for the accelerated hardening kinetics and unique hardness recovery phenomenon during aging process.

title: Activation of pyramidal slip in α₂ phase of lamellar TiAl alloy under high strain rate loading
abstract: The limited deformability of the α₂ phase is a key factor governing plastic accommodation and mechanical anisotropy in lamellar TiAl alloys, especially at room temperature where the number of readily activated slip systems is restricted. Here, we demonstrate that the γ/α₂ interfacial structure plays a pivotal role in controlling the dislocation activation mechanisms under high strain rate loading. The interface associated with 〈110]γ twinning shows increased lattice mismatch and enhanced local strain energy. The resulting interfacial incompatibility promotes pyramidal 〈2c+a〉 slip in the adjacent α₂ lamellae, carried by 1/3〈112¯6〉-type dislocations and accompanied by antiphase boundary formation. In contrast, α₂ lamellae adjacent to the 〈101]γ twin related interface mainly accommodate deformation by prismatic slip, where the interfacial mismatch remains nearly unchanged. Atomistic simulations further show that 〈110]γ twin propagation modifies the γ/α₂ interface. The associated resolved shear stress on the pyramidal slip system is comparable to the critical stress required for activation. These results suggest that γ phase twinning can favor pyramidal slip in α₂ lamellae by increasing interfacial mismatch and local strain concentration. This finding provides insight into the role of γ/α₂ interfaces in plastic accommodation in lamellar TiAl alloys.

title: Editorial Board
High‑entropy-stabilized amorphous boride for long‑life lithium-sulfur batteries
abstract: Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries are promising next‑generation energy‑storage devices but suffer from the polysulfide shuttle effect and sluggish reaction kinetics. Herein, we design and synthesize an amorphous high‑entropy boride (HEB) via an entropy‑driven “coordination‑etching‑reduction” strategy, and employ it as a multifunctional separator coating. The high configurational entropy effectively stabilizes the amorphous structure and enables the incorporation of multiple active metals (Fe, Co, Cu, Mn, Ru). This unique structure fosters a hierarchical multi‑site synergistic adsorption‑catalysis mechanism: Fe and Ru serve as primary adsorption sites, while Co, Mn, and Cu facilitate charge transfer, collectively enhancing polysulfide confinement and conversion. Consequently, a Li-S battery equipped with a HEB‑coated separator exhibits an exceptional performance: outstanding rate capability (758 mAh g⁻1 at 10 C), good cycling stability (67% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 4 C), and stable operation under high sulfur loading (5.0 mg cm⁻2). This work demonstrates the great potential of entropy‑stabilized amorphous materials as advanced catalytic mediators for practical Li-S batteries.

title: Oxygen effect on deformation mechanism and mechanical behavior of pure Ti at 77K
abstract: Interstitial oxygen is an efficient strengthener in titanium, particularly under cryogenic conditions where exceptional mechanical performance is required. However, the mechanism underpinning this desired phenomenon is not clear. Here we systematically investigate the oxygen mediated evolution of deformation mechanisms of Ti–O alloys at 77 K, and correlate them with the mechanical behaviors. It is found that increasing oxygen content progressively suppresses deformation twinning and dislocation cross-slip. In addition, 〈a〉 slip was suppressed on pyramidal {101¯1} planes and promoted on prismatic {101¯0} planes. The change of deformation mechanisms with increasing oxygen resulted in dramatic increase in strength but also reduction in ductility. An intermediate oxygen content of ∼0.3 wt.% produces an exceptional combination of ultrahigh yield strength (∼1.07 GPa) and retained ductility (>20%), whereas further oxygen addition to 0.5 wt.% results in severe ductility loss and intergranular brittle fracture. It is observed that at ∼0.3 wt.%, multiple prismatic slip systems were activated to enable efficient slip transfer across grain boundaries, mitigating strain localization and preserving ductility. At higher oxygen contents, however, secondary slip activation is inhibited, restricting deformation to single-slip modes and causing severe grain-boundary stress accumulation and premature intergranular fracture. These findings provide a guidance for designing Ti-O alloys for cryogenic applications.

title: Nano-lamellar heterostructures dictate magnetic tunability from ultra-soft to hard states in Fe30Co30Ni30Al5Ti5 alloy
abstract: Achieving broad magnetic tunability within a single alloy, without compromising saturation magnetization (Ms) and mechanical performance, remains a significant challenge. Inherent trade-offs between magnetic and mechanical properties have severely constrained the design of such materials. Here, we achieve synergistic optimization of coercivity, saturation magnetization, and yield strength by introducing a hierarchical heterostructure strategy in Fe30Co30Ni30Al5Ti5 multi-principal element alloy. By systematically varying the aging time, we modulate the evolution of alternating BCC and L12 nano-lamellar structures whose evolution fundamentally governs the magnetic response. These structures induce pronounced nano-lamellar boundary strengthening while, paradoxically, reducing the coercivity by an order of magnitude to an ultra-soft magnetic state (∼0.233 kA m–1), thereby overturning the long-standing paradigm where strengthening phases typically increase coercivity. Extended aging further drives the structural evolution into a highly anisotropic nano-lamellar architecture, enabling a deterministic switch to a robust hard magnetic state (∼21.452 kA m–1) and spanning two orders of magnitude in coercivity. Remarkably, this unprecedented tunability is accompanied by a synergistic enhancement of Ms to 158 Am2 kg–1, effectively mitigating the conventional magnetic dilution effect. The underlying mechanism is attributed to distinct roles of the nano-lamellar BCC FeCo-rich phase, which exhibits an ultra-high Ms (252 Am2 kg–1) and transitions from acting as an exchange-spring softening agent to serving as a potent domain wall pinning network with strong shape anisotropy. This work establishes a “composition-invariant, structure-tailorable” paradigm for multifunctional magnetic materials, offering direct implications for next-generation electromagnetic technologies.

title: Gradient-informed Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for multicomponent CALPHAD model optimization and uncertainty quantification
abstract: CALPHAD model parameter optimization is inherently challenging due to non-smooth objective functions, high-dimensional parameter spaces, and the need for uncertainty quantification (UQ). Traditional weighted nonlinear least squares approaches are computationally efficient but local, whereas black-box global optimizers and ensemble Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods provide broader exploration at substantial computational cost. The objective of this work is to combine the global exploration capability of gradient-informed Hamiltonian Monte Carlo--specifically the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS)--with local deterministic refinement using BFGS to efficiently optimize multicomponent CALPHAD models with minimal manual intervention. Analytic gradients are computed via the Jansson derivative framework. The methodology is demonstrated on the Cr-Fe binary system and extended to the Cr-Fe-Ni ternary system with 32 degrees of freedom. For Cr-Fe, NUTS achieves comparable or superior optimality relative to ensemble MCMC while requiring over an order-of-magnitude fewer likelihood evaluations. Parameter uncertainties are quantified through NUTS sampling and propagated to thermodynamic observables using local expansion, demonstrating a novel modular approach that combines binary and ternary parameter subsets without requiring global relaxation. These results establish gradient-informed exploration as a scalable strategy for multicomponent CALPHAD optimization and provide a practical route toward efficient higher-order database development with quantified uncertainty.

title: Ultra-stable and long-life aluminum storage in (VO)2+ incorporated hexacyanoferrate
abstract: Aqueous aluminum-ion batteries (AAIBs) have garnered notable attention owing to the low cost and exceptionally high theoretical volumetric capacity (8046 mAh cm–3). The advancement is significantly hindered by the scarcity of reliable and efficient cathode materials. Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) are defined by a robust and open framework, which provides sufficient internal space. This unique structure facilitates efficient aluminum-ion insertion and extraction. Thus, PBAs can be established as a highly competitive candidate for aluminum-based battery applications. In addition, the framework of PBAs is also able to accommodate various redox active transition metal cations for charge compensation during multivalent Al3+ ions insertion/extraction. However, due to unstable and irreversible lattice distortions and structural phase transitions, the electrochemical performance of PBAs used for aluminum storage is significantly compromised. In this work, (VO)2+ group was successfully incorporated into the PBA framework via a simple hydrothermal process. Electrochemical characterizations reveal that the (VO)-FePBA delivers an invertible capacity of 109.3 mAh g−1 at 1.0 A g−1. Moreover, it demonstrates exceptional long-term cyclability, retaining 81 % capacity retention ratio after 12,000 cycles at 5.0 A g−1. Structural characterizations indicate that the fluctuation of (VO)-FePBA lattice parameters in the electrochemical process is only 1.9 %. Density function theory (DFT) calculations indicate that the enhanced Al3+-anion interactions in (VO)-FePBA effectively improve the Al storage ability and cycling stability of the host material. The (VO)-FePBA|AlCl3|MoO3 full cell exhibits remarkable electrochemical performances, which delivers a capacity of 76.6 mAh g–1 at 5.0 A g–1 and maintains 83.7 % capacity retention over 3000 cycles, underscoring its exceptional durability. In addition, the full cell is capable of running properly under low operation temperature (-30 °C). This work provides a promising approach to the development of advanced electrode materials for aqueous multivalent ion batteries.

title: Crossover from sluggish to accelerated diffusion in multi-principal element alloys induced by lattice distortion
abstract: Sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion are core factors in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) that are responsible for their unique properties. Nonetheless, the existence and mechanisms of sluggish diffusion remain controversial. In this study, we reveal the intricate interplay between diffusion and lattice distortion using equilibrium Monte Carlo (MC) and kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations driven by a Graph Neural Network (GNN) model that captures local atomic environment-dependent energy states and path-dependent transition rates. Our results demonstrate that lattice distortion significantly elevates equilibrium vacancy concentrations in MPEAs. Integrating insights from vacancy concentration and kMC-derived diffusivity, we identify a crossover in the self-diffusion coefficient of MPEAs as a function of the degree of lattice distortion. Sluggish diffusion is observed in systems with moderate distortion, where increased vacancy concentration, accelerated vacancy jump frequency, and stronger correlation effects compete. Unexpectedly, a higher degree of lattice distortion leads to accelerated instead of sluggish diffusion due to the weak correlation effect. Our findings establish the critical connection between structural features and kinetic properties in MPEAs, offering a foundation for designing high-performance alloys with tailored kinetics by strategically tuning structural characteristics within the vast compositional space.

title: Lamellar kinking mediates exceptional cryogenic strength-ductility synergy in pearlitic steel wires
abstract: Low-temperature brittleness has long been a critical challenge for most body-centered cubic (BCC)-structured metallic alloys, a phenomenon attributed to scarce deformation mechanisms. In this work, exceptional mechanical properties even at liquid-nitrogen temperature are intriguingly exhibited in pearlitic steel wires with lamellar structures of alternating BCC-ferrite and cementite, overcoming both low-temperature brittleness and the strength-ductility trade-off. In-depth microstructure characterizations reveal that lamellar kinking with varied morphological features in as-drawn and annealed wires serves as an essential mediating mechanism during cryogenic deformation. Molecular dynamics simulations indicate that the dominant slip system in ferrite shifts from {112}〈111〉 to {110}〈111〉 as temperature decreases. Nevertheless, the strong 〈110〉 fiber texture severely restricts available slip variants at liquid-nitrogen temperature, causing highly aligned atomic motion and severe shear stress concentration. To accommodate this and sustain slip, slight microstructural rotation is activated and progressively develops into micron-scale lamellar kinking. Notably, the discontinuous lamellar structure not only offers more dislocation slip channels but also undergoes kinking more readily. For kinking to operate, nanoscale cementite lamellae must possess sufficient cryogenic deformability, a prerequisite experimentally confirmed for the first time. Severe non-uniform plastic deformation facilitates rapid accumulation of geometrically necessary dislocations at phase boundaries, inducing pronounced strain gradient strengthening and thereby significantly improving work hardening capacity. Additionally, frequent yet dispersive formation of delaminations along the lamellar direction reduces the driving force for transverse disastrous crack propagation, ensuring a further enhancement of cryogenic ductility. Our findings provide new insights for comprehending cryogenic behavior of pearlitic steel wires and designing advanced metallic wires.

title: Achieving strong interface bonding in CuAl/Fe bimetal laminated composites via tailoring an ordered large-scale interlocking structure
abstract: Tailoring large-scale interlocking structures is one of the most reliable methodologies for enhancing the bonding strength of heterogeneous interface. In this investigation, the continuous solid-liquid bonding method was employed to prepare Cu-7Al/DT4 bimetal laminated composites featuring an interlocking structure interface. Furthermore, the formation mechanism of interfacial intergranular penetrations was also elucidated using microstructure observation, mechanical property tests, thermodynamics, molecular dynamics and density functional theory calculation. It is found that an interlocking structure layer with a thickness of about 20 μm is formed between Cu-7Al and DT4, with a bonding strength exceeding the shear strength of Cu-7Al (about 250 MPa) alone. The type and concentration of solute atoms, and insulation period are proposed to be the key factors influencing the formation of intergranular penetrations. Besides, the formation of the ordered large-scale interlocking structure is primarily attributed to the structural transformation of Fe, surface diffusion, grain boundary/volume diffusion, Marangoni effect and interface/grain boundary migration. Tailoring intergranular penetrations can counteract the barrier of interfacial oxides, enabling a strong bonding of the interface. More importantly, apart from Cu-7Al/DT4, such a type of large-scale intergranular penetrations has also been achieved in Cu-Sn and Cu-Zn systems, strongly indicating that it is indeed a reliable approach for bimetal laminated composites. This investigation provides a streamlined approach for preparing various bimetal laminated composites with a strong interface and develops the foundation for designing novel bimetal laminated composites.

title: Temperature and dose rate effects on dislocation loop formation and decoration in self-ion irradiated high-purity Fe-Cr model alloys
abstract: Body-centered cubic (BCC) Fe-based alloys are promising candidate materials for advanced nuclear reactors. A widespread perception is that the addition of Cr favors the formation of ½ <111> dislocation loops. However, the Cr effects on dislocation loop formation/evolution remain unclear due to the limited experimental studies. In this study, we irradiate ultra-high purity bulk BCC Fe-xCr (x = 3, 5, and 8 wt%) with 6.7-8 MeV Fe ions over a wide range of temperatures (Tirr = 250-500 °C) and dose rates (10⁻⁵ to 10⁻³ dpa/s) to two midrange doses (0.35 and 3.5 dpa). The major irradiation-induced microstructures are loop decoration along non-screw dislocation lines at low temperatures and high dose rates as well as self-assembled loops at elevated temperatures. Post-irradiation Burgers vector analysis via g•b method on loops and electron tomography reveals that <001> preponderance is observable in all irradiated Fe-Cr samples at elevated temperature, resulting from stronger elastic energy originating from <001> edge.

title: Abnormal Tabor factor in ultra-high strain rate indentation testing
abstract: Evaluation of mechanical properties using indentation tests often incorporates a constraint factor, also known as the Tabor factor, which links the hardness and yield strength of the material. It is commonly known to remain nearly constant, with a value around 3 (hardness is three times the uniaxial strength) in conventional testing regimes. Here, by reanalyzing recent impact indentation test data, we present the first evidence of a transition to a significantly higher value of the apparent Tabor factor at strain rates of 106–107 s–1. The impact of an alumina particle on a Cu substrate was simulated through finite element modeling with several plasticity models. Conventional plasticity models produce the expected Tabor factor closer to 3. However, hardening models based on the phonon drag mechanism reproduce the abnormal Tabor factor with values as high as 6 for copper. This effect arises from extremely high rate hardening, which can be produced by mechanisms such as dislocation drag. Such hardening alters the evolution of the plastic strain field and distributes plastic strain over a wider zone, thereby reshaping the crater. The hardness upturn seen in the highest-rate indentation experiments is reflective of a true upturn in strength, in combination with this upturn in apparent Tabor factor as well.

title: Synergistic design of high-performance A2M2O7 NTE materials via Ion Radius and Jahn-Teller effect
abstract: Materials with both a broad temperature range and giant negative thermal expansion (NTE) are highly demanded for advanced engineering applications. The A2M2O7 family, featuring low cost and facile synthesis, holds great potential for such applications, yet scattered research and lack of unified design guidelines have hindered the targeted development of high-performance candidates. Here, a rational design strategy based on the synergy of ion radius tuning and Jahn-Teller (JT) effect regulation is proposed for A2M2O7 NTE materials. Guided by this strategy, β-Cu2V2O7 is identified as an outstanding NTE compound, exhibiting a large volumetric contraction (∼3.34%) over a wide temperature range (110–900 K). Meanwhile, Zn2V2O7 is revisited within this framework and shown to exhibit a pronounced volumetric contraction (∼4.07%), consistent with the proposed design principles. Analysis by structural characterizations and mechanism investigations indicates that (i) the broad NTE temperature window of β-Cu2V2O7 originates from the static-dynamic transition of Cu2+ JT distortions; and (ii) the giant contraction in β-Cu2V2O7 is driven by the cooperative deformation of framework units, with the magnitude positively correlated to the sum of A/M-site ionic radii. The present strategy of ion radius and JT effect synergy can serve as a reliable approach to explore high-performance NTE materials in the A2M2O7 family.

title: Cryogenic micropillar compression of Ti3AlC2, Ti3SiC2 and Cr2AlC: A comparative evaluation of composition-dependent dislocation mobility in MAX Phases
abstract: MAX phases serve as an ideal model system for studying the crossover between metallic and ceramic behavior, and improved ceramic ductility. This ductility is primarily linked to the anomalously easy glide of basal plane dislocations; yet a full theoretical understanding of the characteristics governing their mobility remains a subject of continuing research. Following recent efforts using atomistic simulations of MAX phase basal plane dislocation cores, the present study focused on an experimental evaluation of friction and Peierls stresses in three representative MAX phase compounds, Ti 3 AlC 2 , Ti 3 SiC 2 , and Cr 2 AlC, using micropillar compression at cryogenic temperatures. The study examines specifically the effects of temperature, size, and pristine dislocation morphology under aid of crystal plasticity finite element simulations to derive the lattice resistance for each compound and compare it with previously simulated results. Measured Peierls stresses of 142 MPa (Ti 3 AlC 2 ), 150 MPa (Ti 3 SiC 2 ), and 359 MPa (Cr 2 AlC) confirm a significant role of core structures and bonding characteristics on MAX phase dislocation plasticity, with Ti-based MAX phases exhibiting significantly lower lattice resistance than Cr-based compounds. The cryogenic tests presented here mark the first such experiments in MAX phases and open new pathways for understanding their deformation behavior at low temperatures.

title: Harnessing instability: Intra-grain spinodal engineering unlocks high thermoelectric performance in Mg2(Si,Sn) alloys
abstract: Decoupling thermal and electrical transport through microstructural engineering represents a fundamental challenge in optimizing thermoelectric performance of Mg2(Si,Sn) systems. Here, we exploit the intrinsic miscibility gap in Bi-doped Mg2Si0.3Sn0.7 alloys to create hierarchical spinodal-like nanostructures using high-pressure synthesis combined with spark plasma sintering. Microstructure characterization revealed a coherent intra-grain network comprising Si-rich vein-like nanogrids and nano-domains embedded with smaller subdomains, with characteristic length scales ranging from several to tens of nanometers. Transport properties analyses show these coherent structures provide substantial phonon scattering while preserving carrier mobility, successfully decoupling heat and charge transports. The resulting synergy between enhanced power factor and reduced thermal conductivity yields excellent thermoelectric performance: a peak zT of 1.63 at 713 K and a high average zT of 1.13 over 300–823 K. This work demonstrates controlled spinodal-like decomposition as a powerful design strategy for high-performance thermoelectrics, transforming thermodynamic instabilities into beneficial nanostructuring tools with broad applicability to other limited solid solution systems.

title: Raman-informed reverse Monte Carlo for disordered materials: Case studies in borate-based glasses
abstract: The structural freedom of disordered materials limits the ability of diffraction-only reverse Monte Carlo (RMC) to uniquely recover key motifs such as three-membered rings. We present Raman-informed RMC (RiRMC), which incorporates experimentally measured Raman spectra as direct structural constraints in addition to diffraction. Spectra are reconstructed on the fly using a database of atom-resolved contributions for predefined motifs derived from density functional theory (DFT) calculations, eliminating the need for costly on-the-fly ab initio calculations and guiding the refinement toward spectroscopically consistent microstructures. Applied to vitreous B2O3 and lithium borate, RiRMC consistently yields abundant three-membered rings, captures the characteristic sharp band near 800 cm−1, and simultaneously reproduces neutron diffraction S(q), thus addressing motifs that conventional RMC and melt–quench MD underproduce. For larger models, constrained MD initialization with Raman-guided motifs speeds convergence and produces ring populations that agree reasonably with experimental inferences while maintaining S(q) consistency. Remaining challenges include DFT underestimation of intensities for non-boroxol rings in alkali-rich glasses and the need for more efficient Monte Carlo sampling; experimentally decomposed spectra and enhanced sampling methods might mitigate these issues in practice. Overall, RiRMC offers a scalable, spectroscopy-driven framework for quantitative microstructural modeling of glasses. It is readily adaptable to other disordered materials and characterization approaches, enabling atomistic simulations anchored to experimental data.

title: GND density in an additively manufactured CoNi superalloy: A 3D EBSD perspective
abstract: Investigating dislocation evolution during the complex thermal cycling inherent to additive manufacturing (AM) remains a challenge. In this study, we address this by integrating TriBeam-based three-dimensional (3D) orientation mapping with thermomechanically coupled crystal plasticity finite element (CPFE) simulations to study solid-state thermal cycling in an additively manufactured CoNi-based superalloy. The modeling framework incorporates experimentally measured temperature-dependent elasticity, thermal conductivity, and expansion, enabling microstructure-resolved predictions under realistic thermal gradients during thermal cycling. A direct comparison between 2D and 3D geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density estimates reveals a mean voxel-level relative difference of 25%, quantifying the contribution of out-of-plane curvature captured by the 3D analysis. Experimentally, GND accumulation scales inversely with grain size and remains insensitive to crystallographic orientation. Simulations predict residual stresses along the build direction that arise from thermal cycling and show a clear correlation with both the GND density distribution and the maximum temperature reached during the cycle. Regions with high initial misorientation induced by the printing process align with zones of elevated GND density accumulation in simulation, highlighting the influence of initial orientation distribution imposed from the as-solidified microstructure on dislocation evolution. Finally, the results show that the simulated solid state thermal cycle (SSTC) produces a measurable GND contribution, while the remaining GND density is associated with orientation gradients already present in the as-built microstructure. These findings underscore the value of 3D orientation data and using temperature dependent thermophysical parameters in resolving micromechanical fields in additively manufactured microstructures.

title: Strengthening Ni-rich NiTi alloys against dislocation slip in martensite by introducing local chemical heterogeneity via low temperature aging
abstract: It is well known that NiTi shape memory alloys need to be strengthened to display stable stress-strain-temperature responses in cyclic thermomechanical loads. Strengthening by final cold work/heat treatment at 773 K for 10 minutes commonly used in industry gives rise to superelastic NiTi wires and sheets with nanocrystalline microstructure that display recoverable stress-strain-temperature responses with acceptable functional fatigue but limited structural fatigue (N f = ∼5000) and ductility (∼12%). The limited ductility often results in wire fractures due to accidental overloading, which is a serious problem for engineering applications. Plastic deformability of NiTi wires at high stresses thus becomes of concern besides functional thermomechanical properties. Moreover, strengthening via cold work/heat treatment cannot be applied to bulk NiTi components, thin films and/or additively manufactured NiTi components. Therefore, various alternative ways of strengthening NiTi based alloys have been recently explored in the SMA field. In this work, we show that cyclic superelastic performance of coarse grain superelastic NiTi wires can be significantly improved and yield stress for plastic deformation can be increased while assuring high strength (∼1 GPa) and large ductility (∼80%) by low temperature aging at 523 K for times optimized based on the results of Monte Carlo simulation of Ni diffusion. It is claimed that the local chemical inhomogeneity introduced by aging into the alloy microstructure increases critical stress for [100](001) dislocation slip in martensite which stabilizes cyclic superelasticity, widens superelastic window by increasing yield stress for plastic deformation and improves plastic deformability of NiTi at high stresses. This strategy opens a new pathway for designing coarse grained NiTi alloys with improved functional fatigue performance, high strength, and excellent plastic deformability.

title: Synergistic d-p regulation on Fe-Sb dual-atom catalysts enables high-performance oxygen reduction and wide-temperature Zn-air batteries
abstract: Dual-atom catalysts (DACs) surpass the limitations of single-atom catalysts by harnessing synergy between adjacent metal sites. Herein, we propose a novel strategy employing d-p orbital synergistic modulation in Fe-Sb DACs. Combined density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the significant d-p orbital synergistic regulation between Fe and Sb sites promotes O2 adsorption and activation, lowers the energy barrier for OO bond cleavage, and optimizes water desorption. As a proof-of-concept, Fe/Sb DACs anchored on a nitrogen-doped carbon matrix (Fe/Sb-N-C) were synthesized. The atomic-level local coordination of Fe-Sb dual atoms was systematically characterized by aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) analyses. The as-fabricated Fe/Sb-N-C exhibits exceptional alkaline oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance, featuring a half-wave potential of 0.92 V and outstanding durability. Aqueous Zn-air batteries equipped with Fe/Sb-N-C achieve a high maximum power density of 196 mW cm-2 and a specific capacity of 795 mAh g-1. Furthermore, quasi-solid-state Zn-air batteries demonstrate wide-temperature operability (-30 to 60 °C) and stability under high current densities. This work establishes d-p orbital synergy as a new paradigm for designing high-efficiency ORR catalysts, broadening their application in energy devices across extreme temperatures.

title: Boosting power factor via self-exsolved metallic nanonetworks in SrTiO3-based thermoelectric thin films
abstract: Perovskite oxide SrTiO3 is promising for thermoelectrics due to its high intrinsic Seebeck coefficient and stability, but its overall power factor still needs further improvement. Compositing with metallic phases can enhance conductivity, yet precise nanoscale control remains a challenge. Here, we employ exsolution to self-assemble metallic nanonetworks within La-doped SrTiO3 (La:SrTiO3) epitaxial thin films on LSAT (001) substrates. By controlling exsolution conditions to tune nanoparticle size and density, we achieve a dense, uniformly distributed nanonetwork with strong interfacial bonding, significantly enhancing electrical conductivity. This yields a superior power factor, with a peak PFmax of ∼1352 μW m−1 K−2 at 528 K and a high average PFave of ∼1106 μW m−1 K−2 from room temperature to 886 K. These values are highly competitive within state-of-the-art n-type oxide thermoelectrics. This work establishes exsolution as a powerful pathway for nano-composite engineering in perovskite oxides, offering guidance for the design of high-performance thermoelectric single-crystal thin films.

title: The effect of ultra-dilute boron addition on solidification behavior and toughness of a laser powder bed fused eutectic high-entropy alloy
abstract: Maintaining structural integrity and damage tolerance remains a critical challenge in the additive manufacturing of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs), where residual-stress-driven distortion and microstructural brittleness can limit robust fabrication and mechanical reliability. Here, we show that ultra-dilute boron addition provides a significant effect on tuning the solidification pathway of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 during laser powder bed fusion. Guided by thermodynamic calculations, boron is identified as a solute rejected by both eutectic phases, which expands the solidification interval (ΔT) and promotes elemental diffusion during rapid solidification. These effects stabilize cellular–lamellar heterostructures, suppress microstructural embrittlement, and alleviate residual stress accumulation. As a result, the engineered microstructure achieves a yield strength of ∼1342 MPa and a fracture toughness (KIC) of ∼74.4 MPa·√m, surpassing those of reported eutectic alloys. This work demonstrates a ΔT-guided minor-alloying strategy, showing that ppm-level compositional tuning can generate disproportionate improvements in the toughness and structural robustness of an additively manufactured EHEA.

title: Mechanistic origins of low‑hydrogen embrittlement in titanium: Synergistic multiphase hydrides and thermal stresses enabling efficient powder production
abstract: The hydrogenation-dehydrogenation (HDH) process is a cornerstone for the cost-effective production of high-quality titanium powder, yet its efficiency is traditionally constrained by the conventional assumption that effective embrittlement requires full conversion to stoichiometric δ-TiH2. This conventional route is inherently energy-intensive and time-consuming because it relies on high hydrogen uptake. Here, we propose a shift to stress-dominated embrittlement mechanism enabled by targeted multiphase microstructure design. Under low-pressure (≤0.1 MPa) and short hydrogenation durations (<60 min), a unique three-phase architecture comprising α-Ti, a metastable body-centered tetragonal (BCT) hydride, and face-centered cubic (FCC) δ hydride was engineered. We demonstrate that the pronounced thermophysical mismatch among these coexisting phases generates substantial internal stress gradients, these stresses become the primary driving force for crack initiation and fast propagation, enabling efficient fragmentation at hydrogen concentrations far below those required for full δ-hydride saturation. Compared with traditional protocols, this strategy reduces total hydrogen consumption by ∼50% and shortens processing time by >80%. This work provides an energy- and time-efficient route to titanium powder, and establishes a microstructure design framework for controlling hydride-induced failure in hexagonal close-packed (HCP) metals through phase-interaction-mediated stress engineering.

title: Stop-and-go dislocation dynamics in semiconductor heterostructures revealed by in-situ X-ray imaging
abstract: Understanding how the real-time motion of individual dislocations collectively produces macroscopic plastic deformation in strained crystalline materials remains a central open problem. Here, dislocation propagation in epitaxial heterostructures is tracked using in-situ dark-field X-ray diffraction microscopy in a grazing-incidence geometry, providing ∼100 nm spatial resolution over a ∼200 × 200 μm² field of view with second-scale temporal resolution. Rather than gliding continuously, dislocations advance through intermittent, stop-and-go bursts with a broad distribution of stopping times and a progressive loss of activity at fixed temperature. Statistical analysis of hundreds of propagation events enables a stochastic jump-process model in which dislocation segments either become immobile or traverse a heterogeneous sequence of energy barriers arising from glide-induced changes in the dislocation core. The model explains the observed decay of activity as a rare-event–driven form of temporal hardening intrinsic to dislocation motion. This work establishes a general framework for analyzing real-time plasticity in materials with complex dislocation kinetics.

title: Gradient phase selection between (Ti,Nb)5Si3 and (Ti,Nb)3Si phases within rapidly solidified Ti-Nb-Si alloy
abstract: The phase selection and microstructure evolution of rapidly solidified Ti70Nb14Si16 alloy varying with cooling rate and undercooling were systematically investigated through arc-melting (AM), electromagnetic levitation (EML), electromagnetic levitation coupled with fall casting (EML-FC) and electromagnetic levitation coupled with die casting (EML-DC) techniques. In-situ temperature monitoring and finite element simulations were employed to analyze the heat transfer characteristics and quantify the undercooling, cooling rate and temperature gradient during solidification. In the near-equilibrium solidification process, the liquid-solid phase transformation sequence of the alloy was identified as L → (Ti,Nb)5Si3 → (Ti,Nb)5Si3 + (βTi). Under EML conditions, the alloy’s average cooling rate was below 20 K/s, and the solidification pathway was mainly controlled by undercooling. As the undercooling exceeded 210 K, the solidification pathway shifted from L → (Ti,Nb)5Si3 → (Ti,Nb)5Si3 + (βTi) to L → (Ti,Nb)5Si3 + (βTi). By contrast, the average cooling rate of the alloy exceeded 102 K/s under AM, EML-FC and EML-DC conditions. The metastable (Ti,Nb)3Si phase became the dominant phase, which was attributed to insufficient Si element diffusion and inadequate incubation time for nucleation of the (Ti,Nb)5Si3 phase. With the synergistic impact of the high cooling rate (105∼106 K/s), the extreme temperature gradient (106∼107 K/m) and the remarkable solute trapping effect, the nucleation competition between the (Ti,Nb)5Si3 and (Ti,Nb)3Si phases further intensified, leading to a transition from a two-layer eutectic to a three-layer eutectic with gradient phase and size distribution.

title: Unlocking a twofold yield strength increase in metastable Ti-10Mo alloy through cooling-rate-controlled ω precipitation and β grain refinement
abstract: Metastable β titanium alloys with high strain-hardening rate and ductility earn great potential development, thanks to the activations of both transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) and twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) during deformation. But the low yield strength puts the structural applications of metastable β titanium alloys into dilemma. Here, we report a facile route to substantially raise the yield strength of metastable β titanium alloys, simply by decreasing the cooling rate after β-annealing, i.e., from water quenching (WQ) to air cooling (AC). In a model Ti-10.0 wt.% Mo alloy, the yield strength of both coarse (D = 240 μm) and fine (D = 8 μm) grained microstructures was doubled following this route. Through systematic characterizations of the deformation microstructures, it is revealed that the significant enhancement in yield strength of air-cooled Ti-10 wt.% Mo alloy arises from the promoted ω precipitation and associated elemental partitioning. The dominant deformation mode changes from strain-induced α″ martensitic transformation alone to multiple mechanisms, including strain-induced α″ martensitic transformation and {332}<113> deformation twinning with decreasing cooling rate. Fine-grained Ti-10Mo alloy after air cooling exhibits an unprecedented ultrahigh yield strength of ∼ 1.4 GPa but suffers from a dramatic decrease in ductility due to the combined effects of planar slip localization and GB α precipitates that in turn cause premature intergranular fracture. In contrast, coarse-grained Ti-10Mo alloy, in which GB α precipitates and strong elemental partitioning (between ω and β matrix) are effectively suppressed, early intergranular fracture is prevented, thus enabling a better balance between yield strength (955 MPa) and uniform elongation (19.1%). This work offers a simple and efficient strategy for advancing the development of high-performance metastable β titanium alloys.

title: Simultaneous improvement of strength and corrosion resistance in β-type Ti-24Nb-4Zr-8Sn alloy through a spinodally modulated dual-phase microstructure
