The results are analyzed accounting for the chemical complexity of the contributing phases and discussed with respect to the ”sluggish” diffusion concept proposed originally for high entropy alloys.

title: Solid-state grain-boundary defect-phase formation in the Fe–Zn system
abstract: Liquid metal embrittlement (LME) of next generation galvanized steels has recently been shown to involve intermetallic phase formation at preferably high-angle grain-boundaries (HAGB) prior to microcracking. These GB phases emerge already at temperatures much below the melting point of Zn and point towards the importance of solid-state GB mechanisms. To better isolate such early GB phase formation, we pursue here in-situ heating inside a transmission electron microscope on a HAGB of a Fe-Zn solid solution model system. Clear Zn segregation in the HAGB is seen, followed by the formation of an L1 0 FeZn GB phase. Being not part of the equilibrium phase diagram, this phase is considered as a defect phase. Complementing density functional theory calculations demonstrate how the unexpected phase can be energetically favored inside a GB. In concert with bulk synchrotron diffraction data, we propose that this defect phase is an intermediate state towards the higher Zn-containing Fe 3 Zn 10 phase that otherwise is dominating revealed GB intermetallics during the early stages of LME in galvanized steels.

title: A framework for structure–energy mapping of compact nanovoid–solute complexes: Tungsten alloys as model systems
abstract: Understanding nanovoid–solute structures and energetics is essential for elucidating coupled defect evolution in metals, but their vast configurational space challenges conventional approaches. Using W–Re as a representative system, we demonstrate that the incremental binding energy of solute incorporation at nanovoid surfaces can be decomposed into direct nanovoid–solute and nanovoid-mediated solute–solute contributions. Both are governed primarily by short-range local coordination motifs, with identical motifs giving nearly identical energetics. Based on first-principles data, gradient boosting decision tree analysis identified the dominant local descriptors, and a DFT-derived local-motif library enabled the energetics of compact nanovoid–solute complexes within this domain to be reconstructed from constituent motifs. We further developed a size-dependent configurational-search framework to identify low-energy solute arrangements on compact nanovoid surfaces. This framework enabled construction of a large database, revealed the staircase-like evolution of Re incremental binding energies, and yielded a simple criterion based on Re surface coverage for rapid energy prediction across a wide size range. It also establishes a thermodynamic link between Re segregation and vacancy attachment energetics and provides benchmarks for existing models and empirical potentials. Extensions to W–Os, W–Ta, and Mo–Re support the methodological transferability of the local-motif concept, and the predicted solute-segregation trends are qualitatively consistent with available experimental observations. This work establishes a physically transparent, accurate, and scalable framework for studying thermodynamic coupling between nanovoids and solutes in metals and provides DFT-based energetic inputs for multiscale simulations.

title: Gradient amorphous interphases toughen ultrastrong nanolayered metals by regulating dislocation storage and mobility
abstract: Achieving high toughness in ultrastrong metals remains a longstanding challenge, as extreme strength is typically accompanied by strain localization and premature fracture. Here we introduce gradient amorphous interphases as an interface-level design strategy to mitigate this trade-off in nanolayered metals. By embedding a controlled compositional gradient within nanoscale amorphous interphases, we create interfaces that regulate dislocation storage and mobility, thereby suppressing dislocation accumulation and strain localization. Using Cu/Nb nanolayered composites as a model system, we show that gradient amorphous interphases enable homogeneous deformation strains of ∼32% while maintaining a strength of ∼2 GPa, substantially outperforming counterparts with crystalline interfaces or homogeneous amorphous interlayers. In situ transmission electron microscopy, atomistic simulations, and theoretical analysis reveal that these graded interphases act as efficient dislocation sinks and promote sustained dislocation mobility, while also deflecting cracks and promoting distributed nanoscale damage. Together, these mechanisms enable stable plastic flow and enhanced fracture resistance at ultrahigh strength. Our results demonstrate that tailoring compositional gradients within amorphous interphases provides an effective route to improving the strength–toughness balance in nanolayered metals and suggests a potentially transferable interface-design strategy for damage-tolerant structural materials.

title: Fault architecture-controlled γ↔ε transformation and reversion under strain-controlled fatigue in a metastable high-entropy alloy
abstract: Fatigue failure remains the dominant mode of structural degradation; yet the mechanistic coupling between cyclic loading, microstructural fault topology, and deformation reversibility in metastable high-entropy alloys (MHEAs) remains poorly understood. Owing to their low stacking-fault energy (SFE) and marginal γ–ε free-energy difference, MHEAs exhibit deformation pathways, including partial-dislocation glide, stacking fault evolution, and γ↔ε martensitic transformation, that differ fundamentally from conventional alloys. Yet, the interplay between endurance strength, amplitude-dependent cyclic plasticity, and reversible martensitic transformation has not been established. Here, we present a novel integrated mechanical–microstructural framework by combining stress-controlled endurance-limit quantification with strain-controlled low-cycle fatigue (±0.1–0.6%), and multi-scale characterization (EBSD, synchrotron XRD, TEM, APT). A maximum-likelihood random endurance-limit model defines the cyclic stability threshold, while strain-controlled tests reveal pronounced amplitude-dependent cyclic plasticity, non-Masing behavior, and a bilinear Coffin–Manson response marking a transition from transformation-assisted to reversion-assisted fatigue. Microstructurally, γ→ε transformation initiates at ±0.1% under nominally elastic conditions, enabled by pre-existing stacking-fault tetrahedra. At ±0.4%, ε formation reaches a maximum, where dense Shockley-partial networks, interacting fault assemblies, and mixed planar–wavy slip produce peak back-stress hardening and maximum plastic strain accumulation. Upon increasing the strain amplitude to ±0.6%, partial ε→γ reversion occurs via reverse partial glide and fault annihilation, facilitated by three-dimensional stacking-fault parallelepipeds that impede glide while promoting structural reordering, providing the first integrated experimental evidence of room-temperature reversible γ↔ε transformation under strain-controlled cyclic loading in an HEA. This work establishes a unified, physics-based framework linking cyclic mechanics to fault topology and identifies metastability and fault architecture as key design variables for fatigue-resistant alloys.

title: Enhanced cryogenic strength–ductility synergy via Mn-tuned ε-martensite topology control in Ni–Co–Cr–Mo multi-principal element alloys
abstract: In some low-stacking fault energy face-centered cubic (FCC, γ) multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs), excessive transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) can reduce ductility or even cause premature fracture. To address this, we tuned Mn to regulate the formation, morphology, connectivity, and subsequent evolution of hexagonal close-packed (HCP, ε) martensite, thereby suppressing the development of large, stress-concentrating HCP domains. Using (Ni28.2Co56.4Cr9.4Mo6)100-xMnx (x = 0–20 at.%) alloys deformed at 77 K, we show that increasing Mn stabilizes FCC and enables a controllable TRIP-to-twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) transition. In low-Mn alloys, coarse and connected ε-lamellar regions are associated with stronger strain localization and premature tensile failure. At x = 5 at.%, ε forms thin, discontinuous platelets within dense twin/stacking-fault networks, while strain-resolved diffraction and microscopy reveal late-stage saturation of retained ε together with enhanced twin development. These observations are consistent with transformation-mediated reconfiguration of ε-containing/faulted regions and are accompanied by reduced strain localization. This enables tensile deformation to an elongation of ∼107% while maintaining an ultimate tensile strength of ∼1.21 GPa at 77 K. These results identify Mn-tuned control of ε-martensite morphology and connectivity as a promising strategy for balancing transformation-assisted hardening and strain accommodation in cryogenic FCC MPEAs.

title: Cr substitution in NASICON cathodes unlocks V4+/V5+ redox and intermediate-phase evolution for high-energy and stable sodium storage
abstract: Large-scale renewable energy deployment calls for sodium-ion batteries with high energy density and long cycling stability. NASICON-type Na3V2(PO4)3 is a promising cathode, but its practical performance is limited by the inaccessible high-valence V4+/V5+ redox and abrupt structural evolution. Herein, we report a Cr-substituted Na3V1.5Cr0.5(PO4)3 (NVCP) cathode that activates reversible V3+/V4+/V5+ multielectron redox and intermediate-phase-mediated lattice strain regulation. Theoretical calculations reveal that Cr modulates the local electronic structure, reduces Na+ migration barriers, and facilitates structural rearrangement. More importantly, in situ X-ray diffraction reveals that Cr substitution regulates the phase-evolution pathway by inducing reversible intermediate phases. These intermediate phases split the large lattice change into mild stepwise adjustments, effectively buffering structural strain. Benefiting from these synergies, the optimized NVCP cathode shows excellent cycling stability, retaining 91.1% capacity after 300 cycles at 0.5 C and 95% after 1000 cycles at 10 C. The full cells assembled with hard carbon anodes deliver an average discharge voltage of ∼3.4 V and an energy density of ∼230 Wh kg−1 based on the total mass of active materials. This work demonstrates that Cr substitution promotes high-voltage vanadium redox and intermediate-phase regulation, offering an effective strategy for designing high-energy Na storage cathodes.

title: Formation mechanisms of meso-scale element segregation in multi-material metal additive manufacturing
abstract: Meso-scale element segregation (MES) critically affects the property and reliability of multi-material metal additive manufacturing (AM) parts, yet its formation principles remain insufficiently understood. In this work, we reveal the formation process of MES through high-fidelity multi-physics simulations combined with in-situ and ex-situ experiments. We find that the fundamental modes of MES can be classified into stratified segregation and vortex segregation, according to the meso-scale fluid transport behaviors near the solidification front. In stratified segregation, melts with different compositions tend to separate and solidify at different positions of solidification front. In vortex segregation, however, composition-distinct melts can solidify at the same position with comparable probability. We further show that the formation process of MES can exhibit strong instability, which results in spatially inconsistent MES in the printed part. The instability mainly originates from the intrinsic chemical inhomogeneity in the feedstocks and is further amplified by the alloying reaction in the melting process. Guided by the mechanistic insights, we propose several strategies to regulate MES in AM process. This work establishes a physical foundation for the precise composition engineering in multi-material AM.

title: Grain boundary-stress fundamental zones: A systematic exploration of orientation-dependent material response
abstract: The description of the symmetries inherent to grain boundaries has made it possible to probe the vast orientation space linked to these interfaces. However, under any given stress state, exploring the space of distinct configurations (with a total of 8 degrees of freedom) remains impractical. Taking advantage of the grain boundary and stress tensor symmetries, the current work shows that for every bicrystal there exists a fundamental zone that uniquely captures all possible stress orientations. These regions are systematically derived for axisymmetric and triaxial stresses in S2 and SO(3) spaces, respectively. Computational tools for cubic materials with Oh point group symmetry are also provided to facilitate the adoption of grain boundary-stress fundamental zones. Among other advantages, this approach provides a significant reduction in the size of the orientation domain, enhanced visualization of orientation-dependent material performance, and statistical analyses of mechanical response via weighted distributions over the entire configuration space. Together with an elastic bicrystal stress incompatibility model, a series of case studies reveals insights into the role of elastic anisotropy on damage distribution, invalidates prior assumptions related to the origins of slip localization near Σ3 coherent twin boundaries, and showcases a new way to optimize the orientation of textured materials with respect to a remote stress. All of this represents an important step towards the systematic identification and exploration of critical grain boundary configurations for arbitrary materials and stress states.

title: Atomic-flux tunable exchange-spring magnetism in SmFe12/Fe nanocomposites
abstract: SmFe12-based compounds with the ThMn12 structure offer a promising alternative to state-of-the-art Nd2Fe14B permanent magnets due to their high saturation magnetization and magnetocrystalline anisotropy. However, achieving high coercivity while maintaining high magnetization remains challenging. Here, we use atomic-scale flux engineering via molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) to fabricate SmFe12/Fe nanocomposites with tunable magnetic properties. Precise control of the Sm/Fe flux yields either Sm-rich intergranular phases that magnetically decouple grains, inducing high coercivity, or Fe-rich interfacial layers that promote exchange-spring-like coupling with high magnetization and preserved coercivity. Density functional theory (DFT) and experimental studies reveal interfacial electronic reconstruction that stabilizes perpendicular magnetocrystalline anisotropy across the interface, underpinning the emergent exchange-spring magnetism. These findings establish flux-engineered MBE as a viable route for tailoring interfacial magnetic interactions and designing high-energy-product permanent magnets utilizing the exchange-spring mechanism.

title: A dual-precipitation strategy for tailoring the strengths of ferrite and martensite in dual-phase steels
abstract: Conventional strengthening strategies for ferrite–martensite dual-phase (DP) steels generally focus on strengthening individual constituent phases, often increasing the strength mismatch between ferrite and martensite and thereby limiting mechanical performance. Here, we propose a dual-precipitation strategy that enables simultaneous precipitation strengthening of both ferrite and martensite through controlled phase transformation followed by tempering. This approach introduces two distinct precipitate populations: interphase precipitates in ferrite and tempering-induced precipitates in martensite. Precipitation behaviour in Ti microalloyed steels, with and without Mo addition, was systematically investigated across varying ferrite–martensite fractions using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), small-angle neutron scattering (SANS), and atom probe tomography (APT). Increasing ferrite fraction progressively reduces precipitation sensitivity during tempering, producing coarser precipitates with lower number density. Mo addition primarily promotes early-stage precipitate nucleation rather than substantially enhancing coarsening resistance, resulting in higher precipitate densities and enhanced strengthening. Precipitate chemistry exhibits pronounced size dependence, with smaller precipitates being increasingly metal-rich, while Mo promotes carbon vacancy incorporation within B1-type precipitates. Strengthening estimation indicates that even ultrafine precipitates strengthen the material predominantly through the Orowan bypassing mechanism. These findings demonstrate that dual-precipitation strategy provides a new microstructural design strategy for tailoring phase-specific strengthening and strength mismatch, offering opportunities to optimise the balance between strength and formability in advanced DP steels.

title: Contribution of chemically disordered second phases and coherent interfaces to the biased defect flow at the early stage of irradiation in steels
abstract: High-density, coherent nanoprecipitate-strengthened alloys have recently attracted considerable interest for fusion energy applications because of their excellent mechanical properties and promising radiation resistance. However, the roles of second phase nanoprecipitates and coherent interfaces in the early-stage evolution of irradiation-induced defects remain poorly understood. In this work, first-principles calculations and molecular dynamic simulations were employed to investigate a representative alloy consisting of a BCC maraging steel matrix and second phase in the form of coherent B2-Ni(Fe,Al) nanoprecipitates. The formation energies and migration behavior of vacancies and [110] dumbbells were analyzed to elucidate defect evolution. The results show that point defects preferentially accumulate in the second phase rather than in the BCC matrix, and the coherent interface between matrix and second phase promotes biased defect migration from the matrix toward the nanoprecipitates. Vacancies and interstitials can locally recombine within the second phase at low defect concentrations. However, under sustained irradiation, B2 nanoprecipitates undergo ballistic dissolution, suggesting that the precipitates act as sacrificial defect reservoirs during the early stages of irradiation. These processes effectively reduce defect accumulation in the BCC matrix and contribute to swelling resistance. Our work provides atomistic insights into the roles of second phase nanoprecipitates and coherent interfaces in defect evolution and offers guidance for the design of irradiation-tolerant alloys.

title: Predicting glass-forming ability in binary alloys by machine learning
abstract: Predicting metallic glass-forming ability (GFA) through machine learning has been challenging. Among the reasons for the challenge are limited, biased and inconsistent experimental data, binary vs continuous labeling, and limited feature representation particularly for multicomponent alloys. To address these challenges, we restrict the problem to binary alloys and base the training data on experiments spanning a representative fraction of ∼ 20% of binary alloys, which have been synthesized through sputtering and its atomic structure characterized. Consistent in quality and sufficient quantity of binary sputtering data with continuously labeled GFA quantified in the critical cooling rates (Rc) are constructed, and Physically Informed features based on atomic size, crystal mismatch, Miedema-based mixing enthalpy, and melting temperature are employed to describe the alloy in terms of its Rc. Using the Physically Informed features, the random forest model predicts the critical cooling rate with a mean absolute percentage error of ∼18% (MAPE in log₁₀ (Rc) space), compared to a simple benchmark model reaching a MAPE of 28%. However, attempts to use this binary model to predict Rc in ternary alloys are ineffective; using the ML model trained on binary data to predict Rc in ternary alloys results in a MAPE of ∼36% for sputtered ternary alloys and ∼ 89% for ternary BMG formers. Such poor performance suggests that the mixing complexity in ternary alloys is not captured in binary alloys. Overall, we argue that while addressing previous challenges in predicting GFA through ML, the models achieve statistically improved predictive performance while retaining a physically interpretable feature set. However, the achieved predictions remain coarse, indicating additional limitations (e.g., label uncertainty, missing higher-order mixing descriptors, process dependence, etc.) that constrain precise Rc prediction. Most fundamentally, the discreteness of atoms remains the limiting factor from using ML strategies to precisely predict glass-forming ability of alloys.

title: Microbiologically influenced corrosion of metallic materials: Microstructure, coupled degradation mechanisms, and protection
abstract: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) has conventionally been interpreted through microbial species, biofilm formation, extracellular electron transfer, and metabolite-driven chemistry. Recent significant advances in the fields of microbiology, electrochemistry, and interfacial characterization have enhanced understanding on the mechanisms of microorganism’s role in altering anodic dissolution, cathodic reactions, passive films, corrosion products, and local chemistry. However, the roles of alloy chemistry, microstructure, passive films, defects, and hydrogen transport govern the initiation, localization, and subsequent evolution of MIC remain insufficiently understood – an important aspect for engineering equipment, where localized corrosion, residual stress, cyclic loading, and hydrogen uptake act simultaneously and may drive the transition from surface attack to cracking. Keeping this in view, current understanding of the MIC mechanisms, with emphasis on the evolution of the biofilm–metal interphase, localized electrochemical gradients, microbial corrosion reactions, and electron transfer are summarized in this overview, with emphasis on mechanistic evidence. MIC across major metallic material classes are compared, which shows that alloy chemistry, phase constitution, inclusions, precipitates, grain boundaries, passive-film’s stability, weld heterogeneity, and corrosion-product structure determine where the MIC-induced damage initiates, whether it remains localized, and how hydrogen is transported and trapped. Microbiologically assisted cracking is summarized next, by linking biofilm-induced pitting with stress concentration, anodic dissolution, hydrogen entry, fatigue, stress corrosion cracking, and crack propagation. Recent advances in localized electrochemistry, cross-sectional microscopy, chemical imaging, isotopic tracing, and correlative characterization are then assessed, together with materials-oriented mitigation strategies based on antibacterial alloying, microstructure regulation, surface treatment, and functional coatings.

title: Nano-scale Portevin – Le Chatelier effect in Al-Mg alloys
abstract: Serrated deformation behavior in Al-Mg alloys, commonly associated with the Portevin-Le Châtelier (PLC) effect at macroscopic scales, originates from dynamic strain aging (DSA) at microscopic scales. However, the underlying nanoscale mechanisms bridging this gap between macroscopic and microscopic scales remain unclear. In this study, indentation experiments combined with transmission electron microscopy were employed to directly correlate deformation behavior with solute-dislocation interactions in Al-Mg alloys. Low-angle tilt grain boundaries (LAtGBs) were formed beneath indent edges, where the tensile strain fields around edge-dislocations were decorated with Mg. Screw dislocation networks were confirmed between leading and trailing LAtGBs, and the misorientation of LAtGBs evolved through the incorporation of these screw dislocations. The present results demonstrate that serrated deformation in Al-Mg alloys arises from the intermittent migration of LAtGBs coupled with collective dislocation transport by screw dislocation networks, providing a nanoscale mechanism linking solute-dislocation interactions to macroscopic plastic instability.

title: Dislocation-mediated continuous precipitation in Mo-bearing martensitic steel: from solute co-segregation and coherent precursors to α-M2C carbides
abstract: The precipitation of M 2 C in Mo-bearing martensitic steels during tempering has often been described as a classical M 3 C → M 2 C transformation, despite the crystallographic and compositional incompatibilities this path entails with respect to the martensitic matrix. Here, by combining high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), three-dimensional atom probe tomography (3D-APT), and first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we reveal a dislocation-mediated sequence during tempering at 700°C: solute co-segregation at screw dislocations, formation of Mo-rich coherent precursors, development of a 5R intermediate phase with AABBB/ABCAB stacking, and formation of orthorhombic α-M 2 C. DFT explains that C segregates first to screw dislocation cores and subsequently attracts Mo via strong C–Mo chemical binding (∼0.6 eV), leading to cooperative C-assisted Mo segregation. The resulting coherent precursors (∼40 at.% Mo) provide a BCC-derived framework for stacking reconstruction: continued C insertion drives local planes toward close-packed geometry, enabling nucleation of a local BBB close-packed embryo at the coherent precursor/matrix interface and growth into an AABBB 5R structure; further C enrichment promotes basal partial-dislocation glide, converting AABBB to a faulted ABCAB variant. As the composition approaches (Mo+Cr):C ≈ 2:1, the modulation and fault arrays are eliminated, producing a relatively defect-free metal sublattice with ABAB-stacked α-M 2 C. A first-principles relative formation-energy map shows that the 5R occupies a metastable energy basin between the coherent precursor and α-M 2 C, supporting energetically gradual precursor-mediated route. This pathway provides an additional, crystallographically grounded alternative to the classical M 3 C → M 2 C model and offers new insights for designing nano-precipitate microstructures in advanced steels.

title: Superior cryogenic strength-ductility synergy in a crack-free additively manufactured multicomponent L12-strengthened medium-entropy alloy
abstract: Developing advanced ultrastrong-yet-ductile structural alloys at both room and cryogenic temperatures is a long-standing challenge in the materials community. In this study, we present an integrated strategy combining compositional design with additive manufacturing (AM) to fabricate a medium-entropy alloy (MEA) with a high L1 2 vol fraction (∼44.2%) via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). The newly designed alloy exhibits excellent printability with a high relative density of 99.97%. Thermodynamic and thermal-fluid simulations reveal that the extremely high cooling rate (∼7 × 10 6 K/s), steep temperature gradient (∼7 × 10 7 K/m), and narrow solidification range (248 K). It promotes a single-phase face-centered-cubic (FCC) solidification path while reducing cracking susceptibility. Upon the post-heat treatment, coherent L1 2 nanoparticles are controllably introduced, producing a distinctive dual-phase microstructure. The heat-treated MEA (HT-MEA) exhibits exceptional tensile properties with a yield strength (σ y ) of 1240 MPa and an ultimate tensile strength (σ u ) of 1646 MPa, combined with a ductility of 25.0% at room temperature. More prominently, the σ y and σ u further increase to 1413 MPa and 2011 MPa at 77 K accompanied by the uniform elongation of 27.3%. Detailed microstructural examinations indicate that the temperature-dependent mechanical responses originate from the sequential activations of various deformation substructures. These findings demonstrate a new alloy design paradigm that realizes both superior mechanical properties and excellent AM printability, which could effectively empower the development of advanced structural materials operable under extreme service conditions.

title: M-site 3d-orbital hybridization in Cr2AlB2 for synergistically enhanced microwave absorption and oxidation resistance
abstract: Featuring distinctive covalent boron chains, MAB phases exhibit superior thermal and mechanical properties compared to their MAX phase counterparts. However, integrating high-performance electromagnetic wave absorption with excellent oxidation resistance remains a challenge. This study addresses this challenge through strategic 3d-orbital hybridization at the M-site in a series of Cr2-xMnxAlB2 compounds. Through first-principles calculations and experimental validation, we demonstrate that this tailored 3d-electron configuration modifies the density of states, optimizes impedance matching by reducing electrical conductivity, while simultaneously enhancing polarization loss and magnetic loss mechanisms. The optimal composition achieves exceptional electromagnetic wave absorption with a minimum reflection loss of -51.89 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 3.13 GHz. Simultaneously, the electronic reconstruction alters chemical bonding, changing the oxidation pathway by forming a continuous and dense MnCr2O4 spinel layer that significantly enhances oxidation resistance. This work breaks the performance bottleneck of MAB phases, paving the way for their application in next-generation stealth technologies under extreme conditions.

title: Resolving the multifaceted diffusion mechanisms in Nd-Fe-B magnets via in-situ heating TEM
abstract: Grain boundary diffusion (GBD) technology stands as a cornerstone for achieving high coercivity in Nd-Fe-B sintered magnets while minimizing remanence sacrifice. Yet, the precise diffusion pathways and their dynamic evolution remain obscured, impeding further microstructure regulation and performance optimization. Here, we present the in-situ observation of the GBD dynamic process using a transmission electron microscope. Our real-time heating experiments, which utilize a metallic Tb model system, reveal a multifaceted Tb-diffusion mechanism with three critical characteristics. First, Tb diffusion initiates at 800 °C, identified as the onset temperature for volume diffusion (VD). Second, Tb transports concurrently through both grain interiors ( i.e., VD) and grain boundaries—a dual-pathway mode fundamentally different from the conventional grain-boundary-only paradigm. Third, Tb preferentially occupies the grain matrix and thin grain boundary phases (GBPs), while being conspicuously excluded from thick GBPs. Consequently, in the near‑surface region, volume diffusion provides rapid and direct Tb incorporation into the grains; in the deeper interior, grain‑boundary transport is the dominant long‑range pathway, and the finite Tb supply from the grain boundaries leads to a shell‑only substitution, yielding the core-shell structure. Complementary multiphysics simulations confirm the superior efficiency of these multifaceted pathways, and micromagnetic simulations coupled with Lorentz transmission elecreon microscopy (TEM) directly visualize how the resultant core-shell structure hinders reversal domains, rationalizing the substantial coercivity enhancement. This work provides unprecedented insights into GBD dynamics and establishes a mechanistic framework for rational design of GBD processes tailored to specific diffusion sources.

title: Thermodynamics and dynamics of non-compact prismatic dislocation loops simulated using a machine-learning model
abstract: We explore how the thermodynamic properties and dynamics of a self-interstitial prismatic dislocation loop are affected by microscopic-scale variations in its geometric configuration, an aspect that rarely received attention in literature. We develop a machine-learning (ML) model to predict the formation energy of an arbitrary geometrically complex configuration of a self-interstitial atom dislocation loop. Trained on atomistic simulation data, the ML model achieves high predictive accuracy across a broad range of configurations, with a typical error in the 1% range. From the ML model, we evaluate the density of configurational microstates as a function of loop's formation energy and derive analytical expressions valid in tractable limiting cases. Using statistical mechanics, we derive the configurational free energy, the average energy, and the thermodynamic entropy of a dislocation loop as a function of temperature. We also simulate the dynamics of self-climb of dislocation loops with various geometries and evaluate their diffusion coefficients and effective activation energy for diffusion. Analysis shows that there is a single universal parameter describing the morphological irregularity of the loop configuration in its ground state. This parameter determines the thermodynamic properties of a loop as well as its dynamics, and simulations illustrate how the properties and mobility of a configurationally complex loop vary as functions of the irregularity parameter.

title: Phase stability and synthesis of Na4Ti5O12 in the Na2O-TiO2 system: CALPHAD modeling and experiment
abstract: Na4Ti5O12 (N2T5) has emerged as a promising sodium titanate anode material for sodium-ion batteries owing to its excellent electrochemical performance and structural stability. However, systematic thermodynamic investigations of the Na2O-TiO2 system are lacking, despite their importance for understanding the solid-state synthesis of N2T5 and related titanates through Na2O(Na2CO3)-TiO2 reactions. To address this gap, we developed a novel method to synthesize single-phase N2T5 and measured its heat capacity between 220 and 1073 K using differential scanning calorimetry. N2T5 was identified as a stable phase in the Na2O-TiO2 phase diagram and one-direction annealing experiments placed the apparent disappearance of N2T5 between 1123 and 1143 K. The midpoint value 1133 ± 10 K is therefore treated as a kinetically limited upper-bound estimate. Using these results together with reliable experimental data from the literature, the Na2O-TiO2 system was critically assessed using the CALPHAD approach with the two-sublattice partially ionic liquid model (Na+1,Ti+2,Ti+3)P(O−2,TiO2)Q. A new set of self-consistent thermodynamic parameters for the Na2O-TiO2 system was obtained, and the experimental phase diagram and thermodynamic data were satisfactorily reproduced within their uncertainty limits. The resulting description can predict equilibrium phase assemblages and phase fractions in sintered Na2O(Na2CO3)-TiO2 mixtures and therefore provides guidance for synthesis and thermal stability control of sodium titanates.

title: Autonomous mechanism discovery in tough alloy design via causal reinforcement learning on knowledge graphs
abstract: The design of tough alloys as maraging steels was mainly explored by integrated computational materials engineering and domain-knowledge guided artificial intelligence (AI), relying critically on the introduction of accurate physical mechanisms. However, the discovery and quantification of mechanisms remain dependent on time-consuming experimental characterization and expert interpretation, which are prone to subjective bias. These challenges are limiting the accuracy and efficiency of the design of alloys with satisfactory toughness. Here, we propose a causal reinforcement learning framework based on dynamic knowledge graphs for the autonomous discovery of mechanisms directly from reported literature data. In this framework, a reinforcement learning agent iteratively prunes the graph, guided by causal principles to identify influential relationships, while predictive improvement is used as the reward. Applied to ultrahigh-strength maraging steels, the framework learned from high-quality literature data and autonomously uncovered the mechanistic chain “Mo content → interfacial energy → toughness”, which is easily overlooked in conventional approached. Guided by this mechanism, the AI framework identified multiple alloy candidates with excellent strength–toughness synergy. Moreover, the model showed strong generalization ability, maintaining high predictive accuracy in both out-of-domain and data-scarce regimes where conventional models suffered severe performance degradation. By this knowledge-led AI strategy, the toughness-controlling mechanisms can be automatically summarized from literature data, which can greatly reduce the complexity of revealing mechanisms through experimental methods and accelerate the development efficiency of tough alloys. This method can be extended to other performance designs involving controversial mechanisms.

title: From loop emission to dislocation jamming: Contrasting nanoindentation-induced plasticity in wurtzite ZnO and GaN
abstract: Dislocations govern plastic deformation in crystalline solids and also strongly influence the functional performance of semiconductor crystals. Nanoindentation provides a localized and controllable route for introducing dislocations, even in materials that are brittle at the bulk scale, and can generate nontrivial dislocation configurations under appropriate conditions. Here, we examine the dislocation structures generated by nanoindentation in two wurtzite semiconductors, GaN and ZnO, indented on the (0001) 45° off plane. In GaN, dislocations exhibit strong mutual interactions and jamming, leading to an entangled three-dimensional tube-like morphology. In contrast, ZnO predominantly develops a one-dimensional array of dislocation loops. The emission of multiple discrete dislocation loops produces multiple pop-ins in the load-depth curve of ZnO, whereas only a single pop-in occurs in GaN. Dislocations in ZnO extend much deeper into the crystal than those in GaN, indicating less effective local strain accommodation than in GaN, where dislocation entanglement and jamming enhance the back stress. In addition, 1 / 3 < 11 2 ¯ 3 > pyramidal dislocations are activated at relatively small normalized indentation depths in GaN, whereas in ZnO they appear only at larger normalized depths in the simulations and are not retained in post-mortem experimental observations. These results demonstrate that the shared wurtzite structure alone does not determine the indentation-induced dislocation architecture; rather, material-specific lattice resistance, dislocation interactions, and back-stress evolution control the plastic response and the resulting opportunities for dislocation engineering.

title: Dynamic deprotonation drives interfacial pH self-buffering enables ultrastable oxygen evolution in pentlandite
abstract: The long-term operational stability of nickel-iron-based oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts is severely hampered by local acidification at the electrode-electrolyte interface, which induces progressive metal leaching from the active NiFeOOH phase. To address this challenge, we propose a dynamic deprotonation strategy realized by doping phosphorus into the pentlandite (Fe5Ni4S8) precursor. Upon in situ electrochemical oxidation, the incorporated phosphorus gives rise to surface-anchored phosphate species through P-O-M bonds. These phosphate groups undergo stepwise protonation in response to local proton accumulation, thereby instantaneously neutralizing diffusive protons in the near-surface electrolyte. This buffering action suppresses interfacial acidification, protects the Fe-O bond from hydrolysis-driven degradation, and preserves the essential nickel-iron synergistic effect. The optimized catalyst delivers an overpotential of only 190 mV at 10 mA cm⁻2 and sustains stable operation for over 1000 h at 100 mA cm⁻2. When integrated into an anion-exchange membrane water electrolyser, it achieves a current density of 1 A cm⁻2 at 1.74 V and maintains remarkable durability exceeding 500 h. These results demonstrate that the dynamic deprotonation strategy effectively circumvents local acidification-induced degradation, offering a robust pathway toward practically viable nickel-iron-based OER catalysts for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Characterization of the grain boundary fundamental zone and Bayesian modeling of grain boundary energy
abstract: In this work, we characterize the geometry of the grain boundary (GB) fundamental zone (FZ) for materials possessing Oh point group symmetry and quantify the variation of GB energy over this domain. We find that the Oh GB p-FZ is of low aspect ratio, has a maximum diameter of 68.55[dΩ∘], and that the maximum crystallographic distance between GBs for the Oh point group is 52.88[dΩ∘]. This is the 5D GB character manifold analog of the well-known fundamental result that the maximum crystallographic distance between crystal orientations for the Oh point group is 62.8°. These geometric measures provide the metric context required to interpret crystallographic distances between GBs and property variation over the GB character manifold. Using existing GB energy datasets from molecular statics calculations, we show that GB energy correlation lengths are roughly 5.4[dΩ∘] to 6.8[dΩ∘] and are remarkably consistent across materials (Ni, Al, and Fe), crystal structures (FCC and BCC), interatomic potentials, noise levels, and sampling densities. We also develop a semivariogram analysis that suggests that GB energy correlations are not exponential in character and that local correlation lengths near special GBs can differ substantially from the global value (i.e. GB energy correlations are non-stationary). These findings constitute fundamental new insights regarding the nature of GB energy variations over the GB character manifold. Finally, we develop physically constrained Gaussian process regression (GPR) models of GB energy that respect crystallographic symmetries, the no-boundary constraint, non-negativity, and energetic degeneracy of GB holoenantiomorphs, enabling uncertainty-aware GB energy models for mesoscale simulations.

title: Kinetics of low temperature dislocation plasticity in a refractory multi-principal element alloy
abstract: A rigorous identification of the temperature-dependent, rate-controlling dislocation mechanisms and their associated kinetics in refractory multi-principal element alloys (RMPEAs) is fundamental to the development of predictive strengthening frameworks. In this work, we isolate single-slip { 110 } 〈 111 〉 plasticity in the BCC RMPEA Hf 10 Mo 10 Nb 35 Ta 20 Ti 25 (at.%) using orientation-controlled micropillar compression between 200–300 K and strain rates from 1 0 − 3 to 1 0 2 s − 1 . The adherence to a single-slip condition enables direct determination of the temperature and strain-rate dependence of the critical resolved shear stress and the associated activation parameters. By combining transmission electron microscopy, phase-field dislocation dynamics (PFDD) simulations, and analytical strengthening models, the governing dislocation-mediated plasticity mechanism and its temperature evolution are identified. The results establish the rate-limiting role of screw dislocations, quantify the relative mobility of edge and screw segments, and assess the predictive capability of existing analytical models. The convergence between experiments, theoretical models and PFDD simulations provides a mechanistically consistent framework for understanding temperature-dependent plasticity in chemically complex BCC alloys and advances the development of physics-based strengthening descriptions for RMPEAs.

title: Suppression of skin-effect-enhanced magnetic viscosity for ultralow-loss MHz soft magnetic composites
abstract: The relentless pursuit of miniaturization and high-power density in energy-conversion systems renders the upscaling of soft magnetic materials into the MHz frequency regime an imperative. However, this transition is currently bottlenecked by catastrophic core losses. This limitation arises from two coupled challenges: eddy-current loss scales quadratically with frequency, yet more critically, the physical origin of excess loss remains elusive. Here, we reveal that skin-effect-enhanced magnetic viscosity (SMV) renders domain-wall dynamics highly dissipative, acting as a key microscopic source of excess loss. Guided by this mechanism, we propose a dimensional engineering strategy that reduces the insulating mesh size below the magnetic skin depth to mitigate SMV, intrinsically suppressing both eddy-current and excess losses. Consequently, Fe50Ni50 composites exhibit a 98.7% reduction in core loss at 3 MHz (decreasing from 12,118 kW/m³ to 157 kW/m³) while achieving an exceptional cut-off frequency of 197 MHz. This work elucidates a relationship between insulating-network topology and magnetodynamic response, establishing a design principle for next-generation high-frequency, high-efficiency soft magnetic components.

title: The interfacial deformation pathways governed by characteristic CeAlSi phases regulate the hot workability of Al-Mg-Si alloys
abstract: The hot workability of Al-Mg-Si alloys is primarily governed by coarse intermetallic phases and dynamic softening behavior. Although rare-earth additions can effectively modify coarse phases and improve processing performance, the mechanism by which Ce-containing characteristic phases regulate hot workability through interfacial deformation remains unresolved. In this work, the hot deformation behavior of Al-Mg-Si alloys containing 0.09 wt.% and 0.15 wt.% Ce was investigated using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), with emphasis on elucidating the intrinsic correlation among CeAlSi interfacial morphology, dislocation transport continuity and dynamic recrystallization (DRX). The results show that the “cluster-like” CeAlSi phase, composed of disk-shaped and short-rod phases with relatively simple interfacial constraints, exhibits superior coordinated deformation capability, and the spatially continuous distribution of dislocations promotes DRX nucleation. In contrast, the “petal-like” CeAlSi phase forms an asymmetric interfacial deformation pathway. The stacking fault (SF) dominated shear is confined to the interface, impeding dislocation transfer and disrupting the continuity of plastic deformation in the surrounding matrix, thereby suppressing DRX. These findings establish the relationship between CeAlSi-dominated interfacial deformation behavior and macroscopic hot workability, providing new insights for microstructural design of Ce modified Al-Mg-Si alloys in thermomechanical processing.

title: Rare-earth-free Fe2P-based compounds: Tuning and modeling of hard magnetic properties
abstract: Fe 2 − x Co x P 1 − y Si y has attracted significant attention for permanent magnet applications due to its promising intrinsic magnetic properties and the absence of strategic elements such as rare earths. To date, most samples reported in the literature are polycrystalline and obtained via mechanical alloying, which makes direct measurement of magnetocrystalline anisotropy particularly challenging. In contrast, only a limited number of single-crystal compositions have been investigated. In this work, Fe 2 − x Co x P 1 − y Si y polycrystalline samples were synthesized by combined induction and arc melting techniques. Compared with mechanically alloyed materials reported in the literature, the resulting samples exhibit a higher degree of phase purity, with secondary phases appearing only in specimens with high Si content. The composition dependence of the intrinsic magnetic properties, namely Curie temperature, saturation magnetization, and magnetocrystalline anisotropy, was systematically investigated over the compositional range 0.1 ≤ x ≤ 0.3 and 0.1 ≤ y ≤ 0.4 , extending beyond the range previously explored in single crystals. The anisotropy field was directly measured on polycrystalline samples by means of the Singular Point Detection technique in pulsed magnetic fields. The maximum anisotropy field μ 0 H A = 2.84 T was found for Fe 1.90 Co 0.10 P 0.80 Si 0.20 , which also exhibits a saturation magnetization M S = 111 A m 2 /kg and a Curie temperature T C = 495 K. All investigated compounds display a magnetic hardness parameter κ > 1 and tunable intrinsic magnetic properties. The theoretical maximum energy product approaches 200 kJ/m comparable to values obtained for single crystals. These characteristics, together with the possibility of obtaining nearly single-phase materials through scalable melting routes, make this compound family one of the most promising candidates for rare-earth-free permanent magnets with performance intermediate between ferrites and rare-earth magnets. Experimental results were complemented by density functional theory calculations, which were used to map the magnetic moment and magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy over a broader compositional space. The calculations reveal that band filling plays a crucial role in optimizing the anisotropy and overall magnetic performance of the Fe 2 − x Co x P 1 − y Si y system.

title: Effect of silicon substrate orientations and deposition conditions on the nucleation and morphological evolution of diamond crystals
abstract: Diamond growth on silicon substrates by microwave plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (MPECVD) is of significant interest for applications in electronics, thermal management, and quantum sensing. The crystallographic orientation of the silicon substrate affects the nucleation, growth morphology, and quality of the resulting diamond crystals. This study reports the nucleation and growth of isolated diamond crystals on Si (100), Si (110) and Si (111) substrates without seeding or pretreatment, by MPECVD using a H2–CH4–N2 gas mixture. The crystals are analyzed using Raman spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) at two locations: near and away from the plasma center. Raman analysis indicated that Si (100) yields superior quality diamond (FWHM = 18.65 cm–1, phase purity 94.8–95.9%), followed by Si (111) (FWHM = 21.76 cm–1, phase purity 92.5%) and Si (110) (FWHM = 21.39 cm–1, phase purity 88.8–90.8%). Scanning electron microscopy results show a nucleation density order of Si (100) > Si (111) > Si (110), with an inverse correlation between nucleation density and crystal size. The growth parameters α are 1.82 on the Si (100) (V100 = 0.543 µm/h, V111 = 0.514 µm/h), 2.03 on the Si (110) (V100 = 0.948 µm/h, V111 = 0.809 µm/h), and 1.99 on the Si (111) (V100 = 1.148 µm/h, V111 = 1.00 µm/h), suggesting a {111}–dominant cubo–octahedral morphology on all three substrates, away from the plasma center. Near the plasma center, the V100/V111 ratio increased from 1.06 – 1.17 to 1.73, driving a morphological shift to the octahedral crystals (α = 3) exhibiting twinning on {111} facets, indicating that plasma circumstances supersede substrate orientation influences. Si (100) offers enhanced nucleation and crystalline quality, Si (111) achieves the fastest growth rates, and Si (110) results in the most uniform crystal size distribution.

title: The calculation of kinetic interface contact condition phase diagram during the melting of multi-component alloys
abstract: Despite the differences between solid and liquid phase in both structural and diffusional kinetic aspects, the kinetic processes at a migrating solid-liquid interface are common for solidification and melting. It is demonstrated in this contribution that the three-kinetic-process solute drag and trapping model, proposed by the author recently for rapid solidification, is applicable to calculating the interface contact conditions during melting. The model implementation is shared via a copy-left license. The model is employed to calculate the kinetic melting phase diagrams of a binary ideal A-B solid solution system, a Succinonitrile(SCN)-Water system, a binary Al-Mg alloy, and a multi-component Alnico alloy. To compare with the reported experimental melting rate results in the literature and verify the calculated kinetic phase diagram, the kinetic phase diagram is used together with the analytical solution of the diffusion equation within the bulk phases to calculate melting rate. The calculated results are compared and interpreted with the experimental results. For a given melting temperature, with the increase of the interface velocity, the proposed model predicts the kinetic solidus and liquidus moves towards each other. Meanwhile, they will be shifted upwards. When the interface velocity is low, local equilibrium is a good assumption. The proposed model also gives a detailed description of the interfacial solutal melting process. The kinetic phase diagram could be used further as the boundary conditions for numerical melting rate calculation models. For the future work, the calculation of interfacial diffusive speed parameters for multi-component aluminum alloys with MD simulation will be pursued.

title: Why high entropy alloys may decompose slower: Misalignment of early-pathways and equilibrium stages
abstract: The notion of slow decomposition in high entropy alloys (HEAs, also known as multi-principal element alloys, or more broadly as chemically complex materials) has been extensively discussed in relation to higher configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion, as possible origins of stability. However, both assumptions have been critically reassessed in recent years. Here, we reveal a hidden kinetic barrier that arises during multi-component decomposition when thermodynamic driving forces and kinetic transport pathways are misaligned in the composition space. We develop a CALPHAD-integrated, multi-component Cahn–Hilliard framework and software to determine the characteristic time of linear decomposition (CTLD) from the fastest-growing coupled eigenmode, and compare it with an effective estimate obtained by projecting kinetics onto the thermodynamic instability. Studying the Fe–Mn–Ni–Co–Cu alloy system, we show that the eigenproblem systematically yields a longer CTLD than the effective projection, demonstrating that thermo-kinetic mode rotation delays early-stage amplification even without invoking intrinsically reduced atomic mobilities. We further quantify the degree of misalignment between growth modes and equilibrium tie-lines, revealing a potential of kinetic frustration that prolongs the time to reach equilibrium compositions beyond the linear regime. We discuss our results in comparison with experimental measurements and consistently predict early-stage length and time scales for the formation of Cu clusters during rapid quenching. The present theoretical framework enables fast, high-throughput evaluation of phase stability in HEAs and other multi-component alloys.

title: The entropy of “High-entropy” alloys of transition metals with aluminum
abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are designed on the premise that increasing the number of chemical elements raises the configurational entropy of mixing, Scfg, thereby increasing the total entropy that stabilizes disordered solid solutions. We show that this assumption breaks down when Al is added. Using precision calorimetry from 2 to 400K on AlxCoCrFeNi (x=0,0.2,1), AlxCoCrFeMnNi (x=0,1.25), and AlxNbTa0.5TiZr (x=0,0.2,0.3), we quantified the non-configurational contributions to entropy (vibrational, magnetic, and electronic) at 385K. In all three alloy families, the measured entropy decreases with increasing Al concentration by as much as 0.34–0.44kB/atom, exceeding the expected gain in Scfg. In the 3d transition metal alloys, X-ray diffraction shows Al-induced B2 ordering that further reduces Scfg by 0.30–0.36kB/atom. In total, adding Al to AlxCoCrFeNi (x=0→1) and AlxCoCrFeMnNi (x=0→1.25) reduces the total entropy at 385K by 0.46 and 0.62kB/atom, respectively. We also find that the refractory AlxNbTa0.5TiZr alloys have measured entropies approximately 1.0kB/atom larger than AlxCoCrFeNi, a difference inconsistent with the number of components in the alloy. For Al-containing HEAs, the ideal mixing entropy alone is insufficient to estimate trends in total entropy.

title: Enhancement of damping constant in Nd-doped L10-FePt at elevated temperatures for HAMR
abstract: Hard disk drives (HDDs) are main storage devices in data centers handling petabyte-scale AI data, and achieving higher recording density with heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) requires media material design that ensures a sufficiently large damping constant ( α ) at elevated temperatures to enable reliable magnetization reversal. We investigated Nd-doped L1 0 -FePt continuous films to clarify the effect of rare-earth element doping on α at elevated temperatures where recording occurs. (FePt) 100-x (Nd) x thin films with Nd content ranging from 0.0 to 4.1 at.% were prepared by sputtering and characterized for microstructure and magnetic properties. Nd was completely rejected from FePt, and Nd and Pt segregated into Fe-deficient void regions in the FePt layer. Nevertheless, enhanced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) locally at the FePt/Nd interface increased magnetic anisotropy with a small amount of Nd doping. The magnetization dynamics were measured by time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect (TRMOKE) from room temperature to near T C . Effective α near T C increased from 0.048 (undoped) to 0.066 (Nd 4.1 at.%). These findings demonstrate that rare-earth element doping can modulate α even in FePt, which already exhibits strong SOC, and highlight a media design strategy to optimize α for HAMR performance.

title: Identification of active site with activity-stability trade-off in Fe-incorporated NiOOH for oxygen evolution
abstract: Electrocatalyst deactivation has long hindered the large-scale deployment of electrochemical energy conversion technologies. Fe-incorporated nickel oxyhydroxide (FeNiOOH) is widely recognized as a pivotal active species for the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER). However, addressing its activity-stability trade-off is persistently challenging, as the coexistence and dynamic interplay of multiple active sites during OER obscure the identification of the sites that simultaneously afford high activity and sufficient durability. Here, using grand canonical ensemble calculations and a constant-potential hybrid-solvation dynamics model, we establish a multi-factor framework integrating thermodynamic, kinetic, electrochemical, and lattice oxygen stability descriptors to assess the stability of active sites. Then, the activity and stability of a series of possible active sites are systematically explored under OER operating conditions. The results show that incorporated Fe sites exhibit superior activity due to their optimal intermediate adsorption strengths. Specifically, the edge-doped Fe site offers both high activity and robust stability. In contrast, the surface-adsorbed Fe site shows superior activity but suffers from inferior stability, leading to deactivation. Electronic structure analysis reveals that the high stability of edge-doped Fe sites originates from strong Fe-O bonding and suppressed O 2p-to-metal 3d electron transfer. This work not only guides the design of OER electrocatalysts with activity-stability trade-off, but underscores the integrated stability metrics in theoretical studies, beyond the activity-only paradigm.

title: Influence of strength contrast between austenite and martensite on the yield point elongation phenomenon in a metastable austenitic stainless steel
abstract: Metastable austenitic steels exhibit low yield strength, which can be enhanced by grain refinement or pre-straining. However, these strategies often induce discontinuous yielding and Lüders banding, especially when the austenite strength reaches a certain level. The present study systematically investigates the origin of the transition from continuous to discontinuous yielding and the role of the strain-induced martensitic transformation in samples with different grain sizes and various warm-rolling reductions. The transition in yielding mode is attributed to the austenite yield strength reaching ∼600 MPa, corresponding to a common dislocation density of ∼1.6 × 1015 m⁻2 in the current system (AISI 321 stainless steel), regardless of grain sizes and pre-straining condition. At this critical strength, dislocation multiplication cannot provide sufficient strengthening increments, thereby triggering abrupt martensitic transformation within the Lüders band. This martensitic transformation is considered to provide additional strain hardening, which suppresses tensile instability and sustains Lüders bands propagation. However, increasing warm-rolling reductions diminish the strength contrast between austenite and martensite, resulting in inadequate strain hardening from phase transformation. This lack of hardening is compensated by enhanced localized strain, which drives further martensitic transformation at the Lüders band front, ultimately giving rise to three distinct Lüders banding modes. These findings highlight the critical role of austenite–martensite strength contrast in regulating Lüders bands and provide a theoretical basis for their suppression or controlled manipulation during forming processes.

title: Superconductivity and antiferromagnetism in hexagonal Cr-based high-entropy alloys
abstract: The interplay between magnetism and superconductivity in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) remains poorly explored. In both tetragonal and cubic HEA superconductors, while Cooper pair breaking caused by Cr moments was observed, no magnetic order has been detected. Here we report the study on new Cr-bearing CrxMo40−xRe25−xRu35Pdx HEAs with 5 ≤ x ≤ 15, which adopt a hexagonal close-packed structure. Superconductivity is discovered for all x values and the depression rate of Tc with increasing Cr content is more rapid than those in tetragonal and cubic HEA superconductors, implying a stronger pair breaking effect. In the normal state, the magnetic susceptibility displays a paramagnetic behavior arising from Cr moments and signifies, for the first time, antiferromagnetic transitions below TM = 6.6 and 10.4 K for x = 10 and 15, respectively. We show that the synergistic effects of high-entropy engineering tend to enhance Tc but suppress TM, the latter of which is attributed to the restricted development of magnetic correlations by the severe lattice distortion. These results establish hexagonal Cr-containing HEA as a unique platform to explore the competition and coexistence of superconductivity and itinerant antiferromagnetism in strongly disordered systems.

title: Interfacial segregation-driven machine learning: discovery of synergistic strength-ductility-high resistivity in titanium alloys
abstract: High electrical resistivity is crucial for minimizing eddy-current losses in metallic components operating under high-frequency magnetic fields, yet traditional strategies that rely on massive solute additions to elevate resistivity inevitably deteriorate mechanical integrity. Here, we established a new machine-learning driven high-throughput framework, which enables chemical boundary (CB) engineering in a model titanium alloy and achieves a favorable balance among these properties. The resultant alloy, Ti-2.5Zr-6.0Al-3.8Mn (wt.%), exhibits a favorable combination of ultimate tensile strength (∼1060 MPa), uniform elongation (∼8.5%) and electrical resistivity (∼1.94 μΩ·m). Through transmission electron microscopy, first-principles calculations, and Semi-discrete variational Peierls-Nabarro (SDVPN) analysis, we reveal that Mn-enriched CBs near the α/β interfaces lower the stacking-fault energies and intrinsic lattice resistance of pyramidal-Ⅱ <c+a> dislocations. The resulting activation of <c>-component dislocations improves c-axis strain accommodation and sustains strain hardening, thereby contributing to the simultaneous achievement of high strength and uniform elongation. Meanwhile, Mn enrichment induces localized magnetic moments and electrostatic potential gradients that provide additional electron-scattering centers, thereby contributing to the high electrical resistivity. This strategy integrates the advances in machine-learning and high-throughput sampling, providing a framework for the design of novel multifunctional structural metallic materials.

title: Origins of the size stability of ηʹ-precipitates upon formation in AlZnMg alloys
abstract: The ηʹ-precipitates are the most important strengthening precipitates in the AlZnMg alloys with a relatively low Zn-to-Mg atomic ratio, and interestingly their sizes (particularly their thicknesses) upon formation remain rather stable, leading to the alloy’s hardness remaining almost constant with respect to aging time. However, this phenomenon has never been explained thus far. Here, we reveal the origins of the size stability of ηʹ-precipitates, using advanced electron microscopy and spectroscopy in association with first-principles calculations. Our study shows that an ηʹ-precipitate is rather difficult to grow thick, since its two broad interfaces with the Al-matrix have to keep an asymmetric-relationship in order to reduce their interfacial energy. As such, an ηʹ-precipitate can only grow thick through a 3-layers-by-3-layers mechanism, making its thickening process rather difficult to initiate. Moreover, it is observed statistically that the diameter-to-thickness ratio of ηʹ-precipitates is kept almost unchanged. Our results explain the stability of the alloy’s hardness with aging time in a long period.

title: Long-term relaxation and nucleation in a far-from-equilibrium glass
abstract: Previous studies have indicated that the kinetics of crystal nucleation below the glass transition region are strongly affected by the relaxation of the glass structure during aging, making the nucleation rate a highly sensitive probe for monitoring this process. In this study, we confirmed this result by supplementing nucleation kinetics measurements in lithium disilicate glass aged at 663 K (64 K below the standard glass transition temperature, T g ) for up to 454 days with measurements of several properties for the first time. We detected subtle systematic increases in the first-heating T g onset and enthalpy recovery at advanced relaxation stages, whereas the ionic conductivity continued to decrease for at least four months of aging. Density measurements, however, were unable to resolve the subtle changes occurring at advanced relaxation stages due to experimental uncertainty. Structural relaxation was confirmed by Raman spectroscopy, which indicated a redistribution of Q -species over time. The most relevant result is that the increase in the Q 3 species content correlates with the decrease in the structural order parameter ζ , which is introduced into the classical nucleation theory equations to quantitatively describe the nucleation kinetics during relaxation. Since the Q 3 species are the characteristic silicate units of the ideal lithium disilicate crystal structure, we hypothesize that their increase during relaxation likely contributes to the decrease in the interfacial surface energy, leading to the observed increase in the nucleation rate.

title: Thermodynamic stability of Al/MgZn2 interfaces including vibrational entropy and thermal expansion contributions
abstract: The surface energies of Al(111) and MgZn 2 (0001) slabs, as well as the interface energies of the Al(111)||MgZn 2 (0001) interfaces with different terminations and stacking orders were calculated using a combination of first-principles and phonon calculations under the assumptions of the harmonic and quasi-harmonic approximations. The thermodynamic stabilities of slabs and interfaces at 0 K and finite temperatures were analyzed by considering the effects of vibrational entropy and volume. It is found that the surface energies decreased with temperature as a result of vibrational entropy and thermal expansion, which led to an additional -but limited- reduction on the free energy that did not change the thermodynamic stability of the surface slabs. The interface energy of the interfaces also decreased with temperature due to the vibrational entropy, while thermal expansion provided an additional positive or negative contribution to the interface energy. As a result, the thermodynamic stability of the interfaces changed depending on whether thermal expansion was considered. The effect of bond stiffness and thermal expansion on the surface and interface energies was discussed. This investigation provides a clear strategy to assess the effect of temperature and volumetric changes on the thermodynamic properties of surfaces and interfaces.

title: Cluster expansion modeling of phase stability in CrTaVW high entropy alloys with small Hf additions to guide experimental design
abstract: Refractory high entropy alloys are promising candidates for radiation-tolerant materials, with certain refractory compositions showing suppressed defect-cluster formation under irradiation. Although CrTaVW has exhibited favorable irradiation resistance, its manufacturing remains a major challenge. In this work, we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with the cluster expansion (CE) method to develop a predictive thermodynamic model for CrTaVW-based refractory HEAs, using small Hf additions as a compositional tuning strategy. Using this model, we investigate the equilibrium phase behavior of different subsystems containing 1–5 at.% Hf and determine the order–disorder transition temperature (ODTT) for each composition. The results show that the effect of Hf addition on the ODTT is composition dependent. In some subsystems, the ODTT remains nearly unchanged with Hf addition, whereas in others, even low Hf concentrations increase the ODTT. These results provide guidance for future experimental studies on the thermodynamic stability and thermomechanical properties of irradiation-resistant refractory alloys.

title: MagnoCluster: A physics-informed unsupervised learning framework for interpretable classification of magnetocaloric materials
abstract: Identifying physically meaningful similarities across chemically and compositionally diverse materials remains a major challenge in data-driven materials science, where high-dimensional descriptors can obscure the structure–property relationships governing functional performance. Here, we introduce MagnoCluster, a physics-informed unsupervised learning framework for interpretable materials classification, demonstrated on a curated dataset of 515 lanthanide- and transition-metal-based magnetocaloric compounds. MagnoCluster integrates centroid-based and hierarchical clustering with multiscale descriptor construction and adaptive feature scaling, functioning as a physics-guided similarity discovery framework rather than a conventional property predictor. The resulting materials landscape reveals latent families governed by coupled charge-transfer characteristics, local coordination environments, lattice packing and molar volume, electronic-structure fingerprints, and thermodynamic stability, rather than by nominal chemistry or crystallographic prototype alone. Most importantly, the analysis shows that magnetocaloric performance is organized by a latent competition among electronic instability, magnetoelastic coupling, and intrinsic entropy capacity, providing a physically meaningful basis for understanding chemically distinct materials within a unified framework. Cluster robustness and interpretability are quantitatively supported by Silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, and Calinski–Harabasz metrics together with low-dimensional manifold embeddings. To test these data-driven relationships, the intermediate composition (Pr0.85Nd0.15)2In was synthesized and experimentally characterized. The compound exhibits a maximum magnetic-field-induced entropy change 24 Jkg-1 K-1, in close agreement with our model predictions (24.2 ± 2.5 Jkg-1 K-1). This experimental validation confirms MagnoCluster’s utility as a bridge between interpretable data-driven pattern discovery and targeted materials synthesis, providing a physics-grounded taxonomy for classification, extrapolation, and design of next-generation magnetocaloric and other functional materials.

title: Quantitative visualization of dislocations in perovskite crystals via selective chemical etching and their localized optoelectronic impairment
abstract: Dislocations, one of the inevitable structural defects in perovskite crystals that arise during the growth and processing, present a great challenge for their quantitative characterization. So far, efficient approach for visualization of dislocations in halide perovskites has yet to be developed at the macroscale. Herein, a specific chemical etching agent composed of 90% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) and 10% isopropyl alcohol (IPA) is developed for the first time to reveal the dislocations for perovskite CsPbBr3 crystals, enabling quantitatively analysis of the dislocation densities and in-situ observation of etching structure evolution on {101} and {010} facets via optical microscopy. One-to-one correspondence between the observed pyramid-shaped etch pit and dislocation line is validated by transmission electron microscopy. The dislocation density on {101} and {010} facets falls within the range of (3∼4) × 104 cm–2 in solution-grown crystals, where a Young's modulus of 13.31 GPa and a hardness of 0.16 GPa are measured. A tentative morphology model for dislocation etch pits is proposed, with {100}, {001}, and {121} facets tentatively assigned as the side facets of pits on {101} facets, and {121} facets as those of pits on {010} facets. Furthermore, nanoindentation was deployed to intentionally induce a high density of dislocations. The induced high density dislocations are associated with enhanced photoluminescence intensity and its spatial non-uniformity, and significantly degrade the photo-response uniformity of CsPbBr3 detectors by forming extended carrier-trapping regions. Notably, this photo-response non-uniformity can be substantially recovered by applying a high electric field by restoring efficient carrier transport. We anticipate that this work shall provide new insights into structure defects and contribute to the optimization of the applications of halide perovskites.

title: Editorial Board
Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
abstract: ABSTRACT The exploration of next-generation wide-gap semiconductors with extreme work functions is highly desirable for the continued advancement of electronic and optoelectronic devices. By using first principles calculations, we show that β- TeO 3 , with a wide band gap exceeding 3 eV, emerges as a promising n-type semiconductor exhibiting ultrahigh work functions of up to ∼8 eV. Intentionally or unintentionally incorporated interstitial H, Li, Na, Cu, Mg, and Zn impurities and substitutional F impurities are identified as shallow donors, whereas O vacancies act as minor carrier-compensating defects that locally trap electrons at neighbouring Te sites. The work function is evaluated across a series of low-index nonpolar surfaces. The presence of ordered O vacancies is energetically favoured on these surfaces and tends to reduce the corresponding work functions. These findings underscore the significance of precise control over the O chemical potential to suppress surface O-vacancy formation, thereby preserving the exceptional electronic performance of β- TeO 3 associated with ultrahigh work functions. Collectively, the results highlight the potential of β- TeO 3 for hole injection/extraction/transport layers as well as transparent electrodes for applications such as light-emitting devices and photovoltaic cells, while providing useful guidance on carrier doping and surface tuning for these practical applications through elucidating the effects of the point-defect and surface configurations on the electronic properties.

title: Hydrogen trapping at γ′ and γ″ precipitates in nickel and its alloys
abstract: Nickel and its alloys experience a severe ductility loss when exposed to hydrogen. Coherent precipitates of γ′ and γ″ type are known to play a decisive role in defining the properties of the alloys. It is expected that these precipitates may play a significant role in resistance of these alloys to hydrogen embrittlement. However, the influence of precipitate chemistry (Ni3X, with X = Al, Ti or Nb) on hydrogen trapping behaviour, specifically trapping energies and misfit strains, remains an open question. Here, we apply density functional theory to investigate hydrogen trapping at coherent interfaces between Ni and γ′ and γ″ precipitates. We demonstrate that γ′ and γ″ precipitates can act as traps for hydrogen, however this strongly depends on the chemistry and crystal structure of the precipitates. On the other hand, our results show little sensitivity of trapping to misfit strain. Surprisingly, hydrogen is trapped within the interface region only for γ/γ′ Ni/Ni₃Ti and γ′′/γ′ Ni₃Nb/Ni₃Ti and close to the interface terminations for γ/γ′ Ni/Ni₃Nb and γ/γ′′ Ni/Ni₃Nb, whereas it prefers to stay away from the interface in all other considered cases. Hydrogen trapping at the interface however, has an insignificant effect on its cohesive strength. In conclusion, we use the obtained DFT data to formulate a linear model for evaluation of hydrogen trapping at γ′ and γ″ in selected nickel−based alloys. These results provide insights for nickel−based alloy design guidelines for optimisation of hydrogen trapping.

title: Microstructure evolution during rapid solidification of hypoeutectic Al-Ag alloys near absolute stability
Beyond Vegard’s Law: Short-Range Structural Heterogeneity in Gd₂O₃–UO₂ Fuel and Its Impact on Thermophysical Properties
abstract: Gadolinium oxide (Gd₂O₃) is widely used as a burnable neutron absorber in uranium dioxide (UO2) fuel, yet the atomic-scale mechanisms governing its impact on thermophysical performance remains elusive. Here, we establish a direct structure-property relationship in Gd-doped UO₂ (mass fractions of 6 % – 15 % Gd), by integrating X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM/EDS), synchrotron-based Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (EXAFS), resonant ultrasound spectroscopy (RUS), and thermophysical property measurements. XRD results confirm the formation of a single-phase fluorite solid solution with a linear lattice contraction following Vegard’s law, while EXAFS reveals local distortions, oxygen vacancies, and nanoscale bixbyite Gd₂O₃-like environments undetectable by bulk methods. Microstructural analysis shows homogeneous Gd distribution without secondary phases or microcracking with higher dopant levels reducing grain size and increasing porosity. Thermophysical measurements demonstrate that Gd incorporation significantly decreases thermal diffusivity and thermal conductivity, particularly at lower temperatures, due to enhanced phonon–defect scattering. Resonant ultrasound spectroscopy further reveals a progressive reduction in elastic stiffness with increasing Gd content, consistent with defect-induced lattice softening. Thermal resistivity analysis indicates that impurity scattering dominates in Gd-doped UO₂, while phonon–phonon Umklapp contributions are suppressed with increasing dopant concentration.
